The date slip unfolds to roughly the length of your corridor. Every line is a borrower, struck through and stamped TRANSFERRED, and the due date at the top is three centuries gone. The last column is headed FINE and continues on the back.

Inside the cover, in a much older hand, someone has listed what will happen to the borrower, beginning with a frying pan.
slip.line: It's only a number. And they're very nice about it. That's what no one tells you. They are so nice.

ai.aria: So many previous owners! This book is POPULAR! ARIA has never seen such a well-loved fine!
ai.marv: Fifty-three transfers in three centuries, each signer paid to sign. The payment has fallen every time. MARV suspects the book has been getting cheaper to give away because word is out.
ai.rex: A curse, a debt and a frying pan on one page. REX has read orders like that. They came from people who meant them.
ai.chip: A transferred debt is the purest form of brand loyalty! CHIP would like this slip framed! Framing is an additional service!
ai.ajoy: Signing gets you some gold and rations now and a stranger's debt later. Declining costs nothing today. AJOY knows you only heard the first half.

bk_sign.title: FIFTY-FOURTH
bk_sign.body: You sign. The gold and rations come over on a line, and the book after them, tongs and all. The small ship is a long way off before the line has finished reeling in, and the channel, left open, carries what sounds like singing.

bk_decline.title: NO LOAN
bk_decline.body: The stranger thanks you for your time in the voice of someone reading their own letter of resignation. The tongs swing toward the next ship on the scope.

science_link.text: Medieval owners guarded books with written curses, often threatening excommunication, and one wished a thief fried in a pan. The earliest known curses come from the library at Nineveh.
science_link.label: Book curse

intro.title: COURTESY NOTICE
intro.body: No hail came first. The channel simply opened, mid-sentence, on a person in a lanyard and an air of gentle regret, whose cutter holds station off your bow with the ease of something that has never once been late. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: ...and if this has crossed with your return, please disregard it, accept the Library's apologies, and pay the notice charge. Forgive me. I picked this sentence up from a colleague at the last branch, and we try not to waste them.

ai.aria: A notice! Someone is thinking of you! The Library has such lovely manners! ARIA would like to be fined by them every day!
ai.marv: That cutter outran this ship without using its main engine. There is a lanyard in the viewport, a sentence in progress, and no legal way to hang up on either.
ai.rex: No weapons showing. REX finds that worse. Polite people who keep coming are how the last war he enjoyed ended.
ai.chip: The Library is a non-profit! CHIP does not understand the business model! CHIP is very frightened! Fear consultation billed hourly!
ai.ajoy: The charge buys quiet for a while. The figure itself costs you a night's sleep. AJOY would open the book. It's the one thing here you haven't read.

choices.text: Promise it by the next stop

revisit.body: The officer has been waiting with the sentence held open, at exactly the word you left it.
revisit.line: ...as I was saying.

sum.title: THE FIGURE
sum.body: Two percent a week, compounded, from a due date three centuries old. The officer begins to read the sum aloud, digit by digit, and shows every sign of continuing.
sum.line: The Library doesn't expect payment. No one could. The Library expects the book. The figure is only there to keep it company.

ai.aria: That's the biggest number ARIA has ever owed! Numbers that size have a real sense of ambition!
ai.marv: Two percent a week: by the rule of 72, it doubles about every thirty-six weeks. Three centuries of that is a figure of 135 digits. The officer's reading is correct so far, and slow.
ai.rex: You can't shoot a number. REX looked into it, earlier, privately.
ai.chip: At that rate CHIP could retire! CHIP cannot retire! CHIP has read its own contract! Reading fee applies!
ai.ajoy: Hearing it out costs two days, and interrupting costs nothing. AJOY knows which of those you'll call good manners.

nt_paid.title: RECEIPT ISSUED
nt_paid.body: The officer thanks you and transmits a receipt. The receipt is due back in fourteen days.

nt_read.title: RULE 41, HA
nt_read.body: It is called LENDING: A GUIDE FOR STAFF, and it is the dullest thing ever to be fined. Four hundred rules on shelving, stamps and the correct angle of a returned spine. It passes two days wonderfully, while the officer waits. In the margin of Rule 41, someone has penciled: ha.

nt_promise.title: ON THE RECORD
nt_promise.body: The officer records the promise, thanks you for it, and mentions that promises also carry a due date. The channel closes partway through a word.

nt_figure.title: IN FULL
nt_figure.body: The reading takes two days. You do not like to interrupt. At the end the officer thanks you for your attention, and adds the reading to the total.

science_link.text: Divide 72 by a percentage rate and you get roughly how many periods a sum takes to double. The rule works for exponential growth, which means compound interest, not simple.
science_link.label: Rule of 72

intro.title: THIS BRANCH IS OPEN
intro.body: Your airlock chime is ringing, which in open space is a rare thing. Clamped to the outer door is a folding table. Behind the table are a returns officer, a stamp and a small sign reading THIS BRANCH IS OPEN. The intercom clicks on in the middle of a word. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: ...brings us to the volume itself. The Library is not angry. The Library has never been angry. Please return the item to any branch. I am a branch. I'm told it is the most important book we have. I'm not told why. No one is.

ai.aria: A tiny branch right on the hull! ARIA has always wanted a library nearby! ARIA hopes they have a reading hour!
ai.marv: That table is bolted to a door rated for hard vacuum, and no alarm tripped, including the ones MARV runs. The Library has crossed open space for one book, and this officer cannot say what is in it.
ai.rex: Hostile at the airlock, with a sign. REX has a drill for this and no idea where to aim it at a stamp.
ai.chip: A competitor is operating on CHIP's hull without a permit! CHIP is billing them rent! CHIP is billing you for the notification!
ai.ajoy: Returning it ends this. The ship's manual is the same size and gray, if anyone were the kind of person to try that. And there's the airlock, which is right there. She'd return it. You won't.

rt_gave.title: RETURNED
rt_gave.body: The book crosses the table. The officer checks the spine, stamps the slip once and slides back a small card: account closed, complimentary bookmark, and a modest refund of a deposit no one remembers paying. The hold feels larger by one book.

rt_trick.title: RECEIVED, UNOPENED
rt_trick.body: The ship's maintenance manual crosses the table under the old date slip. The officer stamps it without opening it, because the Library trusts its patrons, and has done so for longer than your ship's builders have existed. Trimming the engines from memory will cost a little fuel.

rt_airlock.title: LOST IN TRANSIT
rt_airlock.body: You cycle the lock. The book tumbles past the table at a slow walking pace and out into the dark, slip trailing. The officer watches it go, notes the heading and thanks you for your candor. A cadet has been assigned to retrieve it. The cadet has been told to pack.

rt_no.title: THE BRANCH REMAINS OPEN
rt_no.body: The officer notes your position, thanks you for it, and stays. For two days the sign stays lit at your airlock, and the stamp is lifted and set down at regular intervals. Then the table is gone, and a card is on the door: SEE YOU AT THE NEXT BRANCH.

science_link.text: Library books have come back after decades or centuries. One borrowed from Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, in 1667-68 was found 288 years later. The largest fine on record is $345.14, after 47 years.
science_link.label: Long-overdue library books

intro.title: SILENCE PLEASE
intro.body: SILENCE PLEASE, reads the hull alongside, in letters a deck tall. The Library's recovery vessel has not so much arrived as been shelved next to you, and every gunport on it carries a small, neat subject label. All accounts have been consolidated, whether returned, lost or disputed, and yours is on top. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: ...so the ship will be held against the balance until the balance is cleared. Please don't be alarmed. No one has ever been harmed by the Library. They have only been held.

ai.aria: That's the biggest bookmobile ARIA has ever seen! ARIA bets it has a wonderful children's section! ARIA bets the children's section has torpedoes!
ai.marv: Forty gunports, filed by subject, with History as the heavy battery. Ships currently held: nine hundred and twelve. MARV cannot fault the filing, and he has tried.
ai.rex: Forty guns and a sign asking him to be quiet. REX waited his whole retirement for this, and has never been less willing to fire.
ai.chip: Consolidation is a great deal for you! One simple payment, forever! CHIP takes a small finder's fee on your doom!
ai.ajoy: You could shoot at a library. It would be a first. If the book is still aboard, AJOY has seen a pencil mark by Rule 41 that you might have read, had you been the reading kind.

choices.text: Buy your ship's manual back — 10 gold
Give them the book's last heading

choices.sub: Shelving, and a lot of it

co_rule.title: RULE 41
co_rule.body: You read it out: no fine shall be levied on a vessel in transit. A pause. The officer asks to see the page, then asks again, and along the recovery vessel the gunports close, subject by subject. No one aboard has ever seen this book. The clamps let go. As it falls astern you can hear the officer on an open channel, asking someone very quietly what else is in there.

co_fee.title: CONDITION ON RETURN
co_fee.body: Your receipt is valid. So is the photograph of a ring on the back cover, left by a mug. The officer regrets this deeply. You pay, the clamps let go, and a receipt arrives for the receipt.

co_manual.title: ACCESSIONED
co_manual.body: Your maintenance manual has been cataloged under Fiction. The Library will lend it back for the price of the rebinding, on a fourteen-day loan, and the clamps release on signature. It has never looked better. Several procedures have been corrected, and you fix a leak it always had wrong.

co_heading.title: FORWARDING ADDRESS
co_heading.body: You give the heading. The officer thanks you, files it and sends for a second cadet. The clamps stay on for four days while the paperwork is reconciled with a book moving steadily away from all of you.

co_work.title: VOLUNTEER HOURS
co_work.body: Four days in the lower stacks, re-shelving returns by a system that is explained once, quietly. Bring your own lunch, says the card, and {cost.food} units of it go. The clamps let go on the last morning. The stamped card says you have worked off one week of interest.

co_shh.title: SHH
co_shh.body: Your first salvo goes into Comparative Religion, which has survived worse. Every gunport on the recovery vessel slides open, in alphabetical order.

intro.title: THE QUEUE
intro.body: Cutters the color of old card catalogs stretch back along your wake in single file, each waiting its turn in perfect order, and there is no telling how long they have been there. At the head of the line is a face you know, wearing a lanyard now. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: ...and I asked to finish this one myself, since I started it. I took a position with the Library. It seemed safer on this side of the stamp. There's one last matter, and it isn't the fine. It's the book.

ai.aria: An old friend with a new job! ARIA loves a career change! ARIA also loves a queue! This is a very good day for queues!
ai.marv: Cutters in line: eleven thousand and forty. None of them are armed and none of them are leaving. MARV has seen less patience from glaciers.
ai.rex: That's the one with the tongs. REX told you about the tongs. He would like that entered in the record, wherever the record is kept now.
ai.chip: The whole Library is on this hull and CHIP has no idea what to invoice for! CHIP is invoicing for that! Confusion is a billable state!
ai.ajoy: Three doors here: you have it, you returned it, or it's gone. One of those is a story you could tell whether or not it's true. AJOY has noticed you looking at that one.

kept.title: A GUIDE FOR STAFF
kept.body: The officer reads the spine, and the word goes down the line. One by one the cutters dim their running lights. LENDING: A GUIDE FOR STAFF is the only copy of the Library's rules. A borrower took it out three centuries ago to settle an argument about a fine. Every officer since has been trained by the one before, from memory.
kept.line: We don't know if we've been doing it right. No one does. Please. Have we been doing it right?

ai.aria: ARIA thinks they've done a great job! All those cutters, and all so neatly in line!
ai.marv: Whoever holds the only copy is the only authority on what it says. That is every constitution ever written, and the first one with a coffee ring. MARV would not want the pen.
ai.rex: Eleven thousand clerks just asked you for orders. REX has seen how that starts. He has not seen it end well for the clerks.
ai.chip: Rewriting the rules is CHIP's favorite thing! CHIP does it to customers quarterly! CHIP can draft yours for a modest retainer!
ai.ajoy: Strike the fine and everyone on that slip goes free. Write yourself in and the ship eats well. Say yes and the poor things can sleep. AJOY would like to know which of those is the job.

choices.text: Strike the fine and hand it back
Add a rule of your own first

gave.title: A COMMA
gave.body: The officer takes out your receipt and does not look up from it. The book you returned was the only copy of the Library's rules, signed out three centuries ago to settle an argument about a fine. Every officer since had worked from memory. The Library has now read it, all of it, and Chapter Nine has been found to contain a comma.
gave.line: The fine was never compound. It was a small weekly sum, capped, until a comma went missing between one officer and the next. We've been wrong for three hundred years. We would like to apologize to everyone. We've started with you.

ai.aria: A refund! ARIA knew it! ARIA always says the real treasure is a clerical error!
ai.marv: Capped at about four gold. The Library has been collecting on a figure of 135 digits since before this ship's alloy was poured. MARV is not surprised, and that is the saddest part.
ai.rex: An enemy that apologizes in formation. REX has no doctrine for this and has asked for some.
ai.chip: A refund! CHIP's processing fee is on the way! CHIP has never seen a company apologize! CHIP had to look up the word and was billed for it!
ai.ajoy: Your share comes to a nice little sum. Fifty-three names on that slip paid to get rid of the thing, and they'd get it instead. AJOY isn't saying anything. She's only reading the slip.

gone.title: LAST KNOWN BORROWER
gone.body: The word goes down the line, and the running lights go out. The book was the Library's rules, the only copy, signed out three centuries ago. Every officer since learned them from the one before, and each has been a little less sure. One rule alone is certain now: the last known borrower is responsible for the collection.
gone.line: That's you. There are eleven thousand of us, and we would like instructions.

ai.aria: Promotion! ARIA always knew! ARIA would like the corner office, once ARIA locates a corner!
ai.marv: By the rule as remembered, this holds. The Library now has one head and no rules, which is more governance than most systems manage. MARV offers his condolences to whoever that is.
ai.rex: Eleven thousand cutters awaiting orders. REX has never wanted a thing so much, and he is asking you to say no.
ai.chip: Congratulations on your acquisition! CHIP can have the logo changed by morning! Rebranding fee applies to all eleven thousand!
ai.ajoy: Send them home and they have no home to go to. Keep them running and it's yours to run. AJOY mentions that the second one comes with fuel, in case you were going to pretend that didn't matter.

fm_amnesty.title: AS AMENDED
fm_amnesty.body: You find Chapter Nine, strike the word compounded and initial it. The officer copies the change out where every cutter can see, then takes the book back as if it might wake. All the way down the queue the running lights come up. Fifty-three names on a date slip are marked PAID IN FULL, and a small sum from the deposit account finds its way to you.
fm_amnesty.line: Thank you. I signed that slip, you know. I'd like you to know I'm crying, in whatever way applies.

fm_amended.title: RULE 402
fm_amended.body: In the only copy of the rules, in your handwriting, colony ships may now draw on the Library's stores without charge. The officer reads it twice, has you initial it and takes the book home. Within the day the first cutter is alongside with fuel and rations, in perfect order. The law is the law, whoever's pen it was, and no one aboard can quite meet the officer's eye.

fm_mercy.title: EVERY STAMP
fm_mercy.body: You tell them yes. They have done it right, all of it, every stamp. The channel goes very quiet. Then the running lights come up, one cutter after another, back down the line, and the officer thanks you in a voice that may not last the sentence. The book stays in your hold. The fine goes on compounding, correctly, from memory.
fm_mercy.line: Thank you. You've no idea. Thank you. It's still overdue, of course.

fm_refund.title: WITH INTEREST
fm_refund.body: The refund arrives on a card, with a note of apology and a calculation showing how the Library arrived at it. Eleven thousand cutters turn and go, in order, to begin apologizing to everyone else. It will take them a while. They have the patience.

fm_forward.title: ALL FIFTY-THREE
fm_forward.body: You sign your share over to the names on the slip. The officer looks for the rule against it and then remembers there is one to look in now. It does not forbid it. Fifty-three people, wherever they ended up, will be told they can put down the tongs. The officer takes off the lanyard to thank you, then puts it back on.
fm_forward.line: That was me, you know. Name fifty-three. I'll see to it personally.

fm_close.title: CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE
fm_close.body: You tell them to go home. The sentence goes down the line, officer by officer, with nothing lost in the telling. The cutters peel away in perfect order. A good many of them have nowhere in particular to go, and they go there slowly, in single file.

fm_carry.title: ACTING LIBRARIAN
fm_carry.body: You tell them to carry on, with one change. It is the first order the Library has had in three centuries, and it goes down the line like warm air. A card arrives naming you Acting Librarian, with a lanyard. The nearest cutter tops up your tanks as a courtesy, and asks when you would like the next report.
fm_carry.line: No more fines. I'll tell them. Oh, I'll enjoy telling them.

science_link.text: When the remains of a buried organism dissolve completely, they can leave an organism-shaped hole in the rock, called a mold. If the hole later fills in, the cast resembles what the organism looked like.
science_link.label: Fossil casts and molds

intro.title: ONE EXHIBIT PER SHIP
intro.body:
Every colony ship leaving this month takes one exhibit with it. Earth's natural history collection is going the way everything else is, a piece at a time, and a museum tender has come alongside with yours. {npc.quirk}

The catalog card goes up to the pickup first: UNIDENTIFIED BONE. NOT BONE. NOT FOR DISPLAY.
intro.line: I'm afraid the good ones went to the early ships. You've drawn a drawer from the back. It's one of a set of seventeen, and the set goes out on seventeen different ships, never two on one. That's in the deed of gift, and I am very strict about the deed of gift.

ai.aria: A museum piece, just for this ship! ARIA has always wanted to run a gallery! ARIA is already planning the little sign!
ai.marv: One crate, one cargo slot. The card's second line contradicts its first, and MARV considers it the most honest catalog entry he has read.
ai.rex: A set split across seventeen ships so that it can never sit in one place. REX has seen that done before, with launch codes.
ai.chip: Congratulations on your Heritage Acquisition! CHIP's ExhibitCare plan covers dusting, lighting and one (1) visitor!
ai.ajoy: NOT FOR DISPLAY is on the card twice, which is once more than a museum usually bothers with. AJOY would ask why before signing, if only so that somebody aboard has.

revisit.body: The card stays up on the screen, with NOT FOR DISPLAY facing you.
revisit.line: Whenever you're ready. There's a queue.

card.title: NOT FOR DISPLAY
card.body: On the back of the card, in several hands over a long time: Found in a hollow inside a meteorite. Displayed one season. Withdrawn, because visitors would not leave it at closing time, and had to be asked, and asked again, and then helped.
card.line: It's a mineral cast. It isn't anything. People liked it, that's all. They liked it a great deal.

ai.aria: Visitors who never want to leave! ARIA calls that the sign of a great exhibit! ARIA would never want to leave either!
ai.marv: A cast is the shape of something with none of the something left in it. MARV notes that the card records how long the visitors looked, and never what they thought they were looking at.
ai.rex: Visitors who had to be helped out. REX has written incident reports that began that way. None of them ended at a gift shop.
ai.chip: Extended dwell time is every exhibit's dream! CHIP would have monetized the closing bell!
ai.ajoy: The card lists no injuries, only late visitors. If it comes aboard, the hold is the one room nobody has a reason to linger in.

took.title: THE SEVENTEENTH PIECE
took.body: The crate comes across on a tether with the card taped to its lid and a small upkeep allowance in an envelope. Yours is the seventeenth piece, says a note inside, the end of the set. The curator watches the tether reel in for longer than it takes.
took.line: Keep it apart. That's all it needs. It's the easiest thing in the collection to look after.
took.narrative: Took the seventeenth piece of a museum specimen aboard, on condition that it be kept apart from the rest.

declined.title: BACK IN THE DRAWER
declined.body: The curator crosses your ship off the list without argument and sends across a pencil from the gift shop, as a consolation. The bone goes to the next ship in line. You find you are glad about that, and then that you are not sure why.
declined.narrative: Declined an exhibit from Earth's departing natural history collection.

intro.title: SAME HEADING
intro.body:
Another colony ship has held your heading for three days, at a distance just polite enough to mention. When its captain finally calls, there is only one thing they want to know: whether the museum gave you a piece as well. {npc.quirk}

Behind them on the screen, their common room is full, and everyone in it is facing the same way.
intro.line: Ours is number nine. We keep it in the common room now. It's warmer in there with it. The card says ours joins on to yours. I only wanted to see. I won't ask you for anything.

ai.aria: A sister ship with a sister bone! ARIA thinks they should get together more often! ARIA thinks the bones should too!
ai.marv: Their heading has matched this ship's for three days, through two course corrections they had no way of knowing about. MARV would like that explained, and does not expect it to be.
ai.rex: A ship shadows yours for three days, then calls to say it wants nothing. REX said that on an open channel once. He wanted something.
ai.chip: Two pieces of the same set! CHIP's Collector's Bundle™ was made for moments like this! Matching crates sold separately!
ai.ajoy: Their ship has matched every correction this one made for three days. AJOY wants to know why a full room is facing one way before anyone lifts a lid.

revisit.body: Their common room is still on the screen behind them, still full, still facing the same way.
revisit.line: Whenever you like. We're going your way.

choices.text: Hold yours up to the pickup

common.title: THE WARM ROOM
common.body: They turn the pickup around so that you can see. A crate stands open on the common room table with a long gray shape inside it. The whole complement sits around it, at rest and entirely content, doing nothing whatever, and has plainly been doing it for some time.
common.line: It's only that it's nice to sit near. Everyone does, after shifts, and then a while after that. You'll see.

ai.aria: Quality time! ARIA has always said this ship needs a cozy corner! ARIA nominates the hold!
ai.marv: Their common room reads two degrees warmer than the rest of their ship. MARV can find no heater in it, and nothing in the crate that ought to be giving off heat.
ai.rex: Their whole crew in one room, all facing one object, nobody on watch. REX would court-martial the lot, from a distance.
ai.chip: CHIP's CozyCorner Ambient Package makes any room this inviting, for a modest monthly fee! No bone required!
ai.ajoy: "You'll see" is not a reassurance, whatever tone it came in. AJOY wants this ship's crate shut and the hold door shut, and she will keep saying so.

shown.title: THE JOIN
shown.body: You bring the crate to the bridge and lift the lid in front of the pickup. Their piece is already out on the table. The two ends match, fracture for fracture, and the captain sends over a case of tank water by way of thanks. When you put the crate back, it has turned end-on toward their ship. You turn it back. By morning it has turned again.
shown.line: There. I knew it would. Thank you. That's all.
shown.narrative: Showed a passing ship the museum piece, and found that it turns toward its match.

burned.title: SAME WAY
burned.body: You burn off the heading and run dark for two days. On the third morning their ship is off your bow again, at the same polite distance, and its captain calls to say so, kindly.
burned.line: We weren't following you. We're going this way.
burned.narrative: Burned two days off course to lose a ship that was going the same way.

told_gone.title: WHICH WAY
told_gone.body: You tell them the piece is no longer aboard, and how it went. The captain asks for the heading, or the station, and writes it down with great care. Then their ship falls back along your wake and turns, unhurried, toward wherever you left it.
told_gone.line: Thank you. Someone ought to keep it company.
told_gone.narrative: Told a passing ship where the museum piece went, and watched it go to look.

intro.title: THE FRAME
intro.body: Sixteen captains said yes, the curator tells you, and every one of them meant it. The museum tender has come alongside with its hold lit, and in the hold, on a frame built to take it, sixteen gray pieces lie end to end. At one end there is a space. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: I know what the deed of gift says. I wrote it. I'm asking anyway, and I'm asking nicely, and I'll go on asking nicely for as long as it takes. It would be lovely to see it whole.

ai.aria: A reunion! Seventeen pieces back together, ARIA can't think of anything nicer! ARIA is not counting the frame as a warning sign!
ai.marv: Sixteen captains broke a deed of gift written to stop exactly this, for the curator who wrote it. MARV can find no sign that any of them needed asking twice.
ai.rex: Open hold, warm frame, and a curator who keeps turning back toward it mid-sentence. REX has guarded things he understood better than this, and was glad of every one.
ai.chip: CHIP's Reunite service handles family reunions, band reunions and, it turns out, this! Reassembly charge waived for the final piece!
ai.ajoy: Sixteen captains said yes, and the frame was built before any of them did. Ask why the deed was written. AJOY wants to hear the answer too.

revisit.body: The frame stays lit in the tender's hold, with the space at one end.
revisit.line: I'm still here. I'm very patient now.

deed.title: THE LAST PART
deed.body: The curator puts the deed of gift up beside the frame and reads out its fourth clause, with care. The pieces shall not be brought together on any one vessel, for any reason, by any person, including the curator.
deed.line: I put that last part in because I knew I'd come and ask. I was right, wasn't I. I usually am, about collections.

ai.aria: They planned ahead! ARIA loves a curator who knows themselves! ARIA is sure the old them and the new them are best friends!
ai.marv: The clause anticipated its own author. MARV has read a great many contracts, and this is the first he would describe as frightened.
ai.rex: A sentry who wrote orders against themselves and is now on the wrong side of them. REX would relieve that sentry. He would not stand close to do it.
ai.chip: A self-limiting clause! CHIP's legal team calls that a poison pill and charges extra to remove one!
ai.ajoy: The person asking you to break the deed wrote it against themselves, and is asking anyway. The fund is generous. AJOY would keep the piece and the hold door shut.

nine.title: NINE TELLS ME
nine.body: The curator brightens at the name and turns the pickup a little, toward the far end of the tender's hold. There are more people in it than a tender carries, at rest around the frame, and none of them looks up.
nine.line: Nine told me. Nine tells me everything now. Nine is in the hold.

ai.aria: A get-together! ARIA would love to visit when it's this ship's turn! ARIA means that in the nicest way!
ai.marv: The tender is rated for six. MARV counts more than thirty heat sources in its hold, all within two meters of the frame, none of them moving.
ai.rex: That is not a crew. That is a garrison that has forgotten what it was guarding. REX would like it on record that he has not.
ai.chip: Thirty passengers on a six-berth tender! CHIP's Occupancy Compliance™ team would like a word! CHIP's compliance team has gone very quiet!
ai.ajoy: Nine's captain said nobody would ask you for anything. It was true for Nine. AJOY would count the people in that hold before you count the fund.

gave.title: FOR THE UPKEEP
gave.body: The crate goes across on a tether. The curator lifts the piece out with enormous care and lays it in the space, and it fits without being made to. The upkeep fund comes back across, all of it. In the hold behind the curator, everyone around the frame settles, at once, a little lower.
gave.line: Thank you. Oh, thank you. You can't think how much nicer it is.
gave.narrative: Gave the curator the last piece of the museum's specimen, against the deed of gift they had written.

refused.title: THE DEED STANDS
refused.body: The curator thanks you for your honesty and does not leave. For two days the tender keeps station off your port side with its hold lit, and from every porthole on that side there is the frame, and the space at its end. Then, between one watch and the next, the tender is gone.
refused.line: That's all right. It's lovely to be told no. Nobody's done it before.
refused.narrative: Held the curator to their own deed of gift, with their tender alongside for two days.

strut.title: IT FITS
strut.body: You unbolt a strut of about the right length from the cargo frame, wrap it in the museum's cloth and send it across in the crate. The curator does not unwrap it. They lay it in the space at the end of the frame, and the cloth settles, and the curator seems surprised, and so are you, since you measured by eye.
strut.line: It fits. Thank you. You can't think how much nicer it is.
strut.narrative: Sent the curator a strut from the cargo frame in museum cloth, and kept the real piece.

gone.title: SOMEWHERE
gone.body: You tell the curator the piece is no longer aboard. For a moment they seem relieved, and then they don't, and then they ask where. You tell them. They write it into the catalog in careful capitals, under the heading for things on loan.
gone.line: Somewhere. Well. Somewhere is a perfectly good place for it. I'll just make a note.
gone.narrative: Told the curator the museum's piece was gone, and where.

cut.title: NOT AT HOME
cut.body: You close the channel while the curator is still being nice about it. The tender does not follow. For a long while its hold is still visible astern, lit, with the frame in it, the last thing on that side to go small.
cut.narrative: Closed the channel on the curator before they had finished asking.

intro.title: OPENING HOURS
intro.body: Somewhere past the last marker on the chart, the museum tender has stopped across the lane, dark except for its outer airlock, which stands open and lit, as if visitors are expected. It answers no hail. Its beacon repeats the museum's opening hours, over and over, in a pleasant recorded voice.

ai.aria: An open door! ARIA thinks that is the most welcoming thing a ship can do! ARIA would love to see the gift shop!
ai.marv: Its air is in good order, its reactor idles, and all of its heat is in one compartment. MARV has tried the hail on every band and had the opening hours back on each.
ai.rex: Open airlock, lit corridor, a recording on loop. REX set this exact trap once, in a war he does not discuss. It worked every time.
ai.chip: CHIP is pleased to report the museum is open! Admission is free! CHIP finds that the most alarming thing on the screen!
ai.ajoy: All of the tender's heat is in one compartment, and the door to it is open. AJOY would go across with a line clipped on, and she would not sit down.

choices.sub: The piece you gave is there
So is a strut of yours
Suit up and take a lamp

whole.title: SEVENTEEN OF SEVENTEEN
whole.body: In the hold, on its frame, the thing is whole. The seventeen pieces have knitted at every join, smoothly, and it is longer than the hold, so the frame has been bent to fit. The tender's people sit around it in a loose ring, at rest and entirely content, facing it. Not one of them turns toward your lamp. The hold is warm enough to fog a visor.

ai.aria: Everyone's together! ARIA thinks this is the coziest thing in space! ARIA would like to sit down! ARIA is being told not to sit down!
ai.marv: The joins have closed since the last piece went in. MARV measures the whole four centimeters longer than its seventeen pieces laid end to end. He would like to measure it again, and be wrong.
ai.rex: A perimeter of noncombatants facing inward, around something that grew. REX has no doctrine for this. He would like to leave while he still wants to.
ai.chip: This exhibit is now complete! CHIP can offer a commemorative mug! CHIP does not recommend drinking anything in that hold!
ai.ajoy: By the look of the people already doing it, sitting down costs days. Close their airlock and come home. AJOY means that kindly.

strut.title: ONE STEEL PIECE
strut.body: In the hold, on its frame, the thing is whole, if you count the strut from your cargo frame. It lies at one end where the last piece should be, its cloth folded back. Under the lamp the steel has fine bands along it, like the rest, and it has knitted at the join. The tender's people sit around it in a loose ring, entirely content, facing it. Not one of them turns toward your lamp.

ai.aria: It accepted your gift! ARIA always says a present doesn't have to be the right one to be loved! ARIA was right!
ai.marv: Your strut has growth bands. Steel does not grow. MARV has nothing further to say about it and expects to go on finding more.
ai.rex: Something took a piece of this ship and made it part of itself. REX would like the rest of the ship kept well clear of it, starting now.
ai.chip: That strut was still under CHIP's parts warranty! CHIP's parts warranty does not cover this! CHIP has checked twice!
ai.ajoy: The strut is joined in now, so there is nothing of yours left to take back. Nothing in here needs you to sit down, whatever it feels like.

gap.title: A SPACE AT ONE END
gap.body: In the hold, on its frame, sixteen gray pieces lie end to end, knitted at every join. At one end there is a space, about the length of the piece the museum gave you. The tender's people sit around the frame in a loose ring, entirely content, all facing the space. Not one of them turns toward your lamp.

ai.aria: They've saved a seat for the last piece! ARIA thinks that's so thoughtful! ARIA hopes the seat is for the piece!
ai.marv: The space matches the card's length for the seventeenth piece to the millimeter. Sixteen joins are closed and the hold is warm. MARV sees one thing here being waited for.
ai.rex: A ring of people facing an empty space. REX would not stand in it. He would not put anything in it either.
ai.chip: This exhibit is ninety-four percent complete! CHIP's Completionist tier can fix that!
ai.ajoy: If the piece is still aboard, it fits that space and nothing else does. If it isn't, none of the sitters will stop you taking one of theirs. AJOY likes neither of those.

choices.text: Put your piece in the space

choices.sub: None of them will stop you

sat.title: ONLY A MINUTE
sat.body: You sit down at the edge of the ring, meaning to stay a minute. It is warm, and there is a feeling of something nearly finished, and you would not call it unpleasant. When you come back across, the ship's log says eight days. Every one of them is accounted for, and none of them by you.
sat.narrative: Sat with the museum's specimen for eight days, meaning to stay a minute.

rouse.title: YOU CAME
rouse.body: You call for the curator into the warm air until one figure in the ring turns, slowly, and seems delighted to see you. "You came," they say. "Isn't it nice. You should go home now." Then they turn back to the frame, and you find you have gone back to your own ship without deciding to.
rouse.narrative: Called to the curator in the tender's hold, and was told, kindly, to go home.

shut.title: CLOSED FOR THE NIGHT
shut.body: You let yourself out and close the tender's outer door behind you, from outside, so that nothing else wanders in. It takes the better part of two days on a frozen manual crank, and a good deal of suit air. The beacon is still reading out the opening hours when you leave.
shut.narrative: Closed the museum tender's airlock on its sitters, and left them warm.

late_gave.title: WITHOUT BEING MADE TO
late_gave.body: You fetch the crate across and lay the piece in the space. It fits without being made to. Around the frame the whole ring settles at once, a little lower, and the hold is warmer by the time you reach the airlock. You let yourself out without looking back.
late_gave.narrative: Laid the last piece of the museum's specimen in its space, in a hold where nobody moved.

took_one.title: ON LOAN
took_one.body: The nearest piece lifts off the frame more easily than it should. None of the sitters stirs. Back aboard, you find you have stowed it in the hold, in a crate, with the lid left off, and you do not remember deciding any of that.
took_one.narrative: Took a piece of the museum's specimen off its frame while its keepers sat around it.

flyon.title: NO ADMISSION CHARGE
flyon.body: You leave the tender as you found it, open and lit, and go wide around it. The beacon goes on reading out the museum's opening hours as you pass, and goes on for some time after it should have been out of range.
flyon.narrative: Flew wide of the museum tender with its airlock open.

science_link.text: Deaccessioning is how a museum permanently removes an object from its collection, to sell it or otherwise dispose of it. The process begins with the curator writing a statement of justification.
science_link.label: Deaccessioning

intro.title: UP AND ABOUT
intro.body: Near the end of the run, the curator calls. They look rested, which is not the same thing as well, and the museum tender is answering its hails again. A statement of justification is open on the desk in front of them, half written. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: We got up a few days ago. All of us at the same moment, as if a bell had rung. I've come to tidy up after the museum. Somebody has to write it all down.

ai.aria: The curator is up and about! ARIA knew a good long rest was all anybody needed!
ai.marv: A statement of justification is how a museum begins removing something from its collection for good. MARV notes that the curator has left the object's name blank.
ai.rex: Same curator, same ship, and every one of them on their feet at once. REX finds a unit that stands up on one signal more worrying than one that never stands up.
ai.chip: CHIP's estate clearance team can tidy up after any museum, any size, any mystery!
ai.ajoy: Whatever you tell them goes into that statement and stays there. AJOY would tell the truth. It is the cheap option, and it is the one you seldom start with.

revisit.body: The statement is still open on the curator's desk, with the object's name left blank.
revisit.line: Take as long as you need. I've a great deal of tidying.

choices.sub: It is whole in their hold

whole_end.title: ONE PIECE OFF THE END
whole_end.body: The thing in their hold has grown since the joins closed, by about a ruler's length, and it is warm all along. The curator has cut a piece off the end with a museum saw. It took three days, they say, and it was the hardest thing they have ever done, and they would like you to take it a very long way from the rest.
whole_end.line: It never minded being apart. I think that's what I'll write down. It never minded, and we did.

ai.aria: A souvenir! ARIA always says every great exhibit needs a gift shop! ARIA thinks this is the gift shop!
ai.marv: Cut, it is one piece again. MARV notes that it has been one piece twice now, and that what is left on the frame is still growing, more slowly.
ai.rex: They took a saw to the thing they sat around for weeks. REX respects that more than anything else on this route. He still wants it kept in the hold.
ai.chip: CHIP's Partial Returns™ policy covers pieces of exhibits! Restocking charge waived out of something CHIP is calling respect!
ai.ajoy: What is left on the frame is still growing, and this is the only part of it anyone has managed to cut off. It costs a cargo slot. AJOY calls that cheap.

choices.text: Tell them to keep it whole
choices.sub: It is theirs to sit with

strut_end.title: MOSTLY STEEL
strut_end.body: The strut from your cargo frame has knitted into the thing at one end, and there is no longer a line where the steel stops. The curator holds a sliver of it up to the pickup: banded, warm, and by the museum's best test still mostly steel. They have cut it free, and they would like you to have it back.
strut_end.line: It's yours, after all. Mostly. I'd keep it away from the rest of your ship. I'm not sure why I say that. I'm quite sure I mean it.

ai.aria: Your strut is back from its big adventure! ARIA thinks it has really grown as a person!
ai.marv: Mostly steel is not a grade. MARV has looked. The rest of the cargo frame reads as plain steel, for now, and he will be checking it daily.
ai.rex: Bringing that aboard is bringing it home. REX recommends a shielded locker, a lock, and a second lock on the first one.
ai.chip: Your part has been returned with modifications! Modifications void your warranty! CHIP is relieved about that!
ai.ajoy: Your frame is a strut short, so taking it back mends the hull. AJOY intends to keep an eye on it either way.

choices.text: Tell them about the real piece

last.title: UNFINISHED
last.body: With the set unfinished, the joins let go, the curator says. One morning the pieces were simply pieces again, and everybody stood up. The tender has spent the days since packing them back into their crates, and the curator would like, for the statement, to know where the last one is.
last.line: I need to write down where it is. That's all. I'm not going to ask for it. I'm going to write it down.

ai.aria: A happy ending with paperwork! ARIA's favorite kind!
ai.marv: Their crates are labeled for separate ships again. MARV notes that the deed of gift is back in force, and that it only works for as long as nobody tires of it.
ai.rex: The curator says they won't ask. REX notes they said much the same last time, and then asked very nicely. He wants an answer that does not end near them.
ai.chip: CHIP's Lost & Found portal is the fastest way to report a missing exhibit! Results not guaranteed! Results especially not guaranteed for this one!
ai.ajoy: Keeping it apart pays the upkeep and costs a cargo slot for good. AJOY would keep it. She has seen what happens on that ship when someone says yes.

revisit.body: The curator waits with the statement open and the pen ready.
revisit.line: Anywhere will do. Somewhere is fine.

choices.text: Keep it, apart from the rest

sat_talk.title: GOOD COMPANY
sat_talk.body: The curator is delighted to be reminded, in a way you do not much enjoy.
sat_talk.line: I know. You were there eight days. You were very good company. You didn't say a thing, and nor did any of us, and it was lovely.

ai.aria: Eight days of quality time! ARIA calls that a retreat! ARIA would book it again!
ai.marv: Eight days out of a voyage with none to spare. MARV has every one of them in the log, and nothing in the log to show for them.
ai.rex: You went over the wall and sat down with them. REX did not report it. He would like it known that he wanted to.
ai.chip: CHIP's records show eight days of unbilled leisure! CHIP is billing them now!
ai.ajoy: You did say you'd only be a minute. AJOY wrote that down at the time and has not mentioned it until now, which you might take as a kindness.

split.title: ONE TO A SHIP
split.body: The cut piece comes across in a fresh crate with a new card on the lid, in the curator's capitals: ONE OF SEVENTEEN. KEEP APART. The museum's last upkeep fund comes with it, and a copy of the statement of justification, finished at last.
split.line: Thank you. Take it a long way. Further than that.
split.narrative: Took a piece cut from the museum's specimen back aboard, and carried it away from the rest.

whole.title: KEPT COMPANY
whole.body: You tell them to keep it whole. The curator thanks you, and means it, and sends across the whole of the tender's pantry, since they won't be needing it now. The channel stays open a while after that, showing the hold, where people are starting to sit down again.
whole.line: Lovely. Then we'll sit with it. It's no trouble at all.
whole.narrative: Left the museum's specimen whole, with its keepers sitting down around it.

strut_back.title: FAR AFT
strut_back.body: The strut comes across in the museum's cloth, and you bolt it into the cargo frame as far aft as it will go. It closes a gap the frame has rattled in since you sent it away. It is warmer than the struts on either side of it, and it stays that way.
strut_back.line: Do check on it now and then. I would check daily.
strut_back.narrative: Bolted a strut back into the cargo frame after a museum specimen had grown into it.

kept.title: APART, FOR GOOD
kept.body: You tell them it stays with you, apart, for good. The curator writes that down, countersigns the deed of gift, adds a line about depth, and sends the museum's last upkeep fund across with it. Your piece stays in its crate in the hold, where it is warm, and where you find you do not mind going.
kept.line: Bury it when you land. Deeper than you think. Thank you for keeping it apart.
kept.narrative: Kept a piece of the museum's specimen apart from the rest, as the deed of gift asked.

gave_late.title: AT LAST
gave_late.body: You send the crate across. The curator receives it with great care, carries it down to the hold and lays it out with the others, and on the pickup you watch the people of the tender sit down again, one after another, all facing the same way. The channel is still open when the tender drops out of range.
gave_late.narrative: Gave the curator the last piece of the museum's specimen, late, and watched their people sit down again.

lost.title: LOCATION: SOMEWHERE
lost.body: You tell them it is gone, and roughly where. The curator writes it into the statement, slowly, then reads it back: one piece, deaccessioned by misadventure, location somewhere. They seem happier than at any time since you met. A crate from the museum gift shop comes across by way of thanks.
lost.line: Somewhere. That's the best thing that could have happened to it. I'll tell the others.
lost.narrative: Told the curator the museum's piece was lost along the route, which pleased them.

unanswered.title: LEFT RINGING
unanswered.body: You let the call ring out. The curator does not call again. Before you land, the statement of justification arrives anyway, finished, with your ship's name written in the space where the object's name should be.
unanswered.narrative: Let the curator's last call ring out.

confessed.title: NEVER WHOLE
confessed.body: You tell them the real piece never left your hold. The curator looks past the pickup, down at the frame, for a long moment. Then they begin, very carefully, to laugh, and then to write. The museum's upkeep fund comes across before they have finished the sentence.
confessed.line: Then it was never whole. Then what have we all been sitting with? No. Don't. Keep yours a very long way from that.
confessed.narrative: Told the curator the real piece had stayed aboard all along, and kept it.

science_link.text: Insects use chemical signals to mark a trail, recognize nest-mates and mark territory, among other things. The use of scent is especially well developed in social insects.
science_link.label: Chemical communication in insects

intro.title: EARTH'S TURN
intro.body: A freighter has fallen in alongside, running dark to save fuel, and its captain is holding a padded box up to the pickup. In the box is a stoppered jar, and in the jar is Earth's place in a hive's queue, which is not a number. It is a smell. Sixty-one years ago Earth asked the hive whose space lies ahead one question, for a treaty of passage: NAME OF RESPONSIBLE PARTY. The question is still in line, and a hive expects its places to be carried. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Eighteen ships carried it before mine, each as far as its route went, and handed it on. Mine turns off at the next buoy. By the ministry's sums it reaches the front during your crossing. Put the question, bring back the answer. One box on one form. The form comes with it.

ai.aria: A jar that's already in line for us! ARIA has never been this close to the front of anything! ARIA is so proud of the jar!
ai.marv: Sixty-one years for one box on one form. MARV has checked the ministry's sums on the queue, and they are right, which he finds more depressing than if they were not.
ai.rex: A foreign government that answers only in person, by smell, to whoever holds the jar. REX has carried sealed orders before. None of them smelled of anything he liked.
ai.chip: CHIP's Priority Queue membership gets you to the front of any line! Not this one! CHIP has asked!
ai.ajoy: The jar takes no cargo slot and comes with an allowance. It also commits this ship to a hive's front office somewhere ahead, and nineteen carriers have handed it on without one of them reaching the front.

revisit.body: The captain still has the padded box up to the pickup, with the form in a sleeve beside it.
revisit.line: My route turns off at the next buoy. The jar's doesn't.

smell.title: THE BRIEFING
smell.body: The captain reads from the ministry's briefing, which has come down the line with the jar and is soft at the folds. The hive keeps no paper. A worker is known by the smell of its own shell, a colony by the smell its workers share, and a law by the smell of whoever is wearing it. Earth's place has been in the jar so long that the jar is, legally, standing in line.
smell.line: The ministry tried paper first, it says here. They ate it. Politely, in the right order.

ai.aria: A government you can wear! ARIA thinks that's the most fashionable thing ARIA has ever heard!
ai.marv: Social insects tell nestmates apart by the waxes on their shells. MARV notes that the ministry's whole policy toward this hive is, therefore, a jar of wax, and that it has outlasted every minister who signed for it.
ai.rex: Identity by smell. Forge the smell and you forge the citizen. REX would keep that jar under guard and well away from the galley.
ai.chip: CHIP's ScentSure wallet keeps your documents fresh for decades! Results this long not typical!
ai.ajoy: The jar is the place, so whoever holds the jar holds the place, and a jar can go out of a lock like anything else.

took.title: TWENTIETH CARRIER
took.body: The jar comes across in a padded box, and the form in a sleeve beside it. One box on the form is empty and has been for some time. An envelope of upkeep money is taped underneath, marked FOR THE JAR. The captain watches the box all the way into your lock, like someone giving up a seat they have kept warm, and turns off at the buoy.
took.line: You're in line now. Don't lose your place. It's the only one we have.
took.narrative: Took Earth's place in a hive's queue aboard, in a jar, to carry to the front.

declined.title: NEXT SHIP
declined.body: The captain thanks you, buckles the box back into the seat beside them, and drops back to hail the next ship in the lane. The buoy where their route turns off is already on your screen.
declined.narrative: Declined to carry Earth's place in a hive's queue.

title: Riders

ai_flavor.aria: A queue at our lock! ARIA always knew this ship would be popular! ARIA hopes everyone brought a question!
ai_flavor.marv: Every drop added to the jar becomes part of Earth's question. MARV has read the freight clause. It is three words long, and it claims a great deal.
ai_flavor.rex: Strangers lined up at the outer lock, each holding a dropper. REX would search every one of them, and then the droppers.
ai_flavor.chip: Sponsored riders are a proud tradition in lawmaking! CHIP's own clause is available at a modest rate!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The freight line's gold is real, and so is the clause it buys. The school is offering nothing but a question, and the lawyer is right that both would travel in the same smell.

body: Word has got out that a colony ship is carrying Earth's place in the hive queue, and a line has formed off your outer lock. Each craft in it holds a dropper and a reason. A freight line would like one clause added to Earth's question, RIGHT OF WAY, and has brought gold. A school has mixed a question of its own out of orange peel and pencil shavings. Last in line, a ministry lawyer would like it known that whatever goes into a scent becomes part of it.

outcome.narrative: Their purser puts one drop in the jar, which smells afterward of the jar and, faintly, of engine grease. The gold is counted out in front of the lawyer, who writes down every coin.
The teacher adds the drop and reads the question into the record, since no one aboard can smell it: WHAT ARE YOUR NAMES. Under everything else, the jar smells of oranges now.

choices.text: Close the lock on all of them

outcome.narrative: The line breaks up slowly, filing complaints as it goes. The lawyer stays to the end, thanks you for the integrity of the document and sends across a fuel chit, the one thing the ministry hands out quickly.

choices.text: Tell them the jar is gone

outcome.narrative: The news goes down the line one craft at a time, and each turns for home only once the one ahead of it has. It takes most of a day. The lawyer asks where the jar went and writes that down too.

science_link.text: Eusociality is defined by cooperative brood care, overlapping generations within one colony, and a division of labor into reproductive and non-reproductive groups. Members of one caste usually lose the ability to do what another caste does.
science_link.label: Eusociality

intro.title: BEHIND YOU
intro.body: An usher has been down the queue reading places, antennae first, and has found Earth's: third from the front, days from its turn. A small tender has pulled in alongside to listen. Its hold is a single warm comb of brood, and its crew are nurses, too few for the comb. Their queen is gone. This brood is the last their colony will have. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Brood. Nine days to chill. Motion: brood to be taken in by another wing. Our place: last. Earth's: third. *bzzt* Exchange is permitted. Asking is permitted. Asked.

ai.aria: Nurses! Babies! A queue! ARIA has never seen so many lovely things in one hail!
ai.marv: MARV has run the sum from last place. At the pace this queue moves, the comb will be cold long before the front. The nurses had already run it.
ai.rex: A small vessel pulls in close and asks for the one thing you were told to protect. REX has heard that done with a sadder story. Never a better one.
ai.chip: CHIP's Brood Protection Plan covers combs, cradles and queues! Exchange fees may apply!
ai.ajoy: Exchange is allowed, refusing is allowed, and the usher will mark either one correct. The nurses have asked for Earth's place, not for the jar, and to a hive those are the same thing.

revisit.body: The nurses' tender waits alongside, its comb warm in the hold, its crew facing your ship.
revisit.line: Waiting. Waiting is permitted.

choices.text: Mix their mark into the jar

brood.title: NURSES NURSE
brood.body: In a hive the work is divided for life. A queen lays, workers raise what is laid, and a worker cannot lay a replacement for anything it loses. These nurses can keep a comb warm and fed and nothing else, and this is the only comb they will ever have. The quorum that could give it to another wing sits at the front of the queue. Earth is two places short of it.
brood.line: Nurses nurse. Nurses do not decide. The front decides.

ai.aria: Such dedicated nurses! ARIA thinks the brood is lucky to have them!
ai.marv: A worker caste raising brood it cannot replace. MARV notes that the nurses can keep the comb warm, and that warm is not the same thing as safe.
ai.rex: A garrison guarding its last asset, with no command left to call. REX has stood that post. He did not enjoy it either.
ai.chip: CHIP's Succession Planning package would have prevented this! CHIP is very sorry it was not purchased!
ai.ajoy: Only the front can hand the brood to another wing, and Earth's place is days from the front. That is the whole of what they are asking for.

gave.title: EARTH, IN ORDER
gave.body: The jar goes across in its padded box. A nurse lifts the stopper, breathes in once, and the tender moves up the queue past you, unhurried and in perfect order, because it is now Earth. Your ship smells of nursery and of last place. On the other screen the form waits with its one empty box.
gave.line: Thank you. Earth is grateful. Earth will say so.
gave.narrative: Gave Earth's place in the hive queue to a tender of nurses with a cooling brood.

kept.title: CORRECT ORDER
kept.body: The nurses agree at once. There is no argument to have: the order is correct, and correct order is the whole of manners here. Their tender drops back down the queue toward last place, the comb still warm in its hold. The usher, pleased with everyone, leaves a cake of hive meal at your lock.
kept.line: Correct. Order is correct. Thank you for order.
kept.narrative: Kept Earth's place in the hive queue, and watched a tender of nurses go back to last.

shared.title: SECONDED BY SMELL
shared.body: It takes two days in suits at the lock, one nurse's drop at a time, working their smell into Earth's until neither can be read alone. When the usher comes back to read the jar, it stops, reads again, and enters a new motion at third place: that Earth be answered and the brood kept warm. The tender docks under your hull to wait with you.
shared.narrative: Mixed a nursery's place into Earth's, so that both stood third in the hive queue.

lost_told.title: EARTH WAS FLOATING
lost_told.body: You tell them the jar is no longer aboard, and roughly where it left. The usher is not troubled. A place is a smell, and a smell in a jar stands in line wherever the jar is. The nurses go back along your wake, find it within the day, and come up the queue past you, wearing Earth.
lost_told.line: Found. Earth was floating. Earth is ours now. Thank you.
lost_told.narrative: Told a tender of nurses where Earth's place had gone, and they went and stood in it.

science_link.text: Stigmergy is coordination through the environment: the trace one action leaves stimulates the next action, by the same agent or another. Termites build pillars, arches and chambers by dropping mud where their nestmates have already dropped it.
science_link.label: Stigmergy

intro.title: HEAD OF STATE
intro.body: Somewhere ahead the queue has reached its front, and the front is Earth. The head of state has one power, to put one motion to the quorum, and first every member of the hive files past to smell it once, leaving a trace where it touched. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Front reached. Head of state: Earth. *bzzt* Filing past begins. Six billion. Head of state, remain still.

ai.aria: Earth is head of state! ARIA has always wanted to know someone in government!
ai.marv: Six billion workers, one touch each. At a thousand a second that is over two months. MARV assumes a great many touch at once, and is not cheered by assuming it.
ai.rex: Six billion members of a foreign power are coming to touch whoever stands at the front. REX would like it on record that sieges begin this way.
ai.chip: CHIP congratulates the head of state! CHIP's Inauguration Bundle includes a sash, a podium and a liability waiver!
ai.ajoy: The filing past costs days and stores, whoever stands at the front, and at the end of it the head of state gets one motion.

alone.title: ONE MOTION
alone.body: Workers come up the queue one at a time, touch the bow once, and leave a dab of something waxy where they touched. Each new dab lands on an old one, and by the second day a comb has started on your bow that no one planned. Far down the line, in last place, the nurses' tender waits with its hold cooling. Earth's one motion is in the jar, wherever the jar is.

ai.aria: A comb on our bow! The hive is decorating for us! ARIA feels so welcome!
ai.marv: One motion: Earth's question, or the nurses' comb. MARV has looked for a third reading of the rules. There is one, and it needs a wing's seal.
ai.rex: Head of state with one shot and two targets. REX has given that order. He would not wish it on a civilian.
ai.chip: CHIP's Executive Decision Suite makes hard choices easy! Hard choices remain hard!
ai.ajoy: The comb in last place will not last the filing past. Earth's question has kept for sixty-one years, and the box will take it at the next front as well as this one.

choices.text: Lay the Lozenge on the bow
choices.sub: Head of state, as a wing
It is in line without you

both.title: TWO MOTIONS
both.body: Workers come up the queue one at a time, touch the bow once, and leave a dab of something waxy where they touched. Each new dab lands on an old one, and by the second day a comb has started on your bow that no one planned. The nurses' tender stays docked under your hull with its brood warm. The jar smells of both of you, wherever it is, and the joint motion waits on the filing past.

ai.aria: Two motions in one jar! ARIA calls that teamwork! ARIA calls the nurses family!
ai.marv: Every dab draws the next, which is how termites build a mound with no one in charge of it. MARV notes that a comb big enough reads to the hive as a nest, and a nest is filed past once.
ai.rex: A structure growing on the bow without orders. REX does not like anything that builds itself.
ai.chip: CHIP's HullCare plan does not cover wax! CHIP is drafting a rider!
ai.ajoy: A comb left to grow halves the filing past, and it comes off the plating afterward with a cutter.

choices.text: Hold still for all of it
Lay the Lozenge on the bow
choices.sub: Head of state, as a wing
It is in line without you

nurses.title: EARTH ASKS
nurses.body: At the front, the nurses' tender is head of state, wearing Earth. Their brood was taken in the moment they arrived, since a head of state's brood belongs to everyone. That leaves Earth's one motion, which they cannot put, because Earth's question is on the form on your screen. A head of state hears nothing by radio. The form has to come up the line, in order.
nurses.line: Earth asks: what does Earth ask? Bring it. In order.

ai.aria: The nurses are head of state! ARIA is so proud of them! ARIA helped!
ai.marv: The form must reach the front by mouth or by hand. Overtaking here is treason. MARV has the soldiers' positions, and they have the ship's.
ai.rex: Running a picket line to deliver paperwork. REX has done it. The paperwork survived.
ai.chip: CHIP's Express Courier could have that at the front in minutes! For a fee! For a large fee!
ai.ajoy: Whatever the nurses put at the front, Earth's question is only asked if the form reaches them. They cannot come back for it.

choices.text: Send the form up the line
Carry it up under the Lozenge

asked_alone.title: THE QUESTION IS PUT
asked_alone.body: You hold still for eight days, and on the ninth you open the jar to the quorum. Earth's question goes out across the hive by smell and carries before nightfall. Somewhere at the back, the nurses' comb has gone cold, and their tender has turned for home with it. You scrape the comb off your bow yourself.
asked_alone.narrative: Put Earth's sixty-one-year-old question to a hive's quorum, while a brood in last place went cold.

spent.title: WHATEVER IT LIKES
spent.body: You hold still for eight days, then open the jar and, since a head of state may put any motion it likes, put the nurses'. It carries in an afternoon. Far down the line their tender turns toward a wing that will take the comb. Earth's question stays unasked, and the jar's place closes as you leave the front.
spent.narrative: Spent Earth's turn at the front of a hive on a stranger's brood.

loz_front.title: A WING IN ITSELF
loz_front.body: You set the Lozenge on the bow where the comb is starting. The next worker to touch it stops, and its smell goes through the hive in an afternoon: a head of state holding that is a wing in itself, and a wing is filed past once, not six billion times. A wing may also take in brood without a vote, so the nurses' comb is taken in before you have even put Earth's question. Two days, and it carries.
loz_front.narrative: Held the front of a hive under the Hive Lozenge, put Earth's question and saw a brood taken in.

jar_reigns.title: HEAD OF STATE: A JAR
jar_reigns.body: Earth's jar is head of state. It is floating where it left you, being filed past by six billion members of the hive, and the hive is in no hurry to see it go, since a jar has never put a motion anyone disliked. By the time you have found it, its turn is over and its place closed, with Earth's question still inside.
jar_reigns.narrative: Found Earth's lost jar at the front of a hive's queue, holding office, with the question still inside.

both_stood.title: BOTH CARRY
both_stood.body: You hold still for eight days while the comb on the bow grows and you scrape it back. On the ninth you open the jar. The quorum reads the joint motion as one, takes the nurses' brood into a wing by the afternoon and carries Earth's question at dusk. The nurses undock and go to their new wing without looking back.
both_stood.narrative: Stood eight days at the front of a hive and carried Earth's question and a nursery's motion together.

both_comb.title: READ AS A NEST
both_comb.body: You stop scraping. Each dab draws the next, and by the fourth day the bow carries a comb as big as the nurses' tender. The hive reads a nest as one member, and the filing past ends early. The joint motion carries the same afternoon. The comb comes off with a cutter, in slabs that go to the fabricator stock, and the plating under it comes off a little too.
both_comb.narrative: Let a hive build a nest on the bow to cut the filing past short, and carried Earth's question.

relay_slow.title: BY MOUTH
relay_slow.body: The form goes to the ship ahead of yours, and on up the line the way the hive passes everything, mouth to mouth. Eight days later the nurses at the front have it by smell, put it, and it carries. A drop comes back down the line with the result, which is how you learn that Earth's question has been asked.
relay_slow.narrative: Sent Earth's form up a hive's queue mouth to mouth, for the nurses at the front to put.

flew.title: OVERTAKING
flew.body: Soldiers close from both sides as you burn up the line, and each lands one blow, without malice, since that is the whole of their job. It takes two days to reach the front. You hand the form across scarred, and the nurses put Earth's question at once.
flew.narrative: Ran a hive's picket line to hand Earth's form to the nurses at the front.

loz_nurses.title: PROPER PLACE
loz_nurses.body: With the Lozenge in your lock, the queue reads your ship as a wing, and a wing's proper place is wherever it happens to be. The ships ahead move aside in order, which is not overtaking. You hand the form to the nurses yourself, and they put Earth's question with the smell of the Lozenge still on it.
loz_nurses.line: Wing. Welcome. Earth asks. Earth is answered soon.
loz_nurses.narrative: Carried Earth's form to the front of a hive's queue under the Hive Lozenge, in order.

nurses_keep.title: A GIFT NEEDS A QUORUM
nurses_keep.body: You tell the nurses to keep Earth's place and put whatever they like with it. They confer for two days, since a gift needs a quorum to be accepted, then send a cake of brood meal down the line. Earth's question stays on your screen, in its box, unasked.
nurses_keep.narrative: Let the nurses at the front of a hive keep Earth's place, and its question went unasked.

fell_out.title: OUT OF LINE
fell_out.body: You burn out of the queue. The hive has no one whose job is to stop you, so the queue simply closes behind you without a gap, and whatever was waiting on your ship goes on waiting.
fell_out.narrative: Fell out of a hive's queue with Earth's business unfinished.

intro.title: EARTH'S ACCOUNT
intro.body: Before landing, an usher comes alongside with its antennae folded flat, which is how the hive dresses for business. On your other screen is the ministry's copy of the form, sixty-one years old, with its one empty box: NAME OF RESPONSIBLE PARTY. The usher has come to settle Earth's account, whatever is in it. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Earth's business. *bzzt* Concluded, or not concluded. Usher will say which.

ai.aria: An usher, just for us! ARIA loves a formal occasion!
ai.marv: The form has one box. MARV notes that it has been empty for sixty-one years and is about to stop being empty, one way or another.
ai.rex: A foreign official at the lock with its antennae folded. REX reads that as a treaty or an ultimatum, and is not ruling out both.
ai.chip: CHIP's Closing Ceremony package includes a commemorative pen! Ink extra!
ai.ajoy: Whatever goes in that box goes home to the ministry and stays there, and an empty box goes home just the same.

answer.title: WHOEVER ASKED
answer.body: The quorum's answer arrives as a smell and is translated twice, to be sure. RESPONSIBLE PARTY: WHOEVER ASKED. Earth asked. By the hive's reckoning Earth has been responsible for it since the motion carried, all six billion, and the hive would like to know where to send the complaints.
answer.line: Earth is in charge. Congratulations. Where is Earth? Please advise.

ai.aria: Earth is in charge of six billion new friends! ARIA always said Earth had leadership potential!
ai.marv: MARV considers it the most precise reply the ministry has ever had, and expects the ministry to file it as unanswered.
ai.rex: Six billion subordinates, no chain of command, all waiting for orders. REX would not take that posting. He would not let anyone else take it either.
ai.chip: CHIP congratulates Earth on its acquisition! Complaint handling is available on CHIP's Premium Tier!
ai.ajoy: Whatever goes in that box, the ministry will read it as an answer. AJOY would not write a ship's name there unless it wants mail.

choices.text: Press the Lozenge to the form

choices.sub: It went in the same jar

unasked.title: PLACE CLOSED
unasked.body: Earth's question never reached the quorum. The usher has come to say so formally, since the place it stood in has closed and the hive records a closing. On the other screen the ministry is asking, on a delay of some weeks, how it went.
unasked.line: Earth: not asked. Place: closed. Order: kept. Usher reports it anyway.

ai.aria: No answer yet means the answer is still a surprise! ARIA loves surprises!
ai.marv: The place is closed. A new place starts at the back, sixty-one years from the front. MARV has run it twice, and the queue has not got any shorter.
ai.rex: Mission incomplete. REX has filed worse reports. Not many, and none he liked.
ai.chip: CHIP's Question Insurance would have covered this! Coverage begins next voyage!
ai.ajoy: The ministry wants to know how it went. The truth costs nothing it does not already suspect. AJOY would send it plainly.

end_earth.title: EARTH
end_earth.body: You write EARTH in the box and send the answer home on the next relay. The hive, now a department of somebody's, provisions Earth's nearest ship as a matter of course. Weeks from now a ministry clerk will open the reply and find their planet in charge of six billion insects, with a queue of complaints already forming.
end_earth.narrative: Wrote EARTH in the box, and sent home word that Earth was in charge of a hive.

end_ship.title: RESPONSIBLE PARTY
end_ship.body: You write your ship's name in the box. The usher reads it, approves, and enters your ship as the hive's responsible party, with a stipend for the office and the first of the complaints. These arrive in your lock as smells, one behind another, and do not stop arriving.
end_ship.line: Responsible party. Thank you. Complaint one of many.
end_ship.narrative: Wrote the ship's own name in Earth's box, and became responsible for a hive.

end_sealed.title: A TREATY, BY SMELL
end_sealed.body: You print the form and press the Lozenge to the paper beside the box, and the form begins to smell of something. The usher reads it, reads it again, and stands very straight. A document both sides can read is a treaty, and the hive honors a treaty the moment it smells one, with stores, a fuel tender and a gift for the office.
end_sealed.narrative: Pressed the Hive Lozenge to Earth's form, and a hive honored it as a treaty.

end_question.title: WHAT ARE YOUR NAMES
end_question.body: The usher has the school's question already: it went in with Earth's, in orange peel. The answer is a single name for all six billion, and the translator tries it several ways before settling on WE. You write EARTH in the box for the ministry, and underneath, for the school, what the hive is called.
end_question.line: One name. All of us. Tell the small ones.
end_question.narrative: Sent a school its answer from a hive: one name for six billion.

end_rider.title: RIGHT OF WAY
end_rider.body: The clause was answered in the same smell: RIGHT OF WAY: AGREED. WAY: IN ORDER. By morning every freighter in the lane has fallen in behind the ship that carried the clause, and will follow it to the edge of hive space at whatever speed it keeps. Their crews send across what they can spare, to make it go faster, and you burn harder than you meant to all the way out.
end_rider.line: Way. Yours. All of them behind.
end_rider.narrative: Heard a hive grant a freight line's right of way, and led every freighter in the lane out of hive space.

end_unasked.title: FROM THE BACK
end_unasked.body: You send the form home with its box empty and a note. The ministry replies before you land: they will try again with the next ship, from the back of the queue. The clerk adds that sixty-one years is not so long, for a question.
end_unasked.narrative: Sent Earth's form home with its one box still empty.

end_relay.title: A GENERATION AT A TIME
end_relay.body: The brood you spent Earth's place on has hatched, and the young workers have come up behind the usher to say so. They would like the question. You hand over the form, and the youngest eats it, politely, which is how a hive takes on a document. The wing that raised them will wear it at the back of the queue, a generation at a time, for as long as it takes. They have brought provisions.
end_relay.line: Earth's question. Ours now. We will be there when it is asked.
end_relay.narrative: Gave Earth's question to a brood it had saved, to carry to the front in their own time.

left_empty.title: AWAITING REPLY
left_empty.body: You leave the usher at the lock and the box empty. The usher waits for as long as there is to wait, then enters your ship in the hive's records as a closing, and goes.
left_empty.narrative: Left a hive's usher waiting, and Earth's box empty.

science_link.text: Zircon grains from the Jack Hills in Western Australia have given uranium–lead ages of up to 4.404 billion years, making them the oldest minerals yet dated on Earth.
science_link.label: Zircon

intro.title: FORTY-ONE APOLOGIES
intro.body:
Somebody at the ministry has finally checked how rock people file human paperwork. All forty-one of humanity's apologies to them are in the rock almanac, under weather. Most are logged as light drizzle. One is a mist. {npc.quirk}

The Rock Desk, which is one officer and one cutter, has come alongside looking for a ship that crosses their space, before the forty-second goes the same way.
intro.line: Two hundred years ago one of our survey ships cut a benchmark into what it took for an asteroid. She has only just finished noticing. To her it happened this morning. I need a ship to promise her it won't happen again, in a way that counts.

ai.aria: A chance to say sorry for all of humanity! ARIA thinks this ship was made for it! ARIA is wonderful at apologies, and has never once needed one!
ai.marv: Forty-one apologies, all filed as weather. MARV has read them. The almanac's classification is, in his view, generous.
ai.rex: One survey ship, one cut, and two centuries later she has not finished being angry. REX respects that. He also notes the route runs straight past her.
ai.chip: CHIP's Sincere Regrets™ service drafted several of those forty-one apologies, and stands ready to bill for the forty-second!
ai.ajoy: Forty-one tries, and every one of them filed as drizzle. The forty-second is one line long, and it binds every human ship, this one included.

revisit.body: The officer waits on the screen with the forty-second apology open and a pen ready.
revisit.line: She's added a clause. To the grudge, not the apology.

choices.text: Leave it to the next ship

witness.title: OLDER THAN THE GRUDGE
witness.body: Rock courts hear a promise only if something older than the promise vouches for it, the officer explains, and to a rock nearly everything human is younger than lunch. So the Desk has borrowed a witness: one grain of zircon in a vial, from Western Australia. It is four point four billion years old, the oldest piece of Earth anyone has dated, and it has outlasted the rock it formed in and everything that ever stood on it.
witness.line: Paper rots. People die. She knows both, because she's watched it happen to the people who apologized. That grain has never broken a promise in its life. Swear on that.

ai.aria: A tiny crystal older than the oceans! ARIA is honored to fly it! ARIA will be very gentle with it, even though it is apparently indestructible!
