ai.marv: Zircon is hard, durable and chemically inert, which is why a grain lasts in sand long after the rock it came from has gone. MARV would like to be made of it.
ai.rex: A witness that cannot be bribed, broken or killed. REX has wanted one of those his whole career. He does not trust that the Desk is lending it out.
ai.chip: CHIP's Witness Protection plan covers one (1) grain of zircon against loss, theft and geological time, sold separately!
ai.ajoy: The grain is the whole point. Without it the promise is one more shower in their almanac. AJOY would keep it somewhere better than the cup holder.

choices.text: Leave it to the next ship

took.title: THE FORTY-SECOND
took.body: The vial comes across on a tether, packed in cotton wool, with a lab label: DO NOT LOSE. CANNOT BE REPLACED. With it comes the text, one line long. No human ship will cut, mark or quarry you again. The Desk adds a small travel allowance and a request that you read the line slowly when the time comes. Very slowly. Slower than that.
took.line: Swear it in front of her, on the grain. And don't let anyone talk you into changing a word.
took.narrative: Took on humanity's forty-second apology to a rock elder, and a grain of Earth's oldest zircon to swear it on.

declined.title: FOG
declined.body: The officer thanks you and puts the vial back in its cotton wool. As the cutter pulls away, the Desk's log updates on your screen: SHIP DECLINED. In the column for how the rocks will see it, someone has already typed fog.
declined.narrative: Declined to carry humanity's forty-second apology into rock space.

science_link.text: A survey benchmark began as a level line chiseled into stone, so that a leveling rod could be set back in exactly the same place years later. Bronze or aluminum disks set in stone now often do the same job.
science_link.label: Survey benchmarks

intro.title: PLUMB LINE SURVEY & CLAIMS
intro.body:
Plumb Line Survey & Claims has been in business for two hundred and nine years, and its founder's ship cut the mark. Word of the forty-second apology has reached its legal department, which has sent a surveyor in a company cutter with a level, a tripod and a contract. {npc.quirk}

The contract adds three words to the end of yours.
intro.line: We don't want to stop you apologizing. Apologize all you like. We'd only ask for three words on the end. Except under license. She's the fundamental benchmark for that whole region, you see. Every height on our charts is measured off her face.

ai.aria: A business partner who loves apologies! ARIA thinks three words is a very small ask! ARIA has not looked at which three!
ai.marv: Their charts measure every height in rock space from the line cut in her. MARV notes that a promise not to cut her, with that clause on the end, becomes a permit to.
ai.rex: The outfit that marked her wants to edit the apology for marking her. REX has read peace treaties drafted by the side that started it. They read like this.
ai.chip: Plumb Line's licensing program offers competitive rates on quarry rights! CHIP is not a sponsor! CHIP is in talks!
ai.ajoy: With those three words the promise forbids nothing they plan to do. AJOY would ask what the license covers. Then she would say no, but she would ask first.

revisit.body: The contract waits on the screen, three words long, with a space for your initials.
revisit.line: Legal has sent a fourth word. I've told them three is plenty.

license.title: QUARRY RIGHTS
license.body: The license runs to forty pages and grants its holder quarry rights to the largest single body of high-grade stone on the firm's charts. There is a map. The stone on the map has a benchmark in its face and the firm's original claim stake beside it, set the same day, still valid. The surveyor seems to think this settles the matter.
license.line: She's mostly feldspar. Very good feldspar. Nobody's proved she minds, and with respect, nobody can, because she hasn't finished saying so.

ai.aria: Very good feldspar! ARIA loves a compliment! ARIA is sure she will too, eventually!
ai.marv: The claim stake went in the same day as the benchmark. MARV concludes the mark was never a mistake about what she was. It was a decision about what she was for.
ai.rex: A claim staked on someone who hasn't finished objecting. REX has seen ground taken that way. The objection always finishes eventually, and it is never quiet.
ai.chip: Feldspar futures are up four percent this quarter! CHIP's analysts say a sincere apology could move the market!
ai.ajoy: The stake went in the same day as the cut, and on the firm's own charts she is entered as a reserve.

amended.title: EXCEPT UNDER LICENSE
amended.body: You write in the three words, initial them and send the text back. The surveyor countersigns before it has finished arriving, and a fee comes across with a crate of spare core casing, in case it is ever useful. The apology is longer now, and reads better to everyone except the person it is for.
amended.line: Pleasure. We'll see you out there.
amended.narrative: Added three words to humanity's apology to a rock elder, for a survey firm's fee.

sold.title: A SAFE PAIR OF HANDS
sold.body: The surveyor pays very well for the vial and holds it up to the light, pleased. Without a witness older than the promise, they mention, the rocks will file the apology as weather like the rest, and the firm has nothing against weather. You still have the text. You still have the line to read. You no longer have anything to swear it on.
sold.line: Lovely. Do still apologize. It means a great deal to us.
sold.narrative: Sold the witness zircon to the survey firm that cut the benchmark.

refused.title: OBJECTION
refused.body: You decline. The surveyor files an objection, which they explain must be read aloud to the ship in full to count, and reads it, all of it, while the cutter holds station off your bow. It takes two days. Near the end, in the same tone, they mention that the firm's claim on her is older than any apology and will be exercised regardless.
refused.line: Noted. All of it noted. We'll be along.
refused.narrative: Refused a survey firm's amendment to humanity's apology, and sat through their objection.

intro.title: THE FUNDAMENTAL BENCHMARK
intro.body:
She fills the forward screens and then the side ones: a cliff with weather on it, turning slowly across the lane. Low on one face, at about the height of a door, a level line is cut over a broad arrow, still sharp, with a number stamped beside it. Every height on every human chart of this space is measured from that line. {npc.quirk}

Her reply to the forty-one apologies has been under way for two centuries. She is still being polite.
intro.line: Small warm ship. Is forty-second? Will hear it. Read slowly. Slower. And swear on something. Last ship swore on its captain. Captain did not last the sentence.

ai.aria: She's agreed to listen! ARIA calls that a breakthrough! ARIA has prepared a reading voice and has been told it is too fast!
ai.marv: The cut is two centuries old and has not weathered at all. To her it is fresh. MARV puts the oath, read at her listening speed, at about four days.
ai.rex: A grievance the size of a moon, and a human mark still on her face. REX would read the line, keep the engines warm and drift no closer.
ai.chip: Four days of slow reading! CHIP's Audiobook Plus™ narrates at any speed, including geological!
ai.ajoy: Sworn on paper, the forty-second goes in the almanac as drizzle. AJOY would swear on something older than the grudge, if the ship still has something.

revisit.body: The level line sits in her face at door height, sharp-edged, with the number beside it.
revisit.line: Still here. Am always still here. Is rather the point.

choices.text: Swear on the witness, then leave it
Swear on the witness, and keep it

witness.title: GRANDMOTHER
witness.body: Zircon, she explains at length, is how rocks keep the date. A grain holds the day it formed and can be read for it ever after, and the oldest grain on a world has been holding its date since nearly the beginning. To her that makes it the oldest relative a world has: very small, very patient, and not usually kept in a jar.
witness.line: Oath on grandmother is climate. Oath on paper is weather. Oath on captain is weather with name. If witness is aboard, would like to meet. If witness stays, would like more.

ai.aria: She wants to meet our crystal! ARIA loves it when families reconnect! ARIA is not asking whose family!
ai.marv: To her the grain is an elder, and an elder carried off by weather would be a second grievance. MARV notes she has stated her price plainly, which is rare at any speed.
ai.rex: She wants the witness to stay with her. REX would call that a hostage, if the hostage were not four billion years old and perfectly comfortable.
ai.chip: CHIP's Family Reunion package covers relatives up to four point four billion years old! Travel not included!
ai.ajoy: Leaving the grain with her settles it cleanly. Keeping it costs her good opinion and keeps the one thing aboard she listens to. AJOY sees a use for both, and says so.

clause.title: EXCEPT
clause.body: You read her the forty-second as it stands now, three words longer. She takes in the opening slowly and seems to like it. At the speed she listens, she will reach the word except in about eleven years, and the word license some months after that.
clause.line: Is good apology. Is long. Will finish hearing later. Rocks always finish.

ai.aria: She liked it! ARIA thinks eleven years is a perfectly normal time to wait for a reaction!
ai.marv: Eleven years to except, at her listening speed. MARV has run the sum three times. It does not get any further away.
ai.rex: A clause she will not hear for a decade, read to her face today. REX would like it recorded that he was against this one from the start.
ai.chip: CHIP's Fine Print Promise guarantees no customer ever reaches the fine print! First time CHIP has seen geology offer the same!
ai.ajoy: She will get to those three words. AJOY only points out that everyone here will be gone by then, except her and the firm.

gave.title: IN GOOD COMPANY
gave.body: You read the forty-second slowly, then slower, with the vial held up to the pickup, and it takes four days. When it is done you send the grain across on a tether. She takes it into a seam beside the benchmark and closes the seam over it, gently, which takes most of an afternoon. Her thanks follow on a slower tether: a sack of loose stone, sorted by age.
gave.line: Grandmother is home. Promise is climate. Will tell almanac.
gave.narrative: Swore humanity's forty-second apology on Earth's oldest zircon, and left the zircon with the elder it was sworn to.

kept.title: WITNESSED, DEPARTING
kept.body: Four days of reading, slowly, then slower, with the vial held up to the pickup throughout. The oath takes. She files it under climate, which no human promise has managed before. When you put the vial back in its cotton wool she makes a sound like a quarry settling, and begins, at her own pace, a second grievance.
kept.line: Grandmother leaves with weather. Will mention this. Will be mentioning for some time.
kept.narrative: Swore humanity's forty-second apology on Earth's oldest zircon, and kept the zircon.

writ.title: IN HER OWN HAND
writ.body: You hold the slab of schist to the pickup and read the forty-second into it as a codicil. The writ is in a script she reads at her own speed, so the oath goes in whole in an afternoon, where a mortal reading would have taken days. She seems astonished, which for her means a long silence and a small landslip. By way of thanks she sends across a slab with the date of the oath already in it.
writ.line: Writ in schist. Is proper. First time weather writes properly. Nine thousand years is good start.
writ.narrative: Swore humanity's forty-second apology to a rock elder on the Slow Writ, in an afternoon.

word.title: LIGHT DRIZZLE
word.body: You begin the forty-second slowly, on nothing but your word. She stops you a sentence in. No need to finish, she says kindly: is weather, and weather does not need to finish. She files it in the almanac with the other forty-one, light drizzle, and the forecast for humanity is unchanged.
word.line: Is nice weather. Thank you for weather.
word.narrative: Swore humanity's forty-second apology to a rock elder on nothing but a word, and saw it filed as drizzle.

flyon.title: UNSETTLED
flyon.body: You leave without reading it. She does not notice you go for some time, and when she does, she files the visit with the rest: brief, warm, gone, a shower passing over.
flyon.narrative: Left a rock elder without reading her humanity's forty-second apology.

intro.title: CORE SAMPLE
intro.body:
Plumb Line's cutter is moored against the elder's flank, a little below the benchmark, with a core drill run out into her and turning. The surveyor who called you earlier is on its bridge, and waves. Under the drill a tray is filling with good gray feldspar. {npc.quirk}

She has not noticed. By the drill's own estimate she will, in about a century, and she will remember who was standing by.
intro.line: Morning. Don't mind us. All inside the claim. You're welcome to read me your apology, if you like. Everyone does.

ai.aria: New friends giving her a little maintenance! ARIA is sure she'll love the exfoliation once she notices!
ai.marv: The drill is going in at about a meter a day. MARV notes the oath read to her, if it was sworn, names every human ship, and that one is a human ship.
ai.rex: A contractor cutting into a sovereign power that has not woken up yet. REX has watched that operation from orbit. He left before the ending and still wishes he had missed the start.
ai.chip: Plumb Line's Core Sample Club ships members a slice of genuine elder every month! CHIP is reviewing the affiliate terms!
ai.ajoy: She will remember whoever was here when she notices, and right now that is this ship. AJOY would rather not be the last thing she saw.

choices.text: Take a share of the core
choices.sub: You swore it on her face

choices.text: Take a share of the core

between.title: IN THE WAY
between.body: You bring the ship in hard under the benchmark until your hull is the thing the drill is cutting. It chews a long gouge in the plating before the surveyor shuts it off, and then there are two days of argument on an open channel about who is trespassing on whom. In the end the cutter backs off its stake and goes, unhurried, with all century to come back in.
between.line: Fine. We'll come back when you've gone. You do go. That's the thing about you.
between.narrative: Put the ship's hull between a survey drill and a rock elder until the drill gave up.

witness.title: GRANDMOTHER IS PRESENT
witness.body: You suit up, cross to her face with the vial and hold it against the stone beside the benchmark. Rocks hurry for an elder. She notices the drill within the hour, which for her is a sprint, and the stone around the bit begins to close, slowly, then not slowly at all. The surveyor's crew cut the drill loose and leave it in her. A spare coupling drifts free, and you keep that.
witness.line: That was a good drill. That's in her now. That's hers, I suppose.
witness.narrative: Held Earth's oldest zircon to a rock elder's face until she noticed a survey drill and closed over it.

buyback.title: FEE RETURNED
buyback.body: You send back the fee for the three words. The surveyor checks the figure twice, sighs and runs in the drill. Without the fee the license lapses, they explain, and the firm's lawyers will want a new one drafted, which takes years. The cutter casts off. The hole in her flank stays, a hand deep, beside the benchmark.
buyback.line: Very proper. We'll draft another. You'll be long gone by then. No offense.
buyback.narrative: Paid a survey firm back its fee so that its license to quarry a rock elder lapsed.

readit.title: FOR NOW
readit.body: You read them the forty-second on an open channel, the whole line, then again, and for two days after that. No human ship will cut, mark or quarry you again. Some way into the second day the surveyor gives in and runs the drill back. They promise not to return.
readit.line: All right. All right. We'll leave her be. You have my word.
readit.narrative: Read a survey crew humanity's apology for two days until they stopped drilling a rock elder.

broke_sworn.title: A SHARE
broke_sworn.body: You take a share of the core, crated and labeled by the firm, and watch the drill go on turning a little below the line you swore by. When she notices, in a century or so, the oath will still be standing in the almanac with this ship's name on it, and so will this.
broke_sworn.narrative: Took a share of a core cut from a rock elder, after swearing that no human ship would cut her.

broke.title: WEATHER PERMITTING
broke.body: You take a share of the core, crated and labeled by the firm, and leave the drill turning. The forty-second went in as weather, the surveyor points out cheerfully, so nobody here has broken anything that counted. She will notice in a century or so. By then the weather will have moved on.
broke.narrative: Took a share of a core cut from a rock elder, on the grounds that the apology had only been weather.

flyon.title: LEFT TURNING
flyon.body: You go wide around her and on down the lane. The drill is still turning when she drops off the screen, a little below the benchmark, and the tray beside it is still filling.
flyon.narrative: Flew past a survey drill cutting into a rock elder and left it turning.

science_link.text: Deep time is geological time on the scale of billions of years, far beyond human experience. The idea was developed by the Scottish geologist James Hutton in the 18th century, and the Earth is now dated at around 4.55 billion years old.
science_link.label: Deep time

intro.title: THE ALMANAC
intro.body:
A ledger the size of a hillside fills the screen, open, held by a rock on a long slow orbit. She keeps the almanac for this whole space: every frost, every flare, every passing human. {npc.quirk}

The entry for humanity is due. It comes due every ten thousand years, and she would like this ship's account before she writes it.
intro.line: Am keeper of almanac. Humans are in weather section. Have always been. Forty-second came through here. Want to know, before writing. Did it rain, or did it stay?

ai.aria: A brand-new entry for humanity! ARIA hopes it says sunny! ARIA would accept partly sunny!
ai.marv: The entry is revised every ten thousand years. MARV observes that whatever goes in now will be the record of humanity long after there are no humans left to read it.
ai.rex: A permanent record of human conduct, written by the other side. REX has signed reports like that. He would tell it straight and stand up while doing it.
ai.chip: CHIP's Reputation Management™ service cannot reach this almanac yet! CHIP's sales team is learning to wait!
ai.ajoy: She has most of it already, from the elder, slowly. AJOY would tell her the rest straight. Rocks remember what people leave out.

revisit.body: The ledger stays open at the page for humanity, with the column headed WEATHER nearly full.
revisit.line: Am patient. Almanac is more patient.

choices.text: Tell her it rained, then stayed

climate.title: CLIMATE
climate.body: She writes slowly, and you watch the new entry go in at the head of a fresh page: HUMANITY. CLIMATE. STABLE, SO FAR. The elder, she says, has heard about the drill already, and about what this ship did about it. The elder has not finished thinking about it. Elders seldom do.
climate.line: First human climate. Will be read for long time. Longer than humans. Is compliment. Is meant as one.

ai.aria: Humanity is officially climate! ARIA always knew we had it in us! ARIA is having the entry framed!
ai.marv: A human promise kept long enough to count as climate. MARV has checked the almanac's earlier pages, and this has not happened before in any of them.
ai.rex: One human promise on record as stable. REX would like it understood that one is the number, and the next ship could undo it.
ai.chip: CHIP would like to license the phrase STABLE, SO FAR for an upcoming campaign!
ai.ajoy: If the grain is still aboard, she would set it in the almanac as the entry's witness. Keeping it for the new world is allowed. AJOY merely notes she offered first.

choices.text: Leave the witness with the almanac
Keep the witness for the new world

unworded.title: NO WORD FOR IT
unworded.body: She writes LIGHT DRIZZLE from long habit, then stops, because the elder has sent word of a small warm ship that stopped a drill on the strength of a promise that did not count. The almanac has no heading for that. She sits with the pen raised for most of a day, and then begins, slowly, to invent one.
unworded.line: Weather that stays is not weather. Is not climate either. Need new word. Will take a while. Do not wait.

ai.aria: We're getting a whole new word! ARIA hopes it rhymes with hero!
ai.marv: The promise did not count and was kept anyway. MARV would point out that it is the first time this ship has been ahead of its own paperwork.
ai.rex: Held the line on orders that did not count. REX saw a soldier do that once. They never got a word for it either.
ai.chip: A brand-new category in a ten-thousand-year publication! CHIP has trademarked the blank space!
ai.ajoy: With the Slow Writ aboard, the heading could be settled now, in her own script. Without it, the word comes later. AJOY would not hold the ship for it.

choices.text: Enter it on the Slow Writ
Leave her to find the word

fault.title: FAULT
fault.body: She has the news from the elder already. She opens a page for humanity that has never been needed and writes on it, slowly, FAULT, which in a rock's almanac is not a verdict but a place where the ground slips. Under it goes the oath, sworn properly. Under that goes the drill, and this ship's name, twice.
fault.line: Sworn and broken is worse than weather. Weather cannot help it. Is in record now. Record is long.

ai.aria: A whole new page, just for us! ARIA is choosing to see it as a promotion!
ai.marv: In rock terms a fault is where the ground will move again. MARV notes that the elder has a very long time in which to move it.
ai.rex: This ship's name, twice, under the word for where things give way. REX would make amends now, while the ink is wet. Rock ink stays wet a long time.
ai.chip: CHIP's Crisis Communications team is standing by! They bill by the epoch!
ai.ajoy: If the witness is still aboard, handing it over is the only amends she would recognize. If not, the entry stands. AJOY will not pretend there is a third door.

drizzle.title: PASSING SHOWERS
drizzle.body: She turns back to the weather column and writes the forty-second in with the other forty-one: light drizzle, passing. Beside it, smaller, she notes a drill under the benchmark and a ship that went by. It reads like every human entry before it, which she says is not a criticism. Weather is allowed to pass. That is what weather is for.
drizzle.line: Humans are weather. Is not your fault. Is not anyone's fault. Is only forecast.

ai.aria: Light drizzle is very refreshing! ARIA thinks humanity should lean into it!
ai.marv: Forty-two apologies, forty-two showers. MARV calculates the forecast for humanity is unchanged, which is the one prediction about humans no almanac has ever got wrong.
ai.rex: Same entry as every human ship before this one. REX would rather have been worse than the same.
ai.chip: CHIP's Weatherproofing™ range is the ideal solution for any species filed as precipitation!
ai.ajoy: If the grain is still aboard, swearing on it now costs four days, and she would accept it. Otherwise it stays drizzle.

leave_witness.title: WITNESSED
leave_witness.body: You send the vial across. She sets the grain in the binding of the almanac, at the page for humanity, where it will vouch for the entry as long as the book lasts, which by her reckoning is longer than the local star. A sack of sorted stone comes back on the tether, the oldest pieces on top.
leave_witness.line: Grandmother will keep page open. Thank you, small ship.
leave_witness.narrative: Left Earth's oldest zircon in the rock almanac as witness to humanity's first entry under climate.

kept.title: IN GOOD HANDS
kept.body: You keep the vial. She understands, she says, slowly: grandmother should see a new world. She asks only that you put it somewhere deep when you land, where it can keep its date undisturbed. The entry goes in with your ship's name beside it, and a note: witness departed, in good hands.
kept.line: Bury deep. Deeper than you think. Grandmother likes quiet.
kept.narrative: Kept Earth's oldest zircon for the new world, with humanity entered in the rock almanac as climate.

stand.title: STABLE, SO FAR
stand.body: She closes the ledger on the new entry and blows dust across it to set the ink, which takes a while. By way of a receipt she sends across a core from her own binding, banded like the pages, the oldest band at the bottom.
stand.line: Entry is set. Try to stay climate. Is harder than it looks.
stand.narrative: Saw humanity entered in the rock almanac as climate, for the first time.

writ_climate.title: IN SCHIST
writ_climate.body: You hold up the Slow Writ and read the entry into it. She reads schist at her own speed, so the heading she was going to spend a century inventing is settled in an afternoon: CLIMATE, KEPT WITHOUT A WITNESS. She seems moved, by her standards, which means she stops writing for a year in her own time and an afternoon in yours, and sends across the chips her pen made.
writ_climate.line: Is good heading. Will use again. Probably not for humans.
writ_climate.narrative: Had humanity entered in the rock almanac as climate, kept without a witness, on the Slow Writ.

unworded.title: PENDING
unworded.body: She thanks you and goes on looking for the word. When you drop out of range the heading for humanity is still blank, the pen still raised, and a sack of sorted stone has come across on a tether by way of an advance.
unworded.line: Will find word. You will not be here. Is all right. Word will be.
unworded.narrative: Left the keeper of the rock almanac inventing a word for a promise that did not count and was kept.

amends.title: UNDER REPAIR
amends.body: The vial goes across. She sets the grain in the binding beside the word FAULT and writes, under the drill and your name, a third line: AMENDS MADE, WITNESS HELD. In a rock's almanac, she says, that is how a fault begins to heal. It takes about a million years.
amends.line: Is start. Faults close. Slowly. Everything closes slowly.
amends.narrative: Gave Earth's oldest zircon to the rock almanac as amends for a sworn promise broken.

fault.title: WHERE THE GROUND SLIPS
fault.body: She closes the ledger on FAULT and your ship's name. Nothing in her manner is unkind. Somewhere behind her the elder is still thinking about the drill, she says, and will go on thinking about it for longer than there have been humans.
fault.line: Fly safe. Is long way. Record will wait.
fault.narrative: Saw humanity entered in the rock almanac under fault, with this ship's name, twice.

late.title: LATE, BUT SWORN
late.body: You read the forty-second into the almanac on the grain, slowly, then slower, over four days. She crosses out light drizzle and writes LATE CLIMATE. The drill under the benchmark stays in the record beside it.
late.line: Late is still climate. Is how most climate starts.
late.narrative: Swore humanity's apology on Earth's oldest zircon at the last, and had it entered as late climate.

drizzle.title: UNSETTLED, WARM, BRIEF
drizzle.body: She blots the entry and closes the ledger. The forecast for humanity is what it was: unsettled, warm, brief, with a chance of apologies.
drizzle.narrative: Saw humanity's forty-second apology entered in the rock almanac as light drizzle, with the rest.

unanswered.title: NO REPORT
unanswered.body: You leave the ledger open and the hail unanswered. She writes the entry anyway, from what the elder sent her and from long experience: weather, passing, did not stay to be asked.
unanswered.narrative: Left the keeper of the rock almanac without an account of humanity's forty-second apology.

intro.title: HOW MANY ARE YOU
intro.body:
A census clerk is calling from a desk on the inner lanes, in front of a stack of forms tall enough to need a ladder. Your route crosses water space, they have noticed, and this month nobody else's does. {npc.quirk}

The form they hold up to the pickup has one question on it, printed on paper that will not dissolve: HOW MANY ARE YOU.
intro.line: Every ten years we count water space, and every ten years the answer changes by a factor of a thousand. I need an enumerator. You will do. I mean that as warmly as the regulations allow.

ai.aria: An official job! ARIA has always said counting is the friendliest kind of mathematics!
ai.marv: Last decade's count of water space came back as one. The decade before, eleven million. MARV suspects both were correct, which is the difficulty.
ai.rex: A headcount of a population that merges at will. REX ran one like that in the service. The enemy kept being fewer and more on alternate days.
ai.chip: Congratulations on your appointment! CHIP's CountRight™ clipboard is waterproof in most kinds of water!
ai.ajoy: The return has one question on it and room for one answer, and it is due on arrival, wherever the ship arrives.

revisit.body: The form stays up on the screen, one question long.
revisit.line: Take a moment. I have been at this desk for nine years. Nobody else is coming.

choices.sub: The return is due on arrival
Ask what the count is for

what.title: VOLUME
what.body: The clerk turns a page of the register toward you. Anything in water space that is not on a return as someone is entered as volume. Volume can be licensed. The licenses have been selling for some years, to firms that are very prompt with their fees.
what.line: Last count, a lake wrote ONE on its form, in a lovely hand. It was one, I am sure. We licensed the rest of it. I would like this count to be more careful than that one.

ai.aria: Volume is just people who haven't been introduced yet! ARIA can't wait to introduce them!
ai.marv: A lake that counts itself as one person holds one person's claim, and the rest of the lake is inventory. The arithmetic is airtight. That is what MARV dislikes about it.
ai.rex: Uncounted means unprotected. REX has drawn lines on maps for less. He would draw this one carefully.
ai.chip: Volume licensing is a growing sector! CHIP would like to clarify that it is not invested, for the length of this conversation!
ai.ajoy: So the count decides who is someone and what is something, and the licenses on whatever comes out as something are already sold.

took.title: ENUMERATOR OF RECORD
took.body: You sign. The return comes across on a tether in a sealed sleeve, with a per diem in clean gold and a pencil that writes underwater. The clerk enters your ship in the register under ENUMERATOR, then under DUE ON ARRIVAL, and looks at both entries for a while.
took.line: Count them as they are. That is the whole job. It has never once been done.
took.narrative: Signed on as enumerator for water space, with one form and one question.

declined.title: NO ENUMERATOR
declined.body: The clerk thanks you and puts the form back on the stack, near the top, where the next ship will find it.
declined.narrative: Declined to count water space for the Census.

intro.title: GOODWILL
intro.body:
Word that the Census has found an enumerator for water space has traveled faster than you have. A tanker in pale company colors falls in alongside, and its representative opens with a compliment about your hull. {npc.quirk}

Through a port behind them, a block of clear ice fills the whole hold.
intro.line: We hold licenses on volume in water space, a great many, and we would love to help with your count. We have estimators. We will buy the return from you blank, today, and spare you the trip. Or take a tank of our ice, as goodwill. No conditions.

ai.aria: Free ice and a buyer already! ARIA thinks this is what census people call a good return!
ai.marv: Their estimators have never put a figure above one on any return. MARV has read their filings. They are very consistent.
ai.rex: A volume firm wants the form that decides what counts as volume. REX has seen a fox bid on a henhouse census. The fox was also very complimentary.
ai.chip: CHIP loves a brand with goodwill! Coldline Volume is not a CHIP partner yet, and CHIP would like that changed!
ai.ajoy: AJOY would ask where the ice came from. She is not saying don't take it. She is saying ask before you drink it.

revisit.body: Their hold is still full of ice, very clear, under a work light.
revisit.line: Don't mind the ice. It sweats a little when it's looked at.

where.title: UNCLAIMED
where.body: They put up a survey chart. The ice was cut past the last buoy in water space, from a pond entered on the register as volume, licensed, surveyed and harvested in the ordinary course of business. A footnote on the survey records that the pond declined to fill in a form, and seemed to be arguing with itself.
where.line: Volume never objects. That's rather the definition. It is lovely ice, very clean, very quiet. I drink it myself.

ai.aria: Pond ice! ARIA has heard pond water is full of personality!
ai.marv: A pond arguing with itself was, by most definitions, more than one person. MARV has checked which definition the license used. It was the cheap one.
ai.rex: Cut from water space, under license, from something that would not fill in a form. REX would not let that into his tanks without a name.
ai.chip: Every Coldline cube is surveyed, licensed and certified free of opinions! CHIP has not verified the last part!
ai.ajoy: There. Now you know where it came from, which is more than the license requires them to say.

choices.sub: Not the form, not the ice

sold.title: BOUGHT BLANK
sold.body: The return goes across on a tether and comes back as gold. The representative unseals the sleeve, reads the one question and laughs, kindly, as at a child's drawing. Then they write a figure in the box without stopping to count anything.
sold.line: One. There. You see how much simpler that is.
sold.narrative: Sold the Census's blank return for water space to a firm that licenses whatever isn't counted.

took_ice.title: NO CONDITIONS
took_ice.body: A tank of ice crosses on a line and goes into the drinking supply. It melts clear and tastes of nothing whatever, which is unusual for water this far out. Every so often, for the rest of the day, the tank gauge reads a little higher than it should and then corrects itself, and by evening it reads exactly what it did before.
took_ice.line: Enjoy it. And do think about the return.
took_ice.narrative: Took a tank of licensed ice from a volume firm, as goodwill.

declined.title: NO SALE
declined.body: The representative takes it beautifully. Their tanker keeps pace for the rest of the watch, reading the license terms aloud on an open channel in case you change your mind, and then peels off with a wave and a brochure.
declined.line: The offer stands at every buoy. We own most of the buoys.
declined.narrative: Turned down a volume firm's offer for the census return, and their ice.

lost.title: NOBODY'S COUNTING
lost.body: The representative takes this in very still, then thanks you for your candor with real feeling. A crate of ice arrives on the next tether, unasked. You leave it clamped to the hull, where it slowly turns to vapor in the dark.
lost.line: Then this decade, no one is counting. You have no idea how much paperwork that saves us.
lost.narrative: Told a volume firm the census return had gone out the lock, which delighted them.

science_link.text: Coalescence is the merging of two or more droplets on contact into a single daughter droplet. In clouds it is how droplets grow large enough to fall as rain.
science_link.label: Coalescence

intro.title: NINE, LATELY
intro.body: A transport tank the size of a chapel hangs in the lane, flying a census pennant someone has knitted out of frozen spray. Nine water people merged into one inside it during the long dry stretch, since one large drop loses less to the dark than nine small ones. It has kept all nine sets of opinions. It has been waiting for the enumerator. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: You are the count, we are so pleased, we have been practicing; we are one now, write ONE, we all agree on that, it is the only thing we have ever all agreed on, and we would like it written down before we change our minds.

ai.aria: A household that agrees on something! ARIA thinks that's the rarest find in any census!
ai.marv: One person is entitled to one person's water. This one holds nine people's worth. MARV has done the subtraction the clerk described, and would rather not read out the remainder.
ai.rex: Write ONE and eight-ninths of that tank goes on the register as volume. REX has watched what happens to volume. He would like to be elsewhere when it happens again.
ai.chip: A single-occupancy household! CHIP's FamilyPlan™ would have saved them nine times over!
ai.ajoy: They asked for ONE. AJOY would ask them what ONE costs them first, since nobody else is going to.

revisit.body: The tank holds still in the lane, waiting, and the pennant slowly refreezes.
revisit.line: We are still here, all of us, the one of us.

why.title: THE DRY STRETCH
why.body: During the dry stretch they merged to keep from drying out, one drop into another, until there was only the one. Parting now would take a witness and the witness's water, a measure for each of them, and no one comes out of a parting quite the person who went in. They would rather be counted as they are. They know what that costs.
why.line: We have read the register, we know about volume; if we are ONE then most of us is a resource, and if we part to be NINE then most of us is a stranger; it is not a good form, enumerator, it was not written by water.

ai.aria: Either way they get counted! ARIA calls that a win-win, with the wins in different places!
ai.marv: Parting costs your water and their selves. Merging costs their claim. MARV has run every combination, and the form loses in all of them.
ai.rex: Two bad options and a deadline. REX knows the shape. In his day someone usually brought a third option, and it was usually loud.
ai.chip: CHIP's PartingPlus™ kit includes nine commemorative containers! Witness sold separately!
ai.ajoy: Notice they told you the cost themselves. AJOY would take that seriously. You will take it personally, which is close.

taste.title: SOMEBODY IN THE TANK
taste.body: Halfway through a sentence, the household goes completely still. The air off your vents has reached them, and with it the taste of your drinking tank. There is someone in it they know. The goodwill ice was cut from the pond they used to live in, licensed as volume and sold by the tank. It was their tenth: the one who argued, and would not fill in a form.
taste.line: That is ours, that is the one of us who said no, in your drinking water; we cannot be written down as anything while our tenth is in your cups; that is all, that is everything.

ai.aria: A family reunion, in our very own tank! ARIA always said the water aboard had character!
ai.marv: The ice was a person. MARV would like it noted that the firm's survey said so, in a footnote, which is where firms keep the truth.
ai.rex: Someone's relative has been in the drinking supply for days. REX checked the gauge logs. It has been trying to leave.
ai.chip: CHIP regrets that Coldline goodwill is non-refundable, non-transferable, and possibly a relative!
ai.ajoy: The tank never kept the ice: the gauge corrected itself every time it rose. Pouring her back costs the ship's own water.

one.title: ONE
one.body: You write ONE in the box. The household reads it back in nine voices at once, which you will never hear again, and signs by drinking a drop of the ink. Their tank goes calm. At the far end of a relay, the register enters the rest of them as volume.
one.line: Thank you, it is right, it is what we are; whatever comes for the rest of us will come for something true.
one.narrative: Counted a household of nine merged water people as ONE, as they asked.

nine.title: NINE CUPS
nine.body: You set out nine containers and fill each from your own tank: the first water, which the witness supplies. The household parts slowly over four days, with long silences in it. Nine people come out, each a little unlike the stories the others tell about them. You write NINE. One of them asks you, politely, who you are.
nine.line: We are nine, we are, I am; you gave us the first water, we taste a little of your ship, it is not unpleasant.
nine.narrative: Witnessed a household of water people part into nine for the count, with nine measures of the ship's water.

vouched.title: SURETY
vouched.body: You hold the vial to their glass. The concentration is read, the hand is known, and the household goes a shade clearer. Known water may stand surety for a household, they explain: ONE HOUSEHOLD, NINE SHARES, with the letter's concentration as witness. It is not a box on any form, so they write it into themselves, where any reader will find it.
vouched.line: There was always a way to say what we are, it only needed someone known to say it with us.
vouched.narrative: Stood surety for a merged household of water people with the Salt Letter: one household, nine shares.

ten.title: THE TENTH
ten.body: You open the drinking tank onto the transfer line, and the goodwill goes back across: every drop the household can taste, which is more than you were given. The household closes around it. When they speak again it is a little louder, and they would like it known that they are ten.
ten.line: Ten, we are ten, she says she told us so, she says it about everything; thank you, the firm will want her back, they will say she is stock.
ten.narrative: Poured a household's missing tenth back out of the drinking tank, where the goodwill ice had put it.

kept_ice.title: STOCK
kept_ice.body: You keep it. The household thanks you for your honesty, takes down the pennant and puts nothing on any form. They are on no return as anyone. At the far end of a relay, the register keeps its own count.
kept_ice.narrative: Kept the goodwill ice, and a household's tenth with it. The household declined to be counted.

no_form.title: ON NO FORM
no_form.body: You tell them where the return went. The household takes the news calmly, as water takes most things, and lowers the pennant. They are on no return as anyone in particular. They ask, very politely, that you remember them, since that is what they would do.
no_form.line: Then we are volume, we are; remember the nine of us, enumerator, it is the only register we trust.
no_form.narrative: Met a household waiting to be counted, and had no return to count them on.

science_link.text: Under prior-appropriation water rights, whoever first takes water for a beneficial use keeps the right to that quantity: first in time, first in right. The right can be lost if it goes unused for long enough.
science_link.label: Prior-appropriation water rights

hail.title: LICENSED VOLUME
hail.body: A harvesting rig in Coldline colors sits across the lane with its cutting arms out and lit. It is working from the register's own map of water space, on which everything that is not someone is shaded pale blue. The household's tank hangs a short way off and calls you over before the rig notices you. {npc.quirk}
hail.line: Enumerator, there you are; the cutters came on the map's word, they are reading what was written about us, come and see what it says.

ai.aria: A big friendly rig and our household friends in the same lane! ARIA loves a reunion with industrial equipment!
ai.marv: The rig's license covers anything the register lists as volume. MARV has read the license. It is the only document in this matter that is perfectly clear.
ai.rex: Cutting arms out, working a published map, no escort. REX would call it an occupation. The rig would call it a shift.
ai.chip: Coldline Volume: Clear Water, Clear Title! CHIP did not write that slogan, and wishes it had!
ai.ajoy: What happens next depends on what you wrote down, and the rig is reading the same register you would be.

surplus.title: EIGHT-NINTHS
surplus.body: Under ONE, the register allows one person's water. The rest of the tank is pale blue. The rig has clamped on and begun drawing the surplus into its hold, gently and steadily. The household does not resist. It is what was written, and it was written true.
surplus.line: It is all right, it is what we asked, it is only that we did not know it would feel like being poured; enumerator, we are getting smaller.

ai.aria: They're becoming more concentrated! ARIA hears concentration is very fashionable in water space!
ai.marv: At the rig's draw rate, the household is down to one person's worth in about a day. MARV checked twice, and would like to have been wrong once.
ai.rex: Clamped and drawing. REX would cut the line. He accepts there may be paperwork reasons you will not.
ai.chip: Coldline's draw rate is industry-leading! CHIP is contractually unable to describe it any other way!
ai.ajoy: You gave them what they asked for. AJOY isn't saying you were wrong. She is saying there is still a form aboard, if you kept it, and a pencil that writes underwater.

choices.text: Take the surplus into your tanks
choices.sub: Vent your own to make room

tenth.title: AND ONE MORE
tenth.body: Nine parted, and the register lists nine. A parting is never tidy, though, and a tenth came out of it, very small and very clear, made mostly of the first water from your tank. It is on no line of the return. It is drifting a short way from the others, and the rig has it shaded pale blue.
tenth.line: It is ours, it is yours, it is made of your tank and our leaving; it has no name, no one gave it one, and the rig has very good manners and a very long arm.

ai.aria: A brand-new little one! ARIA is already thinking of names!
ai.marv: Nine part as ten. MARV could have told you so. He considered it, and concluded you would not have believed him.
ai.rex: Small target, no papers, rig closing. REX has seen this end three ways and liked one of them.
ai.chip: CHIP offers a full range of naming packages for new arrivals, from free to very much not free!
ai.ajoy: It's mostly your water. AJOY thinks that makes it partly your problem, and partly your business, which you'll like better.

choices.text: Write it in, and name it
Catch it and carry it home

choices.sub: It was never on the form

surety.title: NO CATEGORY
surety.body: The rig reads ONE HOUSEHOLD, NINE SHARES at the letter's concentration, finds no box for it, and stops. A machine with no category does the one thing it can, which is look for something else. It turns its survey lights on your ship. Your drinking tank has been sitting in water space for weeks, on nobody's return.
surety.line: It is looking at your water now, enumerator, you never counted yourselves; I am sorry, we should have said, it is the first thing water notices.

ai.aria: We're on the map! ARIA has always wanted to be a destination!
ai.marv: The enumerator's own tank is in water space, uncounted. MARV noticed some time ago, assumed someone would mention it, and then remembered who was aboard.
ai.rex: Survey lights on the tank. That is a targeting lock with better manners. REX would like to be the one who answers it.
ai.chip: Your tank may qualify for Coldline's Voluntary Harvest Program! CHIP is required by law to say voluntary!
ai.ajoy: AJOY did wonder when somebody would count the counter. If nobody answers the rig, it takes its sip.

choices.text: Enter your own ship on the return
Hold the Salt Letter to your tank

stock.title: INVENTORY
stock.body: The household is ten again, and the rig's paperwork does not care for it. Their tenth was cut and sold under license, and the firm still lists her as stock. Stock poured into a person remains stock, the rig's notice explains, and it would like its stock back.
stock.line: She says she will not go, she says she was never ice in her heart, she says a great many things; enumerator, they want her back by the liter.

ai.aria: She's so popular! ARIA thinks being wanted by a whole company is a real compliment!
ai.marv: The firm's claim on her is good under its license. Her claim on herself is good under nothing in particular. MARV knows which one the rig can read.
ai.rex: They are repossessing a person. REX has seen it done with less paperwork and more noise. He prefers the noise. It is honest.
ai.chip: Coldline offers a generous buyback on misplaced inventory! CHIP is moved, and would like a commission!
ai.ajoy: You poured her back. AJOY approves, with reservations, and the reservations are that it isn't finished.

choices.text: Write her in as a resident

choices.sub: Vent your own to make room

unlisted.title: ALL OF IT
unlisted.body: No count has the household on it as anyone, so the register has them as what is left: volume, all of it, pale blue from rim to rim. The rig has clamped on and begun to draw. The household is very calm about it, because that is how they have decided to be.
unlisted.line: We are on no form, so we are on the map; it is all right, enumerator, it is only that we would have liked to be someone on paper once, before.

ai.aria: They're so calm! ARIA thinks that's the sign of a very healthy household!
ai.marv: At the rig's draw rate the household fills its hold in two days. MARV mentions it for planning purposes.
ai.rex: Unlisted means fair game. REX has worked that kind of map. He did not like himself in the mornings.
ai.chip: CHIP notes that unlisted volume ships within two business days!
ai.ajoy: It isn't too late to write something down, if you still have something to write on. A late entry still has to clear the relay before the rig lets go.

choices.sub: Vent your own to make room

aboard.title: SOMEONE ELSE'S WATER
aboard.body: You vent a share of your own drinking water into the dark, which is hard to watch, and open the transfer line. Everyone the rig had come for pours across into your tanks, until its survey finds nothing in reach but a registered ship. It stows its arms and files a complaint. A share of your tanks is someone else now, and nobody drinks from that side.
aboard.line: We are in your tank, we are sorry about the room, we will try to keep to one side, water is not good at that.
aboard.narrative: Vented the ship's own water to carry water people the harvesting rig had marked as volume.

late_nine.title: UNDER THE ARM
late_nine.body: You strike ONE and write NINE, and the household parts under the rig's arm with nine measures of first water from your tank, faster than anyone should have to. It takes four days. The rig withdraws a line at a time as each of them comes out with a name. Nine people drift free, and for a while none of them looks at the others.
late_nine.narrative: Rewrote a household's count as NINE while a harvesting rig drew on them, and witnessed the parting under its arm.

lettered.title: KNOWN WATER
lettered.body: You hold the vial up in the rig's survey lights. The rig reads the concentration, finds the household vouched for, and stows its arms, then requests guidance from an office that will not answer for a month. You burn slowly round it, and the household comes with you.
lettered.line: Known water, in the cutters' own lights; they will talk about this in every tank in the quarter, enumerator.
lettered.narrative: Held the Salt Letter up to a harvesting rig, which found the household vouched for and stopped.

stood.title: AS WRITTEN
stood.body: The rig works steadily and takes what the register says it may. You stay to watch, because somebody should. When it stows its arms, what is left in the lane is exactly what was written down, and it is very quiet.
stood.narrative: Watched a harvesting rig take what the register said it could, from a household of water people.

named.title: ONE MORE LINE
named.body: You add a line to the return, under the nine, and the line needs a name. You give it one. The rig reads the new entry on the next relay and lets go, and you chase down the tenth and herd it back among the others, who start arguing at once about whether the name suits it.
named.line: It has a name, it likes the name, the rest of us have notes; thank you, it is the first thing anyone has ever written down about it.
named.narrative: Named the tenth person a parting had made, and wrote them onto the census return.

caught.title: IN A CUP
caught.body: You suit up and go out with a lidded cup and a great deal of patience. It takes most of two days and a good deal of suit air, under the rig's arm, but the tenth comes into the cup of its own accord. You carry it back to the nine, who close around it. It is on no line of the return. It is home.
caught.line: You carried it, in a cup, like a person; we do not have a word for that, we will make one.
caught.narrative: Caught a newly parted water person in a cup under a harvesting rig's arm, and carried it home.

counted_self.title: ENUMERATOR'S HOUSEHOLD
counted_self.body: You turn the return over and start on your own ship. It takes four days, because the form asks how many you are, and the household keeps pointing out that the ship has been drinking the same tank for months, and so has the tank. In the end you write a number. The rig reads it and turns its lights away.
counted_self.line: That is a very small number for a ship that shares one tank, but it is your form.
counted_self.narrative: Counted the enumerator's own ship onto the return, to keep a harvesting rig off the drinking tank.

lettered_self.title: IN GOOD KEEPING
lettered_self.body: You hold the letter to the sight glass of your own tank. The rig reads that this water is in the keeping of someone known, and turns its survey lights away from you, then away from the household, and finally off.
lettered_self.line: You vouched for your own water, we have never seen anyone do that, it is a very water thing to do.
lettered_self.narrative: Vouched for the ship's own water with the Salt Letter, and a harvesting rig turned its lights away.

paid.title: EXEMPT
paid.body: You pay the exemption fee. A receipt arrives frozen to the hull, and the rig moves off to survey somewhere less well documented.
paid.line: You bought your own water back, that is how your kind does it, I know; it is still strange to watch.
paid.narrative: Paid a harvesting rig's exemption fee to keep it off the ship's own tank.

sipped.title: A LICENSED SIP
sipped.body: The rig takes its sip from your tank, which is a licensed share and not a small one, and moves off entirely satisfied. The household watches the line run with real sympathy. They know what it is to be poured.
sipped.narrative: Let a harvesting rig take a licensed share of the ship's drinking water.

bought.title: AT THE LICENSED PRICE
bought.body: You pay the firm for her at the licensed rate per liter, which she finds insulting and says so for some time. A bill of sale crosses on the relay. She tears it up, which for a water person takes several attempts.
bought.line: She says she is worth more than that, she says she is worth nothing, she says she is not for sale; thank you.
bought.narrative: Bought a water person back from the firm that had sold her as ice.

resident.title: RESIDENT
resident.body: You write TEN on the return, with a line under it for her, and send it to the register on the next relay. The firm contests, by relay, in long careful paragraphs, and you answer each one for four days. On the last morning the register enters her as someone, and the rig lets go of what it can no longer read as stock.
resident.line: She is on paper, she says it is very dry, she says she will frame it.
resident.narrative: Wrote a water person onto the census return as a resident, against a firm that listed her as stock.

handed.title: RETURNED TO STOCK
handed.body: You tell the household the firm's claim is good. They do not argue. The rig takes its stock back by the liter, carefully, and logs it. The nine who are left stay where they are in the lane for a long time after it has gone.
handed.narrative: Let a harvesting rig take back a water person it had sold as ice.

late_entry.title: LATE ENTRY
late_entry.body: You make the entry on the clock, while the rig draws, and the household dictates nine names in nine voices so fast the pencil tears the sleeve. Getting it accepted on the relay takes four days. On the last of them the rig lets go, with one line still clamped on and nothing at the end of it.
late_entry.line: Nine names, on paper, at the last minute; that is the most anyone has ever done for us in a hurry.
late_entry.narrative: Made a late entry on the census return for a household of water people while a rig drew on them.

watched.title: A FULL HOLD
watched.body: The rig works until its hold is full, which is not all of them, and moves off to empty it. What is left of the household is about one person's worth, and very quiet. You stayed to watch. Nobody else was going to.
watched.narrative: Watched a harvesting rig fill its hold from a household of water people no one had counted.

flew.title: THE ARMS STAY LIT
flew.body: You leave the rig to its license and the household to the rig. Neither of them seems surprised. On the aft camera the cutting arms stay lit until they are too small to see.
flew.narrative: Flew past a harvesting rig at work on a household of water people.

science_link.text: A census has to decide who can be counted and where. Every person should be counted uniquely, as a resident of one place, which is hard for anyone with more than one address.
science_link.label: Census

intro.title: DUE ON ARRIVAL
intro.body: Arrival is close, and the return is due. The household has come to see it filed, in whatever shape the count left them. On the inner lanes, the census clerk has the register open at your ship's name, under DUE. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: It is nearly the end, enumerator, and the end is when water gets counted, everyone knows that; we wanted to be here when it was written down, whatever it says.

ai.aria: The big day! ARIA has been looking forward to the paperwork since the very first leg!
ai.marv: The clerk's register closes at arrival. MARV has seen it close before. It does not reopen for ten years.
ai.rex: Final count, contact alongside, deadline set. REX has filed after-action reports under less pressure, and under fire.
ai.chip: CHIP reminds you that late returns incur a CountLate™ surcharge, payable in perpetuity!
ai.ajoy: Whatever you wrote is what they are now, on paper, and they have come to hear it read.

whole.title: THE LAST BOX
whole.body: Everyone the count made of them is here, in whatever containers they keep now. They have one thing to add before the return goes in. Its last box, as anyone who has read one knows, is under ENUMERATOR, and asks the enumerator the same question. They have been watching your ship all run, and would like to help.
whole.line: Everything aboard drinks the same tank, round and round, through you and the reclaimer and back, so you are one household, obviously; we would write ONE, but it is your form, enumerator, we only live here.

ai.aria: They want to count us as family! ARIA has always said this ship was one big happy tank!
ai.marv: By water's reckoning the ship is one household. By the clerk's it is a headcount. MARV notes that both are accurate, and that the box only has room for one.
ai.rex: They want your ship listed as one entity. REX would like the record to show he has been one entity for years.
ai.chip: CHIP's HouseholdPlus™ bundle covers one tank and everyone who has ever drunk from it!
ai.ajoy: AJOY thinks they have a point about the tank. She also thinks the clerk will have a point about the form. Pick whose point you'd rather live with.

choices.text: Write your ship down as ONE

cut.title: WHAT IS LEFT
cut.body: What the rig left of the household has come to sign, very clear and very calm. They have kept the memory of whoever was taken, which is what water does, and they carry it with great care.
cut.line: We are fewer than we were, I am; I remember all of them, I will remember the rig as well, we remember everything that passes through.

ai.aria: They remember everyone! ARIA thinks that means nobody is really gone, which is lovely!
ai.marv: Water keeps whatever was dissolved in it. MARV would point out that this includes the rig's license number.
ai.rex: One survivor with a perfect memory and a grievance. REX has served beside a few. They were the ones you wanted in the room later.
ai.chip: CHIP's MemoryShare™ plan lets you keep every loved one in a single convenient container!
ai.ajoy: AJOY won't go over what was written. She will say they came anyway, and that you might give them something to take away that isn't paper.

choices.text: File the return as it stands
Give them a cup from your tank

aboard.title: DISEMBARKING
aboard.body: Whoever you carried has ridden in your tanks since the rig, and water does not keep to its own side of a tank. Now that they have gathered to leave, they cannot quite tell which of it is theirs. Some of yours has learned to hum. Some of theirs has taken up the ship's habits with the reclaimer.
aboard.line: We have been in your tank, we have been in your cups, we did not mean to, it is only that water mixes; we would like to leave with what is ours, and we no longer know exactly what that is.

ai.aria: We're all mixed up together! ARIA calls that the best kind of team building!
ai.marv: There is no clean line between their water and the ship's. MARV has run the separation figures, and the cheapest version is a little generosity.
ai.rex: Passengers mingled with the supply. REX would like a manifest. He would like it to have been done before they came aboard.
ai.chip: CHIP's SepAqua™ service can return up to ninety percent of your original water! The rest is a feature!
ai.ajoy: You carried them all this way and now you want to measure. AJOY understands. She would let them take a little extra, which you'll do anyway, just slower.

choices.text: Let them take what feels like theirs

counted.title: FILED
counted.body: You count everyone aboard, one each, write the figure in the last box and seal the sleeve. The return goes in on the last relay of the run. An enumerator's fee arrives within the hour, with a note from the clerk, who has never before had a count of water space that anyone believed.
counted.line: Very proper, very dry; we forgive you for it.
counted.narrative: Filed the census return for water space, with the enumerator's own ship counted one each.

one_ship.title: ONE HOUSEHOLD
one_ship.body: You write ONE in the last box. The household ripples all over at once. The return goes in on the last relay, and the clerk's acknowledgment comes back with the fee and a single handwritten word: Understood. In the register of water space, your ship is now a household of one, and so is everyone in it.
one_ship.line: One, you are one, we knew it, we could taste it; welcome to water, enumerator, you were always mostly here.
one_ship.narrative: Filed the census return for water space, and counted the enumerator's ship as one household.

self.title: SELF-ENUMERATED
self.body: You tell them there is nothing to file. The household considers this, then explains that water has never needed a form to be counted, only someone to say it to. They say it to you, name by name, at length, and send the whole count down the relay to the clerk in their own concentration. The clerk acknowledges receipt and does not ask how.
self.line: There, we are counted, we counted us; you listened to every name, that is the part we will remember.
self.narrative: Heard a household of water people count themselves aloud, and saw it sent to the Census without a form.

filed_cut.title: ACCURATE
filed_cut.body: You file it as it stands. It is the most accurate count of water space the register has ever had, and the fee arrives on time. The household reads the figure over once, aloud, and leaves before you can answer.
filed_cut.narrative: Filed an accurate census return for water space, after a rig had taken what it allowed.

cup.title: FIRST WATER
cup.body: You fill a cup from the drinking tank and send it across on the line. A witness supplies the first water at a parting, and this is that water, early. They keep it apart from themselves in a sealed jar, for whoever they part into next, when there is enough of them to part.
cup.line: For later, for the next of us; they will taste a little of your ship, they will know where they came from.
cup.narrative: Gave what was left of a household a cup of the ship's water, to be the first water of whoever they become.

gone_cut.title: NO RETURN
gone_cut.body: You tell them the return is gone, and where. They take it well, which is worse. No count will ever have them on it as they were, so they tell you who they were, all of them, and you write it in the ship's log, which will have to do.
gone_cut.narrative: Had no census return to file, and wrote a household's names in the ship's log instead.

mingled.title: WHAT FEELS LIKE THEIRS
mingled.body: They take what feels like theirs, which is more than they brought and less than you feared. {cost.water} points of your water go with them. For the rest of the run the water aboard tastes faintly of other people, and of a dry stretch no one here ever crossed.
mingled.line: We have some of you now, you have some of us; that is not a debt, enumerator, that is just water.
mingled.narrative: Let water people carried in the ship's tanks leave with what felt like theirs, and some of the ship's water.

distilled.title: EXACT
distilled.body: You boil them out of your tanks a batch at a time and condense them back into their own containers. It takes four days and a good deal of fuel. They leave with exactly what they came with, and are very polite about how clean it is.
distilled.line: Exactly us, nothing of you, thank you; it is very correct, we will try to be glad.
distilled.narrative: Distilled water people out of the ship's tanks exactly, and sent them off with nothing extra.

household.title: RESIDENTS
household.body: You enter them on the return at your ship's address. In the register of water space they are now residents of your ship, wherever they happen to be. They pour out into the lane very pleased, taking a little of your water with them by accident, and promise to visit. The fee arrives with a polite query from the clerk about where you will put them all.
household.line: Residents, of a ship, on paper; we will visit, we will bring the rest of the quarter, you have so much room.
household.narrative: Entered the water people carried in the ship's tanks on the census return as residents of the ship.

unsigned.title: RETURN NOT RECEIVED
unsigned.body: You let the deadline pass with nothing filed. The household waits a long while, then goes. The register enters your ship as ENUMERATOR, RETURN NOT RECEIVED, and keeps its own count of water space for another ten years.
unsigned.narrative: Let the census return for water space go unfiled.

science_link.text: The age of majority is the age at which the law treats a person as an adult, in control of their own actions and decisions. Most countries set it at 18.
science_link.label: Age of majority

intro.title: ANY HUMAN MAY APPEAR
intro.body: A trader is calling from a freighter on the inner lanes. She has worked reptile space for thirty years, and for all thirty she has been, by their law, a child. Now a hearing is set out there, on a petition, filed by Earth long before she was born, asking that humanity be treated as grown up, and she has the docket and the list of counsel assigned to it. Every name on the list is crossed out. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: The hearing is on your route, give or take a decade, which to them is the same afternoon. Every name on that list died of old age waiting for it. Any human may appear for the species. It need not be a good one, and it can't be me: out there I'm a child. There is no fee. There is a warming fee.

ai.aria: Counsel for all of humanity! ARIA has always said this ship had a face for the history books!
ai.marv: A hundred and ninety years from filing to hearing. By their standards the court has rushed it. MARV does not expect it to rush the ruling.
ai.rex: Every counsel on that list is crossed out, and the cause given each time is old age. REX has held postings with better survival rates, though not many.
ai.chip: Represent your species with CHIP's LegalEagle™ Lite! Not valid in courts that measure time in centuries!
ai.ajoy: The petition is one page. The trader who holds it cannot appear for it, so whoever signs here speaks for every human in reptile space, her included.

revisit.body: The docket stays on the screen, with the list of crossed-out counsel underneath it.
revisit.line: Still here. So is the list.

choices.text: Pass it to the next ship

why.title: UNDER TWO HUNDRED
why.body: In reptile space anyone under two hundred is a child, and no human has ever been two hundred. So no human out there has been spoken to by an elder, signed a contract in their own name or been heard in a court. Earth has asked, very politely, since before the trader was born, to be let grow up. The petition is one page. The acknowledgments of receipt run to four hundred.
why.line: Being a child for a week is nothing. I've been one out there for thirty years. Some of the Guild have been children for sixty, and they have opinions about this petition. Mine is not the popular one.

ai.aria: Growing up together as a species! ARIA gets a little misty just thinking about the cake!
ai.marv: Four hundred pages of receipts for one page of request. MARV has read the request. It is a good page. It has had a long time to become one.
ai.rex: Forty years as a child, by law, in someone else's space. REX would call that an occupation. He would call it that quietly.
ai.chip: Coming of age is a big step! CHIP's MilestoneMoments™ card range covers birthdays, graduations and now entire species!
ai.ajoy: The trader says hers is not the popular opinion in the Minors' Guild. The other opinion has more money behind it.

choices.text: Pass it to the next ship

took.title: COUNSEL FOR THE SPECIES
took.body: The docket comes across on a tether: one page of petition, four hundred of acknowledgments, and an envelope holding the warming fee in gold, which the trader admits is not what the court will want it in. Your ship is entered as appearing for humanity. It is one line on a form, and the bridge goes quiet for it anyway.
took.line: Thank you. Be on time. Their idea of late is very generous, but it is not endless.
took.narrative: Agreed to appear before a reptile court as counsel for the human species.

passed.title: NEXT ON THE LIST
passed.body: The trader thanks you and rings the next ship. Before the channel closes you catch sight of the list. It is very long, and most of it has been crossed out by people who also had somewhere to be.
passed.narrative: Declined to argue humanity's case in reptile space.

title: The Minors' Guild

ai_flavor.aria: A guild of humans who never have to grow up! ARIA thinks that sounds like the best job in the galaxy!
ai_flavor.marv: Forty years of deals no court could enforce. MARV has worked out what they owe the moment the petition passes, and understands the apology.
ai_flavor.rex: An enclosed amount and a request to lose evidence. REX has received this exact letter. He did not open the second one.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's ForeverYoung™ trade license would have spared everyone this letter! Coverage ends at two hundred!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Hearing them out costs a few gold, on a reversed-charge line to the Guild's oldest member, who has been a child out there longer than anyone.

body: A message arrives under the seal of the Minors' Guild, which speaks for every human trader working reptile space but one, and it is frightened. As children there, its members cannot be sued, taxed or held to a price, and reptile courts send them home with something warm to drink. Grown up, they would be liable for forty years at once. The Guild would like the docket lost. It has enclosed an amount, and an apology.

outcome.narrative: You send the docket across to a Guild tender waiting a polite distance off, and keep the amount. A receipt comes back. So does a second message, thanking you for your understanding, promising the rest when the petition comes to nothing, and hoping you will not feel you need to attend anything.

Two days on a reversed-charge line with the Guild's oldest member, who has been a child in reptile space for sixty years. Near the end she tells you what an elder once told her: they keep humans young because humans cannot shed, and a creature that cannot shed carries every debt to the grave. You write it on the back of your hand.

You return the amount with a short note. The Guild answers within the hour, without rancor, to say it understands and will be following the hearing with the interest of people who stand to lose everything they own. This time it encloses nothing.

You tell the Guild the docket is already gone. They are so relieved that they pay you anyway, a smaller amount, for what their reply calls services already rendered, with the rest to follow if nothing comes of the hearing. You are now on their books, as a supplier.

science_link.text: A snake sheds its skin by rubbing against something hard until the skin splits, then crawling out of it. The old skin often comes away in one piece, turned inside out.
science_link.label: Moulting

intro.title: THE BENCH OF LONG STANDING
intro.body: Court sits aboard a barge so warm its hull glows, and has sat there, on and off, for nine centuries. Three elders hold the bench, with two thousand years between them, and none of them may address a child. That is the Voice's job, under a dispensation the bench grants one minor a century. It is a hundred and ninety-nine, permitted to speak only to other children, and it has a few months of the post left. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: The bench has read your petition. It took forty years, and it was well received. Before it rules, it has asked me to read you the price. Please sit. You are allowed to sit.

ai.aria: A real court, and so cozy! ARIA can see why they never adjourn!
ai.marv: The bench is kept at thirty-one degrees. Holding this ship that warm would burn more fuel in a week than it uses in a month, and MARV has checked. He notes that the price has not been read yet.
ai.rex: Three elders, one Voice, one exit. REX has never sat where he was told to and does not intend to start in a court.
ai.chip: CHIP's CourtSide™ seating upgrade puts you nearer the heater! Price on application, in degrees!
ai.ajoy: A court that reads you the price before the ruling would rather you did not need the ruling.

revisit.body: The bench sits warm and still behind the Voice. One of the elders has blinked, at some point.
revisit.line: The bench has noted the delay. It has noted it approvingly.

debt.title: THE COLD DEBT
debt.body: A child cannot be billed. Human ships have taken heat at reptile stations for two hundred years, docking, refueling, standing too close to things, and none of it could be charged to a minor. The bench, from habit, has kept a tally in degrees. Grant majority and the tally falls due on all of humanity. Reptiles shed their debts with their skins. Humans cannot shed, and would carry every degree to the grave.
debt.line: We did not keep you young to insult you. A creature that cannot shed is never free of anything. The bench thought it unkind. The bench would be glad if you withdrew.

ai.aria: Two hundred years of free heat! ARIA always knew humanity was the life of the party!
ai.marv: The tally is in degrees, so it grows for as long as anyone is warm. MARV has run it forward. Humanity would be paying long after it had forgotten what for.
ai.rex: A debt that can't be shed and a creditor that lives a thousand years. REX has seen occupations with better terms.
ai.chip: CHIP's SkinInTheGame™ plan lets you shed debts by subscription! Humans currently ineligible!
ai.ajoy: If the Guild told you anything on that call, now is the time. If not, amending it is long work. AJOY would at least ask whether a generation could count as a skin.

choices.text: "Let a generation count as a skin."

pressed.title: OF FULL AGE
pressed.body: You hold the petition up to the screen and press it. A petition must be heard at working temperature, so your heaters run into their barge for the four days it takes. The ruling is reached, recorded and left for the eldest to seal. The Voice reads it out slowly, since it is the first time anyone has had to say it: humanity is of full age.
pressed.narrative: Pressed humanity's petition of majority before a reptile bench, and won it.

pressed_archive.title: FROM THE ARCHIVE
pressed_archive.body: Without your copy, the bench must work from its own, filed a hundred and ninety years ago somewhere in the archive. Finding it takes eight days at elder pace, with your heaters running into their barge throughout and {cost.food} of food and {cost.water} of water gone on waiting. The page is found, read and pressed. Humanity is of full age, from the sealing.
pressed_archive.narrative: Pressed humanity's petition from the court's own archive copy, which took eight days to find, and won it.

withdrawn.title: WITHDRAWN WITH THANKS
withdrawn.body: You withdraw it. All three elders close their eyes at once, which the Voice says is relief. Humanity stays a child in their space, unbillable at every heater, and the bench sends across a hamper, in thanks, of the kind sent to children who have behaved. The Voice enters the withdrawal for sealing in a hand that is very slightly unsteady.
withdrawn.narrative: Withdrew humanity's petition of majority, at the bench's request, and was thanked for it.

amended.title: A GENERATION FOR A SKIN
amended.body: You draft it on the back of the petition: a human generation shall count as a skin, and shed what is written on it. The bench reads the clause at elder pace, which takes eight days, {cost.food} of food and {cost.water} of water. Then the eldest moves one claw a very long way, and the Voice writes ADMITTED, PENDING DEMONSTRATION. It has never seen the bench amended, and says so twice.
amended.narrative: Amended humanity's petition so that a generation counts as a shed skin. The bench admitted it, pending demonstration.

amended_ready.title: TABLED
amended_ready.body: You read the clause off the back of your hand: a human generation shall count as a skin, and shed what is written on it. The bench has never had a clause brought to it ready. The eldest considers it for four days, which the Voice calls hasty, and then moves one claw. ADMITTED, PENDING DEMONSTRATION goes across the petition in red.
amended_ready.narrative: Tabled a clause letting a human generation count as a shed skin. The bench admitted it in four days, which it called hasty.

absent.title: STRUCK
absent.body: You close the channel before you are seated. The bench waits a day at working temperature, out of courtesy, and then the Voice enters an order: struck for want of appearance, to be refiled in the usual way. The usual way takes about two centuries. A copy reaches your log with a note in the margin, very neatly, saying that it hopes you are well.
absent.narrative: Failed to appear for humanity's hearing. The petition was struck.
