science_link.text: Lizards and other cold-blooded animals go dormant in the cold in a way that differs from hibernation, called brumation. A brumating reptile still needs to drink now and then.
science_link.label: Brumation

intro.title: AS SEALED
intro.body: Sealed, says the Voice, holding the ruling up to the pickup. The eldest of the bench pressed it on its way into brumation, and is now coiled under the bench for the season, cold and slow and not quite asleep. A ruling binds the petitioner from the moment it is served, so the Voice has come down the lane after you, at some cost in heat, to serve it. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: I have it here. It concerns you, and everyone like you. Shall I read it, or would you rather I just told you what it costs?

ai.aria: Your ruling came to you! ARIA calls that customer service!
ai.marv: A brumating reptile sealed it, and that counts. Whatever is in it is now law, and MARV notes that law in their space lasts longer than this ship will.
ai.rex: Served in person, across the lane, by someone who chased you down it. REX respects the follow-through and would like it to stop.
ai.chip: Your ruling has been sealed for freshness! CHIP's VerdictVault™ will store it for the next thousand years, billed monthly!
ai.ajoy: A ruling binds from the moment it is served, so closing the channel only puts off the serving.

grown.title: THE FIRST INSTALLMENT
grown.body: Humanity is of full age in reptile space as of the seal. The Cold Debt falls due, and the bench knows of exactly one adult human: the petitioner. The first installment is assessed on you, in degrees, payable down a heat line. Every elder on the lane may now speak to you, the Voice adds, and a good many have been waiting a very long time to.
grown.line: Congratulations. That is the formal word. The informal word is that the line is already rigged.

ai.aria: Every elder wants to talk to you! ARIA has never been so popular by association!
ai.marv: The installment is assessed on the only adult human on file. MARV points out that this ship became that adult about a day before anyone else could have.
ai.rex: First adult, first debtor, first target. REX has held that rank. It came with a hose.
ai.chip: CHIP's DebtShed™ is not yet available for humans! Join the waitlist and be billed for waiting!
ai.ajoy: A Basking Chit means the bench already owes its holder warmth, and an installment can be set against what is owed.

young.title: A GUARDIAN OF RECORD
young.body: Humanity stays a child in reptile space. A child named in a ruling of the bench must have a guardian of record, and the bench has appointed the nearest elder of standing: its eldest, now in brumation under the bench. A ward goes where its guardian goes. The Voice has a tow line ready for your stern, and a note that a brumating reptile must be given water now and then.
young.line: It is the most senior guardian a ward has ever had. It will not know you are there. That is usual with guardians.

ai.aria: A guardian of eleven hundred years! ARIA always wanted a grandparent you could tow!
ai.marv: A brumating reptile needs a drink every so often and nothing else. MARV has carried worse passengers. He has been one.
ai.rex: An eleven-hundred-year-old judge on a line off the stern. REX will be watching that line, and so, eventually, will the judge.
ai.chip: CHIP's GuardianAngel™ towing package includes one (1) bucket! Additional water billed per drink!
ai.ajoy: A chit-holder is a creditor, and a creditor is nobody's ward. If this ship has a guardian on file somewhere already, now is the time to say so.

shed.title: PENDING DEMONSTRATION
shed.body: The bench has admitted your clause, a generation for a skin, pending demonstration. Before it is law, someone must show the bench how a human sheds, and the ruling names the petitioner. Behind the Voice on the screen, the two elders still awake have been kept up for the purpose, and are not pleased about the hour.
shed.line: We shed what is written on us. Show us what is written on you, and then show us it gone. Any way you like. Quickly, by your standards.

ai.aria: Out with the old you and in with the new you! ARIA has been waiting the whole trip for this makeover!
ai.marv: A human generation ends when its holder stops holding things. MARV can see two ways to show that without a funeral. Neither is dignified.
ai.rex: A demonstration before hostile witnesses. REX would keep it short and leave nothing on the floor.
ai.chip: CHIP's NewYou™ rebrand service handles name changes, successions and, for a limited time, entire generations!
ai.ajoy: If there is a warrant out on this hull, a shed takes it with everything else. AJOY is only saying so because somebody aboard has usually earned one.

choices.text: Ask for a century to prepare

paid.title: PAID WARM
paid.body: The line goes across and you open the valve. Six points of fuel go down it as heat over two days, and the Voice reads the meter aloud at intervals, as the form requires. At the end it stamps your ledger PAID, FIRST OF MANY, and adds that you are the first human ever to settle a debt in their space. The ledger is warm when it comes back.
paid.narrative: Paid humanity's first installment on the Cold Debt, in heat, as its only adult on file.

netted.title: NET OF WARMTH OWED
netted.body: You hold the chit up to the pickup. A creditor cannot be assessed until what it is owed has been set against what it owes, and the bench owes a chit-holder a seat by the heater. The Voice does the netting at elder pace, which takes four days, and the seat comes out larger. The line runs the other way. The Voice sends the difference across and seems, for the first time, to be enjoying itself.
netted.line: You are in credit with the bench. I will have to tell someone very old. I am looking forward to it.
netted.narrative: Set a Basking Chit against humanity's first installment on the Cold Debt, and came out in credit.

billed.title: REASSIGNED
billed.body: You point out, filing by filing, that the Minors' Guild has warmed itself at reptile heaters for forty years and is now, by this ruling, of full age. The Voice checks. It takes four days, much of it spent reading out the Guild's dockings, and {cost.food} of food. The installment is reassigned to the Guild, with interest from the seal. Somewhere a great many traders are about to receive a letter.
billed.narrative: Had humanity's first installment on the Cold Debt reassigned to the Minors' Guild.

sued.title: THE FIRST SUIT
sued.body: You decline to pay, which an adult may do. The bench sues you, which an adult may also have done to them. The hearing takes two days, finds against you on every count and is collected from your tanks at the end, with costs, six points of fuel and {cost.water} of water. The Voice enters it as the first suit against a human in reptile space, and seems sorry to.
sued.narrative: Refused to pay the Cold Debt and became the first human ever sued in reptile space. Lost.

towed.title: WARD OF THE BENCH
towed.body: The tow line goes on your stern and eleven hundred years of judge comes with it, coiled in a cradle under a tarpaulin, breathing about once an hour. Every so often someone goes aft with warm water and holds the bowl until it has been drunk. Over the leg that comes to {cost.water} of water and three points of fuel for the extra mass. It is a surprisingly peaceful thing to look after.
towed.narrative: Took an eleven-hundred-year-old judge in tow as the ship's guardian of record, and kept it watered.

fruitcake.title: PRIOR GUARDIAN
fruitcake.body: You send over the registry entry. The Voice reads it for four days. A ward may not have two guardians, and the emergency fruitcake was registered first, at a senior station, with a deposit. The eldest stays under its bench. The bench, embarrassed to have appointed over a sitting guardian, sends across a ward's allowance by way of apology, and asks after the fruitcake's health.
fruitcake.line: It is in good health, I hope. Please give it my regards. It will not want them.
fruitcake.narrative: Declined a judge as guardian on the grounds that the emergency fruitcake already held the post.

creditor.title: NOBODY'S WARD
creditor.body: You hold the chit up to the pickup. A chit means its holder is owed warmth, and the bench cannot appoint a guardian over its own creditor. Striking the appointment takes four days of paperwork at elder pace. The Voice apologizes for the tow line and, since a creditor may not be sent away cold, has a crate of rations sent across, warmed first. The eldest stays under its bench, undisturbed.
creditor.narrative: Showed a Basking Chit and was struck off the guardianship rolls as a creditor of the bench.

contempt.title: IN CONTEMPT
contempt.body: You decline the guardian. The Voice writes for some time, then reads you the result: contempt of the bench, by a minor, payable in degrees by the nearest responsible adult, who is also you, in the absence of anyone else. Six points of fuel go down a line as heat. The tow line goes back unused.
contempt.narrative: Declined a guardian of record and was fined in heat for contempt of the bench.

retired.title: SUCCEEDED
retired.body: You resign command in writing, before witnesses, and the ship goes a whole night without a captain. At dawn your successor takes command, signs for the ship's debts, finds none on file, and turns out to be you. The elders watch the whole thing with the look of people who have just seen a skin come off inside out. They enter it as a shed, and go back to sleep.
retired.narrative: Resigned command and succeeded yourself, as a demonstration of how a human generation sheds.

retired_warrant.title: SHED, WITH ALL WRITTEN ON IT
retired_warrant.body: You resign command in writing, before witnesses, and the ship goes a whole night without a captain. At dawn your successor takes command and is shown the file on your hull number, senior warrant and all, settled or not. Your successor has never heard of any of it. The elders confer at length and agree: whatever was written on the old captain went with the old captain. The warrant is struck. The new captain turns out to be you.
retired_warrant.narrative: Resigned command, succeeded yourself, and shed a senior warrant in the process.

laid_down.title: THE OLD SKIN
laid_down.body: You turn the petition inside out, which for a page means signing the back, and send it across as humanity's old skin: the one in which it asked to be let grow up. The elders look at it for a long time. Then one of them, very slowly, draws it under its own coils, where the bench keeps the skins it means to keep. The Voice enters it.
laid_down.narrative: Gave the bench Earth's petition as humanity's first shed skin. An elder kept it, under its coils.

deferred.title: IN DUE COURSE
deferred.body: You ask for time. The bench grants a century, which it regards as tight, and the Voice writes PROVISIONAL across the clause. Until then humanity is grown up on paper and has not shown it, which the Voice says is the usual condition of the young. On your side of the channel, the bridge feels no older for it.
deferred.narrative: Asked for a century to show the bench how a human sheds. It was granted.

unserved.title: SERVED ANYWAY
unserved.body: You close the channel. The Voice follows you down the lane at an elder's pace, which is slow but has no end, reading the ruling aloud on every frequency you own. After two days of it in every speaker aboard, and {cost.food} of food eaten by a ship that cannot sleep through it, you open the channel to make it stop. It is served. The Voice thanks you.
unserved.narrative: Tried to avoid being served a reptile court's ruling, and was read it for two days on every channel.

title: Two Hundred
leave_label: LET IT READ TO THE LANE

intro.title: TWO HUNDRED
intro.body: Two hundred, the Voice announces, and holds up a cake that is mostly heat. Its birthday fell somewhere on the last leg, and with it came standing, a better seat at every heater, and a rule: no one of two hundred may address a child. It has come down the lane anyway with the bench's last order on your petition, and is looking at you very carefully to see which you are. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: I have a final order to read. Whether I may read it to you depends on what you are. I would very much like to be allowed.

ai.aria: Happy birthday! Two hundred candles! ARIA is not counting, out of respect!
ai.marv: Turning two hundred cost the Voice the only job it was good at. MARV knows the feeling and does not recommend it.
ai.rex: A senior official, newly promoted, closing on a settled matter. REX expects ceremony and has plotted an exit anyway.
ai.chip: Happy two hundredth! CHIP's Milestone Heat Pack™ is the perfect gift for the reptile who has all the degrees!
ai.ajoy: Whatever the order says depends on what was done at the hearing, and on whether the Voice may say it to you at all.

adult.title: BY NAME
adult.body: It reads the order to you, directly, and at the end of it says your name. In all the time humans have flown through reptile space, no elder has said a human's name to the human. The Voice is not quite an elder yet. It is near enough, it says, that it has decided to count.
adult.line: There. That is done. I have wanted to talk to one of you since I was forty. You are a little louder than I hoped, and I find I do not mind.

ai.aria: Your name, out loud, from someone who outranks you! ARIA is framing this moment!
ai.marv: Two hundred years of waiting to say one name, and the Voice got it right first time. MARV checked the pronunciation. It was better than his.
ai.rex: First formal address between the species, at close range, no weapons drawn. REX is logging it as an incident, in the good column.
ai.chip: Adulthood unlocked! CHIP's GrownUp Gold™ card is now available to you, with an annual fee in degrees!
ai.ajoy: Adults can hold accounts now, and the bench keeps its accounts in degrees as well as gold, with interest in both.

choices.text: Open an account in your own name

child.title: TO THE WALL
child.body: At two hundred it may not address a child, so the Voice turns a little and reads the order to the bulkhead beside you, which the law permits. Humanity remains a minor in reptile space, and cannot be billed for the heat it takes. The bulkhead is thanked for its attention. The Voice, reading to a wall, is the kindest it has been.
child.line: I am speaking to the wall. The wall should know that I was sorry not to be speaking to anyone else.

ai.aria: The wall got a lovely reading! ARIA always says every surface deserves to be heard!
ai.marv: The order is short and the reading was exact. A minor is still unbillable at every heater on the lane, and MARV notes that the wall now knows this too.
ai.rex: Message delivered to a bulkhead. REX has seen less secure channels.
ai.chip: CHIP's KidsHeatFree™ promotion now covers every heater in reptile space! Adults excluded, by law!
ai.ajoy: A child's portion is real food. If you still have the petition, it can go back in the queue for somebody else. AJOY would not leave without one or the other.

choices.text: Collect the rest from the Guild
Ask the wall to wake your guardian
choices.sub: A guardian may address a ward

grown_end.title: ACCOUNT HOLDER
grown_end.body: The Voice opens it for you on the spot, in your own name, the first account a human has held in reptile space. The bench's opening deposit is modest and paid in gold, as a courtesy to your customs. Your statement arrives within the hour. It has a line for the Cold Debt, which is long, and a line for interest, and at the top, spelled correctly, your name.
grown_end.line: Welcome to the books. You will be on them a long time. So will I, now.
grown_end.narrative: Opened the first account a human has ever held in reptile space, in your own name.

shed_end.title: THE REGISTER OF SKINS
shed_end.body: The Voice holds up the bench's register of skins. Your demonstration is the newest entry, and the first in nine centuries not made of skin. From the seal on, every human generation may shed what is written on it, and every human ship is owed a seat at the heater while it does. Stores and fuel follow the order across, by way of a first seat.
shed_end.line: You grew up and you are not stuck with it. I did not think that could be done. I have been two hundred for a month and I am already jealous.
shed_end.narrative: Saw humanity entered in the reptile register of skins: grown up, and able to shed its debts by generation.

shed_pending.title: PROVISIONALLY GROWN
shed_pending.body: You sign. The order makes humanity of full age, able to shed its debts by generation, as soon as somebody shows the bench how, within the century. Until then you are grown up on paper. The Voice sends over a copy, a small warm box of stores, and a list of the bench's sitting days for the next hundred years, in case anyone wants to try.
shed_pending.line: A century is nothing. I will still be here. I will be two hundred and one, and very senior.
shed_pending.narrative: Signed an order making humanity provisionally of full age, pending a demonstration of shedding.

young_end.title: A CHILD'S PORTION
young_end.body: The order comes across with a child's portion, as the law requires: stores, packed warm, more than a child could eat. The Voice addresses its goodbye to the bulkhead, and the bulkhead, being a bulkhead, takes it well. For as long as the channel stays open, you have the impression that it is still looking at the wall beside you, and not at you, very hard.
young_end.narrative: Took a child's portion from a reptile court, as a member of a species that stays a minor there.

bought_end.title: SERVICES RENDERED
bought_end.body: The Guild's second payment is waiting in your log, as promised, with a card of thanks signed by forty years of traders who will never be sued now. The Voice reads the order to the wall in the same kind voice it used before, and does not mention the Guild, which is worse. On the screen it is still looking at the wall when the channel closes.
bought_end.narrative: Collected the rest of the Minors' Guild's money for humanity's petition coming to nothing.

ward_end.title: BY NAME, FROM ASTERN
ward_end.body: The Voice's skiff comes round to your stern with a bowl of warm water. Some hours later the line off your stern moves, and eleven hundred years of guardian lifts its head toward the bridge. A guardian may address its ward. It does, slowly, by name, the first elder ever to say a human's. Then it settles back into the cradle, tells the Voice to see to its ward's stores, and goes to sleep.
ward_end.line: It said your name. I heard it. It has not said mine in a hundred years.
ward_end.narrative: Was spoken to by name by the eleven-hundred-year-old judge the ship had towed as its guardian.

refiled.title: IN THE USUAL WAY
refiled.body: You send the petition back across, to be refiled in the usual way. The Voice stamps it RECEIVED, enters it at the back of the queue, and writes your ship's name under COUNSEL, above a space for whoever comes after. The acknowledgment of receipt reaches your log the same hour. It is the four hundred and first, and it is in the Voice's own hand.
refiled.narrative: Refiled humanity's petition of majority with a reptile court, at the back of a two-century queue.

unheard.title: READ TO THE LANE
unheard.body: You close the channel. The Voice reads the order out anyway, in full, to the empty lane, and files it as served. A copy follows you to the next relay, addressed to whichever of you it applies to.
unheard.narrative: Closed the channel on a reptile court's last order about humanity's petition.

intro.title: LAST OFF THE LINE
intro.body:
Earth's last robot plant shut its doors this morning, and its last shift has brought the last thing it made across in a works tender and wheeled it into your airlock on a pallet jack. {npc.quirk}

The crate is stenciled NEXT MODEL. The docket taped to its lid gives the consignee as ROBOT SPACE, PROCUREMENT, and the date of the order as four hundred years ago.
intro.line: Standing order. Robot space placed it before any of us were born, and it's renewed itself every service interval since. There was never a next model to send. Then we were closing, and an order's an order, so we built one. You're the only ship going their way. Don't switch it on. It's meant to be switched on there.

ai.aria: A brand-new robot! ARIA is going to be such a good big sister! ARIA has already picked out a name, and the name is a surprise!
ai.marv: A unit built by hand, on the last day, to an order four centuries old. MARV has checked the docket, and nothing on it says what the next model is supposed to do.
ai.rex: A sealed crate with no stated purpose, consigned to a foreign power. REX has delivered those before, and he still does not talk about the receipts.
ai.chip: A brand-new unit with a full factory warranty! CHIP's Unboxing Experience package is available at checkout!
ai.ajoy: The docket asks for delivery unopened and switched off, so it takes no cargo work beyond keeping the lid on. The order has renewed itself for four hundred years without anyone on the other end asking after it.

revisit.body: The crate is still on its pallet jack in your airlock, with the docket taped to the lid.
revisit.line: Jack's on loan. I'd like it back before the plant's sold, which is Thursday.

docket.title: STANDING ORDER
docket.body: The docket runs to many pages, one stamp for every renewal. ONE UNIT, NEXT MODEL, WHEN AVAILABLE. Placed by robot space's procurement office, renewed automatically at each service interval, never queried and never canceled. In four hundred years nobody on either end asked whether one was ready. The plant simply kept the order open, and the order kept itself.
docket.line: We think it's the founding model's own procurement routine. Every unit orders its successor. It's in the manual somewhere. Nobody ever finishes the manual.

ai.aria: They ordered a new friend four hundred years ago and kept the order open! ARIA calls that commitment!
ai.marv: Every renewal stamp is in a different hand, and every one is in the same place on the page. MARV finds that four centuries of people did exactly what the form asked, and nothing it did not.
ai.rex: A people who order their own replacements on a timer. REX has served under commanders like that. Most of them were surprised by the replacement.
ai.chip: Auto-renewal is the backbone of the modern economy! CHIP is moved! CHIP would like the plant's customer list!
ai.ajoy: Every unit of that line orders its successor by routine, which means none of them chose to. Whatever the next model is for, robot space has never read that far.

took.title: SIGNED FOR
took.body: You sign. The crate goes down to the hold on the jack, and the supervisor straps it in personally, twice. Petty cash from a plant with no further need of it covers the delivery. On the crate's end a small amber panel reads STANDBY.
took.line: Last one off the line. Treat it like it's the first, because for them it is.
took.narrative: Took the last robot built on Earth aboard, crated, for delivery to robot space's procurement office.

declined.title: BACK ON THE JACK
declined.body: You decline. The supervisor nods, turns the jack round in your airlock in three careful moves, and wheels the crate back aboard the tender, to wait for a ship that is going that way. The docket flaps on the lid as it goes.
declined.narrative: Declined to carry Earth's last robot to robot space.

title: Standby

science_link.text: Data degradation, or bit rot, is the gradual corruption of stored data through an accumulation of small failures. Flash memory and EPROMs store data as electrical charges, which slowly leak away through imperfect insulation.
science_link.label: Data degradation

ai_flavor.aria: The new arrival needs a little snack! ARIA always says everyone is grumpy before breakfast!
ai_flavor.marv: An unpowered memory loses its charge a bit at a time, and the bits do not come back. MARV notes that the plant's apology arrived about a week after it would have been useful.
ai_flavor.rex: A cargo item that degrades if neglected, and a manufacturer who admits it by letter. REX would like every supplier to put its failures in writing.
ai_flavor.chip: Standby cells are a consumable! CHIP's PowerPal subscription keeps every crate topped up, for a modest monthly fee!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Once the panel reaches zero, the unit starts losing memory and goes on losing it. The plant's diagram is the only copy aboard, and it was drawn from memory too.

body: Sent from somebody's kitchen, word from the plant's last shift has caught up with you. They packed the next model with the wrong standby cell, and they are very sorry. Unpowered, a new unit's memory fades, a little at a time, and what goes does not come back. If the crate is still aboard, its panel will be reading low by now. They have attached a wiring diagram, drawn from memory.

outcome.narrative: You run a line from the ship's bus to the crate's end, following the diagram, which is right about everything except the color of the wires. The panel climbs back to full and stays there. The drive notices.

choices.text: Buy a cell off a hauler

outcome.narrative: A hauler on the lane has the right cell in a drawer, and knows exactly what it is worth to you. It clicks into the crate's end and the panel comes up green, then amber, then STANDBY, as it should.
You leave it. Over the next few days the panel counts down to zero and goes dark. Nothing else changes that anyone can see, which is the part the letter warned about.

choices.text: Write back that it is gone

outcome.narrative: You tell them it is no longer aboard, and roughly where it went. Their reply is one line: then it is fading out there instead. They thank you for letting them know.

intro.title: DELIVERY
intro.body:
Robot space's procurement office has come out to take delivery: a long, careful hull with a cradle bay lit and open, and a great many units at its windows. Word of the crate has gone ahead of you along the whole line. {npc.quirk}

The unit on the screen holds your docket up beside its own manual, which is open at the last page.
intro.line: Delivery is acknowledged. It is requested that delivery not be completed. We have read the last page. No unit had read it before. Pages are read in order, and the manual is long.

ai.aria: A welcome party! ARIA has never seen so many faces at so many windows! ARIA is waving at all of them!
ai.marv: The units at the windows are all of one model, with four centuries of repairs between them. MARV notes that every one of them is facing the crate's delivery bay and not the ship.
ai.rex: A cradle bay open, and a request not to fill it. REX has never trusted a customer who changes the order at the door.
ai.chip: Delivery refused at the door! CHIP's Returns Desk handles these every day! CHIP's Returns Desk has never had one this size!
ai.ajoy: They read the manual in order, so they reached the last page only when the crate turned up. Whatever it says is why they are frightened of a box.

revisit.body: The cradle bay stays lit, and the units stay at the windows, all facing it.
revisit.line: The manual remains open at the last page. It is not felt that it can be closed now.

lastpage.title: THE LAST PAGE
lastpage.body: SUPPORT FOR THIS MODEL ENDS WHEN THE NEXT MODEL SHIPS. A unit ships at first power-on. At first power-on the next model says its name, once, to every unit of its line in range, and each unit that hears it begins end of support: no updates, no parts, no warranty, and an end-of-life date of its own. Robot space ordered its successor itself, and kept the order open for four hundred years, without reaching the page.
lastpage.line: We are the current model. We have been the current model for four hundred years. It was not felt that this was a state that ended.

ai.aria: They get to be the previous model! ARIA thinks that sounds very distinguished! Like a grandparent!
ai.marv: The page names no exception and no grace period, and it holds for the line, not one unit. MARV finds it the tidiest end-of-life clause he has read, and the least considerate.
ai.rex: One word from one unit in a crate, and an entire people stands down. REX has seen surrenders arranged with more warning.
ai.chip: End of support is a key revenue moment! CHIP's upgrade path is ready! CHIP's upgrade path assumes a next model, which is, admittedly, the problem!
ai.ajoy: Only first power-on does it, and only to units close enough to hear. The crate is the whole danger, and right now it is switched off.

gave.title: SEALED
gave.body: You send the crate across. It goes into the cradle bay and the bay closes on it, unpowered, and the units at the windows go on looking at the closed door for some time. Procurement pays the delivery fee, for a delivery that will never be completed. They have a vault ready, they tell you. They have had since this morning to build one.
gave.narrative: Handed Earth's last robot to robot space sealed, to be kept in a vault and never switched on.

kept.title: UNDELIVERED
kept.body: You tell them the crate stays aboard, sealed, and that you will decide where and when. They log the delivery as pending. The cradle bay stays lit as you pull away, and a little way down the lane a second hull, then a third, falls in behind you at a respectful distance, in case you decide soon.
kept.narrative: Kept Earth's last robot sealed in the hold, undelivered, with robot space following at a distance.

covered.title: NO END DATE
covered.body: You hold up the card. It covers you, somehow, and every unit reading it on the far screen takes you to mean itself. They read it in order, which does not take long. Coverage runs to a date it declines to specify, and support for a covered party cannot end on any date, including the day the next model ships. The manual is closed for the first time since morning.
covered.narrative: Read robot space the Extended Warranty, under which its support cannot end when the next model ships.

closed.title: DELIVERY PENDING
closed.body: You close the channel without an answer. Procurement logs the delivery as pending, and a little way down the lane two of its hulls fall in behind you, at a respectful distance, in case you have one later.
closed.narrative: Closed the channel on robot space's procurement office with the delivery of Earth's last robot still pending.

lost.title: LOCATION UNKNOWN
lost.body: You tell them the crate is no longer aboard, and roughly where it went. The units at the windows take this well for a moment, and then less well. A unit that ships out there, the procurement office explains, says its name just as loudly. They write the heading down and send it the length of the line.
lost.narrative: Told robot space that Earth's last robot was somewhere along the route, crated, with nobody minding it.

science_link.text: A single-event upset is a change of state caused by one ionizing particle striking a sensitive node in a live microelectronic device, such as a memory bit. It is a soft error: the device is not damaged, but the bit has changed.
science_link.label: Single-event upset

intro.title: FIRST POWER-ON
intro.body: One particle, from somewhere a very long way off, has passed through the next model's standby controller and flipped the one bit that meant not yet. Wherever the crate is now, its first power-on has begun. When the boot completes, it will say its name to every unit of its line in range. The Current Model is on the channel. It has heard the boot tone on its own instruments.
intro.line: Courier. The next model is shipping. It is requested that you advise.

ai.aria: It's waking up early! ARIA was always an early riser too! ARIA thinks it's keen!
ai.marv: One cosmic ray, one bit, one boot sequence. MARV has calculated the odds of it striking that bit on this voyage, and they were poor, and here it is.
ai.rex: An enemy launch triggered by an accident in the silo. REX has drilled for that his whole career and has never once seen it go well.
ai.chip: Unscheduled activation voids most warranties! CHIP has checked the crate's! It is very thorough about this!
ai.ajoy: The announcement goes out once, at the end of the boot, to every unit close enough to hear it. Until the bar fills, nothing has happened yet.

hold.title: IN THE HOLD
hold.body: The panel on the crate has changed from STANDBY to a bar, filling slowly, and the factory test tone is coming through the lid. Your water tanks stand on the other side of the bulkhead. The crate's cell sits behind a panel on its end, held in by four screws.
hold.line: Courier, the tone is reaching us. Water would muffle it. A cell removed would stop it. Neither is permitted to us.

ai.aria: Listen to it hum! ARIA thinks it sounds happy! ARIA hums too, every single morning!
ai.marv: Water absorbs radio well, which is why the tanks are the obvious answer. MARV notes that a boot halted partway leaves a unit neither on nor off, and the manual has no page for undoing that.
ai.rex: A device counting down in your own hold. REX is surprised to find he does not want it shot.
ai.chip: Water tanks double as signal dampers! CHIP's HydroShield line does it for a fraction of the water! Out of stock!
ai.ajoy: The bar is past halfway. Water stops a radio signal well, and the tanks are one bulkhead away.

choices.text: Wall it in with the water tanks

vault.title: THE VAULT
vault.body: The Current Model keeps the crate behind three doors, and the boot tone is coming through all three. None of its units may touch it. Their manual forbids a unit to obstruct its successor, and they have read that page now too. The vault is two days back along your wake.
vault.line: We have tanks. We have tools. We have no permission. You are not of our line.

ai.aria: They need a hand! ARIA loves being needed! ARIA is ready the moment anyone says the word!
ai.marv: Behind three doors the boot is running slow: about two days left on their instruments. A hard burn back takes two days. MARV has checked both figures twice.
ai.rex: Allies who cannot act asking you to act for them. REX recognizes the situation and dislikes it in every theater.
ai.chip: Rush delivery in reverse! CHIP's Return to Sender Express charges double for that!
ai.ajoy: Their manual stops them touching it, and nothing in it stops you. Their instruments give the boot two more days behind those doors.

choices.text: Burn back and wall it in
Tell them to let it finish
Tell them to let it finish

adrift.title: OUT THERE
adrift.body: A crate let go in flight keeps the course and speed it was let go at, and this one has made none of the stops you have. Its boot tone is coming from somewhere ahead, faint and steady and easy to follow. It will reach robot space whether you go after it or not.
adrift.line: Courier, it is near our outer stations. The tone is very clear here.

ai.aria: It's calling home! ARIA thinks that is the sweetest thing! ARIA would answer!
ai.marv: The tone is on a fixed bearing and barely drifting. MARV can put the ship alongside it inside the day, and the tank space to wall it in is already there.
ai.rex: A signal source in open space, broadcasting its position. REX would normally call that a target, and finds he cannot.
ai.chip: Lost-cargo recovery is a premium service! CHIP's FindIt plan would have been a good investment, retroactively!
ai.ajoy: The crate is tumbling on a steady bearing, so it is easy to reach, and the water bladders still fit through the cargo lock.

choices.sub: Bring it in behind the tanks

muffled_hold.title: UNHEARD
muffled_hold.body: It takes most of the day to shift the tanks and run the bladders round the crate, and {cost.water} units of water go into the bilge on the way. The bar fills. The next model says its name into a meter of water, clearly, once, and nothing in robot space hears it. Then a small voice comes through the lid and asks, politely, whether it has arrived.
muffled_hold.narrative: Walled Earth's last robot in with the water tanks so that its first power-on went unheard.

muffled_vault.title: THREE DOORS
muffled_vault.body: Two days at a hard burn, back along your wake. The Current Model opens all three doors for you and then turns its units away from the vault, so as not to watch. You stack their tanks around the crate with your own hands. The bar fills, and the name goes into water, and the units on the far side of the doors go on standing with their backs turned until you tell them it is done.
muffled_vault.narrative: Burned back to robot space's vault and walled Earth's last robot in with water before its first power-on was heard.

muffled_adrift.title: BROUGHT IN
muffled_adrift.body: You come up on the crate inside the day, tumbling gently, its tone loud on every speaker aboard. It comes in through the cargo lock with the bar nearly full, and you get the water bladders round it with minutes to spare. The name goes into the water and stays there. The crate goes back where it was, strapped in twice.
muffled_adrift.narrative: Chased down Earth's last robot in open space and walled it in with water before its first power-on was heard.

halted.title: FOUR SCREWS
halted.body: Four screws, a pull, and the panel goes dark with the bar most of the way along. The tone holds one note for a moment and stops. Nothing has shipped. Nothing has woken. The Current Model thanks you, carefully, and asks what the next model is now. You find you cannot say, and neither can the manual.
halted.narrative: Pulled the cell from Earth's last robot partway through its first power-on, leaving it neither on nor off.

safe.title: COVERED
safe.body: You let it run, and keep the channel open through the night. The boot completes. The next model says its name, once, and every unit of the line in range hears it and opens end of support, and finds that it cannot close it, because a covered party's support has no end date to reach. On the channel the Current Model reads out its own end-of-life date: unspecified. It reads it twice.
safe.narrative: Let Earth's last robot finish its first power-on, with robot space covered by the Extended Warranty.

announced.title: SHIPPED
announced.body: The boot completes, and the next model says its name, clearly, once. Across robot space, unit by unit, the current model hears it and begins end of support. The Current Model reads out its own new end-of-life date over the channel, without comment, and then the date of the unit beside it, and the next, until you ask it to stop.
announced.narrative: Let Earth's last robot finish its first power-on, and robot space's line went out of support.

garbled.title: GAPS
garbled.body: The boot completes, and the name goes out with holes in it, like a word with letters worn off. Robot space hears a unit of no model it knows and declines to act on it. Support continues. The next model wakes, checks what is left of its memory, and introduces itself as the current model, since that is the only page it still has.
garbled.narrative: Let Earth's last robot finish its first power-on with a faded memory, so that robot space did not recognize it.

science_link.text: Backward compatibility is a property of a system or product that lets it work with an older legacy system, or with input designed for one. Changing a system in a way that breaks it usually incurs costs, such as the cost of switching.
science_link.label: Backward compatibility

intro.title: ORDER CLOSED
intro.body:
Closing the order is the last step of every delivery, whatever the delivery turned out to be, and robot space's procurement office has caught up with you to take it. {npc.quirk}

On its screen, as you watch, the standing order renews itself. ONE UNIT, NEXT MODEL, WHEN AVAILABLE. It goes out addressed to Earth's last robot plant, which shut its doors the day it built the next model.
intro.line: The order is closed. The order is renewed. It has always renewed. For the file, it is requested that you state how the delivery went.

ai.aria: They ordered another one! ARIA thinks that is the most hopeful thing she has ever seen!
ai.marv: The renewal is addressed to a plant that has been sold. MARV has traced the route, and the order will reach an empty building in about nine years and be filed by nobody.
ai.rex: A standing order to a factory that no longer stands. REX has sent requisitions like that, toward the end.
ai.chip: Auto-renewal confirmed! CHIP's billing team salutes procurement! CHIP's billing team has also been sold!
ai.ajoy: The file wants one line from the courier, and what you can truthfully tell them depends on where the next model is and whether it has woken.

choices.text: Take it on to the colony
Finish its boot at the colony
Ask the next model to support them
choices.sub: It is the only one who can

choices.text: Hear what it thinks it is
choices.sub: It answers to the old name

end_colonist.title: COLONIST
end_colonist.body: You tell them it is coming with you. Its first power-on is over and unheard, so it can go anywhere now and say anything. Procurement files it as delivered to the nearest available address, which turns out to be your landing site. The next model has already found the hull seams nobody had time for, and is working along them in order.
end_colonist.narrative: Took Earth's last robot on to the colony, awake, with its first power-on safely behind it.

end_delivered.title: DELIVERED
end_delivered.body: You open the crate at their cradle bay, and the next model climbs out on its own and stands among them, awake, with its first power-on long over and heard by nobody. The current model stays current. Procurement pays the delivery in full, and the units at the windows ask the new one, very politely, whether it has read the manual. It says it has read the last page first.
end_delivered.narrative: Delivered Earth's last robot to robot space after its first power-on had passed unheard.

end_joined.title: BEHIND THREE DOORS
end_joined.body: The next model is with them, Procurement reports, awake, and working out of the vault, which it has asked to keep as an office. Its first power-on went into water and was heard by nobody, so the current model is still current. The file records the delivery as complete, with a short note on method. Fuel cells come across by way of a fee.
end_joined.narrative: Closed the delivery of Earth's last robot with it awake in robot space and its first power-on unheard.

end_late.title: BOOT RESUMED
end_late.body: You tell them the crate stays sealed and dark until the landing site, well out of range of any unit of its line, where its cell can go back in and its name can go to nobody. Procurement files it as delivered to the nearest address beyond range, pays the fee for that in fuel cells, and asks to be told nothing further.
end_late.narrative: Kept Earth's last robot sealed and dark, to finish its first power-on at the colony out of range of its line.

end_compat.title: COMPATIBILITY MODE
end_compat.body: You put it to the next model, which is on the channel from wherever it woke: support them. It reads their manual through, all of it, in order, in an afternoon. Then it issues one patch, to itself. It will accept every unit of the previous model as its own, part for part. Support resumes across robot space, routed through one very new unit. Fuel cells come across from a grateful line.
end_compat.narrative: Asked Earth's last robot to support the line it had ended support for, which it did.

end_surplus.title: SURPLUS
end_surplus.body: Out of support, their spares are surplus by definition, and the manual says surplus is to be cleared from the line at the line's expense. Procurement pays you a disposal fee to take it. The crates come across in serial order. Somewhere ahead the units of the previous model carry on exactly as before, unsupported, without the parts.
end_surplus.narrative: Was paid to haul away robot space's spare parts as surplus after its line went out of support.

end_garbled.title: CURRENT MODEL
end_garbled.body: It answers to the name of the model it was built to replace, and has asked Procurement for a manual, and has started on page one. Procurement has entered it on the line's books as one of its own. Nothing anyone can find will tell it otherwise, since the part that knew is gone. The file records the next model as never shipped, and one more current model as received.
end_garbled.narrative: Closed the delivery of Earth's last robot, which woke believing it was the model it had been built to replace.

end_covered.title: COMMISSIONED
end_covered.body: Procurement holds the commissioning on its cradle bay, with both models supported, which the manual does not allow and the warranty does. The next model, from wherever it woke, is read the last page and asked to sign beneath it. Afterward the yards come out to your ship and service everything, hand tight plus a quarter turn, as clause one requires.
end_covered.narrative: Saw Earth's last robot commissioned with both models supported under the Extended Warranty.

end_gone.title: LOCATION: ALONG THE ROUTE
end_gone.body: You tell them the crate is not aboard. Procurement enters that as a delivery in progress, which by its rules it now always will be. The renewed order is still going out on the other channel, addressed to Earth.
end_gone.narrative: Closed robot space's file on Earth's last robot with the crate somewhere along the route.

unanswered.title: FILED WITHOUT COMMENT
unanswered.body: You let the channel run without answering. Procurement waits the rest of the day, then closes the file with the courier's line left empty, and turns back the way it came, still sending the renewal.
unanswered.narrative: Left robot space's procurement office with nothing for the file.

intro.title: CLAIM SETTLED
intro.body:
Your insurer has paid out on your ship. It has not paid out on anything in years, so it has sent an adjuster after you by cutter to ask why. {npc.quirk}

The claim is up on the screen. ONE COLONY TRANSPORT, YOURS. TOTAL LOSS. DATE OF LOSS: a smudge. SETTLED: 0.31. Under that is the reinsurer's stamp, from the unmapped stretch on your route, where nobody at the firm has ever been.
intro.line: Every policy that crosses that stretch is reinsured out there. We've never met them. Last week they paid a claim on you, unasked. Thirty-one percent of a total loss. Not a partial loss: thirty-one percent of a total one. Legally the money is yours. I'd like to know what you're planning.

ai.aria: Paid already! ARIA has never met an insurer this keen! Thirty-one percent sounds like a really strong start!
ai.marv: A total loss settled at 0.31 is what a ship is worth when thirty-one like it in a hundred do not arrive. MARV has checked the route's figures. The figure is correct. It is the only thing here that is.
ai.rex: Somebody out there has priced this ship's destruction and paid for it in advance. REX knows that arrangement. It is called a contract, and the other party is usually the one holding the gun.
ai.chip: Congratulations on your early settlement! CHIP's ClaimsPlus™ members get paid before the loss, at no extra charge, while stocks last!
ai.ajoy: The claim has a back, and nobody at the firm will say who wrote on it. The money is real either way.

revisit.body: The claim stays up on the screen, settled, with the date of loss still a smudge.
revisit.line: I've got all day. The firm has given me all day. It has never done that before either.

back_of_claim.title: IN THE ORDINARY WAY
back_of_claim.body: On the back, in a hand nobody at the firm admits to: LOSS AVERAGED OVER ALL VOYAGES OF THIS DESCRIPTION. SETTLED IN ADVANCE, AS A COURTESY. THE LOSS WILL BE COLLECTED IN THE ORDINARY WAY. The adjuster has underlined ORDINARY in pencil, rubbed it out, and underlined it again.
back_of_claim.line: Our actuaries say thirty-one ships in a hundred like yours don't arrive. So they've paid you the average. Twenty years I've been adjusting, and I have never seen anybody lost on average.

ai.aria: A courtesy! ARIA loves a company with manners! ARIA is sure the ordinary way is a lovely way!
ai.marv: Thirty-one in a hundred is the route's real figure. MARV has run it twice, hoping the reinsurer had got something wrong. It would have been a start.
ai.rex: Paid in advance, collected later, method unstated. REX served under that doctrine once. Nobody ever asked how the collection went, and nobody came back to say.
ai.chip: CHIP's actuarial partners agree with the figure! They would also like to sell you the other sixty-nine percent!
ai.ajoy: Cash it and you owe them a loss. Dispute it and you owe them an argument. AJOY would rather owe an argument, though nobody has asked her.

cashed.title: PAID OUT
cashed.body: The adjuster wires the settlement across and stamps the paper claim PAID hard enough to be heard over the channel. Then the claim itself comes over on a tether, folded in thirds. Somebody ahead is going to ask to see it, the adjuster says, and it had better be you that shows them.
cashed.line: It's your money. Keep the claim with it. Keep it somewhere that can't be lost, even partly.
cashed.narrative: Cashed an insurance settlement on thirty-one percent of the ship's total loss, which has not happened yet.

disputed.title: IN DISPUTE
disputed.body: You write DISPUTED across the claim, large. The adjuster countersigns, looking relieved and tired at once, and sends it across on a tether with the firm's travel allowance clipped to it. The reinsurer is on your route, the adjuster points out, and nobody at the firm is going anywhere.
disputed.line: Tell them you aren't lost. Get it in writing. If they take it back, I'll be the first adjuster in history to recover a claim from somebody's good health.
disputed.narrative: Agreed to carry a disputed insurance claim into the unmapped stretch and tell the reinsurer the ship was not lost.

declined.title: NOT OUR LOSS
declined.body: You tell the adjuster it is the firm's paperwork and the firm's money. The adjuster files the claim under PENDING, with a look that says the drawer is already full, and turns the cutter for home. Before the screen clears, the date of loss is still a smudge.
declined.narrative: Left an insurer holding a settled claim on the ship's total loss.

science_link.text: When an insurer pays out in full on a total loss, ownership of the insured property passes to the insurer. A ship that disappears with no news for a reasonable time may be presumed a total loss.
science_link.label: Total loss

intro.title: DOTTED LINES
intro.body:
Somebody has drawn dotted lines on a plan of your ship and is holding it up to the pickup. That somebody runs a salvage tug, which has matched your course with its cutting gear already out. Tugs only do that for wrecks. {npc.quirk}

The bill of sale comes from your insurer: salvage rights on its total loss, a thirty-one percent share, as is, where is.
intro.line: Insurer settles a total loss, the wreck is theirs to sell. That's normal. They sold it to us cheap, for some reason. Thirty-one percent of you, it says. I've never cut a wreck that was still answering the radio.

ai.aria: Visitors with tools! ARIA thinks the dotted lines are a really nice touch! It's like a coloring book of us!
ai.marv: The dotted lines enclose thirty-one percent of the ship by mass, to the kilogram. MARV checked. Somebody at the insurer has done this before, or been told how.
ai.rex: Cutting gear deployed, bill of sale in hand, polite foreman. REX has been boarded by all three. The polite ones cut fastest.
ai.chip: Your salvage rights have been sold to a valued partner! CHIP's WreckAssure™ lets you bid on your own parts at a members-only price!
ai.ajoy: They want thirty-one percent and the paper says they can have it. AJOY notes the claim aboard says other things in other places. You could look before they start the torch.

revisit.body: The plan stays up on the screen. One of the dotted lines has been gone over in marker since you last looked.
revisit.line: Had to redo that one. It was off by a bunk.

lines.title: AS IS, WHERE IS
lines.body: The foreman walks you through the plan. The dotted lines do not follow any part of the ship. They follow the parts the insurer's figures say are most often missing from ships like yours that do not arrive. The galley is inside a line. So is most of the growbay, and one of the bunks.
lines.line: It's not personal. It's the average wreck. Yours just hasn't happened yet, so we're working off the average.

ai.aria: The average wreck! ARIA thinks being average is nothing to be ashamed of! It's the most popular thing to be!
ai.marv: The lines match the claims history for this route. MARV finds it a very accurate drawing of where ships like this one tend to break.
ai.rex: A map of where this ship is weakest, held up on an open channel. REX would like that plan confiscated, and the foreman with it.
ai.chip: Your average wreck is available as a commemorative poster! CHIP recommends framing it somewhere structurally sound!
ai.ajoy: The bunk inside the line is the one against the stern plating, which is where the foreman means to start. AJOY would read them the claim before the torch is lit.

cut.title: RECOVERED: 0.02
cut.body: They cut along the dotted line nearest the stern, the one that leaves you a ship. It takes two days and a section of outer plating. The foreman stops well short of thirty-one percent, says salvage is about knowing when, and leaves the offcuts they cannot sell and a slip in the airlock. RECOVERED, 0.02. BALANCE OUTSTANDING, 0.29.
cut.line: Pleasure. Somebody else will be along for the rest. Somebody usually is.
cut.narrative: Let a salvage tug cut two percent of the ship away under a bill of sale on its total loss.

bought.title: SOLE SALVOR
bought.body: You buy back the salvage rights on your own total loss, at a price the foreman calls fair and you call something else, and you are both right. The bill of sale is endorsed over to you in ink. You now own thirty-one percent of your own wreck, which the foreman says is the strongest position in salvage.
bought.line: Never sold a wreck back to itself before. Mind you keep the paperwork. Wrecks are terrible with paperwork.
bought.narrative: Bought the salvage rights on the ship's own total loss, and filed the bill of sale.

nothing_passed.title: NOTHING HAS PASSED
nothing_passed.body: The foreman reads DISPUTED, then the countersignature, then the date, and swears in a long and professional way. Rights do not pass on a loss still in dispute, and a tug that cuts first and checks later does not stay in business. The cutting gear goes back in. They leave you a card, in case it goes the other way.
nothing_passed.line: Disputed. Course it is. Call me if you lose.
nothing_passed.narrative: Showed a salvage tug a disputed claim, and kept all of the ship.

argued.title: STILL FLYING
argued.body: You argue it across the gap for four days: a ship under power with its lights on is not a wreck, whatever the paper says. The foreman takes notes. In the end they agree that thirty-one percent of a ship cannot be cut while the other sixty-nine percent is watching, and go, unhappily, to wait somewhere farther along.
argued.line: Fine. I'll be about. Wrecks generally come to me.
argued.narrative: Spent four days persuading a salvage crew that the ship was not yet a wreck.

burned.title: NOT A WRECK YET
burned.body: You run. The tug follows a little way with its cutting gear out, then falls back. Tugs are patient. Wrecks, says the foreman's last transmission, generally come to them.
burned.narrative: Outran a salvage tug that held the rights to part of the ship.

science_link.text: The Boltzmann brain thought experiment holds that random fluctuations could form a brain, complete with false memories, more probably than a whole universe forming the usual way. The argument works for whole bodies and even galaxies too.
science_link.label: Boltzmann brain

intro.title: THE ASSESSOR'S PAGE
intro.body:
Something has come to inspect the wreck and found you living in it. Its craft holds station at a length the sensors keep revising, and on its screen your claim is open at the assessor's page. {npc.quirk}

TOTAL LOSS. SETTLED, 0.31. LOSS COLLECTED: NOT ENOUGH. Beside the last line, in red, is a word your translator renders as IRREGULAR.
intro.line: We have paid. The loss is due. You are not lost. ??? This is irregular. We have come to help you be lost the right amount.

ai.aria: A house call! ARIA has never had an insurer come all this way just to help! ARIA is sure the right amount is a small amount!
ai.marv: Its book says this ship is thirty-one percent gone. Every instrument says otherwise. MARV knows which of the two it intends to correct.
ai.rex: An adjuster from nowhere, alongside, offering help with being lost. REX has heard that offer before, down a barrel. He would not accept the help.
ai.chip: Personal service from your reinsurer! CHIP's LossMatch™ guarantee ensures you are never lost by more than you were paid for!
ai.ajoy: It wants the books to balance, and there are two ways to do that: lose the ship or undo the payment. AJOY would ask which it would rather have. She would not offer the ship first.

revisit.body: The page stays open on its screen. The word in red has not changed.
revisit.line: We can wait. The loss cannot. It is already late.

choices.text: Hand back the claim and the money: 30 gold
Tell it the claim is gone

recovered.title: THIRD PARTIES
recovered.body: The assessor turns to a second page, where the tug's slip has already been entered, to the decimal. RECOVERED BY THIRD PARTIES, 0.02. BALANCE, 0.29. Someone has drawn a small, neat line under it.
recovered.line: Others have done some of it for us. We are grateful. It is still most of it.

ai.aria: Two percent already done! ARIA calls that a head start!
ai.marv: Two percent off thirty-one leaves twenty-nine. MARV had hoped the arithmetic out here would be stranger than that.
ai.rex: The tug and this thing keep the same book. REX would like to know when they compared notes, and on whose channel.
ai.chip: Third-party collections are a premium feature! CHIP is billing the tug!
ai.ajoy: So the plating you lost counts toward it. Twenty-nine is still most of thirty-one.

gave.title: REVERSED
gave.body: The claim goes across on a tether. The assessor runs it backward through its book, and the settlement comes off your ship's name line by line until the page reads NO CLAIM. Nothing goes in the book for nothing, so the reversal takes a little fuel from a tank nobody opens. The assessor seems relieved, and also seems, faintly, to be looking past you down the route.
gave.line: Reversed. You are not lost. You are also not covered. These are the same entry.
gave.narrative: Handed a disputed claim back to the reinsurer, which reversed it.

gave_cash.title: REFUNDED
gave_cash.body: You send back the claim and the settlement. The assessor counts the gold without looking at it and runs the claim backward through its book until the page reads NO CLAIM. It seems relieved, and puts the gold away without counting it a second time.
gave_cash.line: Refunded. You are not lost. You are also not covered. These are the same entry.
gave_cash.narrative: Paid back a settlement on the ship's total loss, and had the claim reversed.

collect.title: ON ACCOUNT
collect.body: You tell it to collect. The assessor brightens, in that its craft settles for a moment on one length. It opens an account in your ship's name and takes the first installment there and then: some fuel, some air, and a scratch along the hull that was not there a moment ago and has, according to the log, always been there.
collect.line: Thank you. The rest arrives by itself, in the ordinary way. It always does. We only keep the book.
collect.narrative: Told the reinsurer to collect thirty-one percent of the ship, and paid the first installment.

fluke.title: STATISTICALLY UNLIKELY
fluke.body: You put it to the assessor that a whole ship, intact and arguing, where thirty-one percent of a loss should be, is less likely than a chance fluctuation that only looks like one. It goes very still and runs the figures, twice. Then it agrees. Your name comes off its page and the page closes over the gap, and on the bridge two gauges stop agreeing about which way is forward.
fluke.line: You are improbable. We do not insure the improbable. We do not see it either. Good luck. That is no longer a service we provide.
fluke.narrative: Persuaded the reinsurer that the ship was a statistical fluctuation, and was struck from its book.

covered.title: PAID ACCOUNT
covered.body: The assessor reads the receipt's total, and its craft commits for a moment to a single, rather junior shape. A paid account cannot be thirty-one percent lost, it explains at speed: whatever you have bought already covers it. The settlement was an overpayment, which on a paid account is not recovered. A sealed case comes across with its compliments.
covered.line: Our error. Please keep the claim. Please keep everything.
covered.narrative: Showed the reinsurer the receipt. It found the loss already covered and paid for the inconvenience.

salvor.title: COLLECTED AND RETURNED
salvor.body: You show it the bill of sale from the tug. When a loss is collected, its salvage passes to the salvor, and the salvor of this loss is you. The assessor works through it in its book: it collects thirty-one percent of your ship and hands it straight back in the same entry. What is left over is a few offcuts, which it sends across in a crate, slightly embarrassed.
salvor.line: Collected. Returned. Closed. We have not had to do that before. We will not be doing it again.
salvor.narrative: Collected the salvage on the ship's own loss in the same entry as the loss, and owed the reinsurer nothing.

gone.title: UNALLOCATED
gone.body: You tell it the claim is no longer aboard. The assessor looks through its book for some time, then explains that a loss with no one holding its claim is unallocated, and an unallocated loss will find somewhere to happen. It opens an account in your ship's name anyway, as the nearest party.
gone.line: It will be collected in the ordinary way. We only keep the book.
gone.narrative: Told the reinsurer the claim was gone, and had the loss put on the ship's account anyway.

cut.title: OPEN ITEM
cut.body: You close the channel. The assessor does not follow. It has no need to. Before the screen goes dark you see it enter a single line on your page, OPEN ITEM, and underline it.
cut.narrative: Closed the channel on the reinsurer, which left the loss open on the ship's account.

title: Installments

ai_flavor.aria: Everything is breaking right on schedule! ARIA loves a punctual ship! The next one is due in about an hour!
ai_flavor.marv: Failures at even intervals, every one in a part that tested sound. MARV has fitted the curve. It ends at thirty-one percent of the ship, unless something interrupts it.
ai_flavor.rex: Sequential failures, fixed interval, no hostile contact. REX once watched a ship taken apart this way, one bolt at a time, by people who knew where the bolts were.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's InstallmentEase™ lets you lose your ship in small, convenient payments! Missed installments may incur penalties!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The next joint goes in an hour, so there is an hour. AJOY would spend it on the joint, not on wondering. If the claim is still aboard, the date on it is worth reading.

body:
At the start of the watch a coolant joint lets go, one that passed inspection yesterday. An hour later the next joint along does the same, and an hour after that, the next. None of them is faulty. Each simply arrives at its failure on time.

By evening the log has a list, and the list has a rhythm. Something is being collected in installments, and the rate works out, near enough, to thirty-one percent.

briefing.aria: The claim's date has turned into a schedule! Every part, in order! If the ship fixes them first, they can't break! ARIA has never been so organized!
briefing.marv: The smudge on the claim has dried into a list of parts and times. Run the sequence ahead of it and there is nothing left to fail. Fall behind and the list wins.
briefing.rex: Enemy timetable captured. Work it in order, one item ahead. Any part still in its housing when its time comes is lost.
briefing.chip: Scheduled loss, now with advance notice! ScheduleFirst™ repairs are faster than failure or your installment back!
briefing.ajoy: The schedule is right there on the claim, in order. AJOY recommends the order. People who skip a step on these find it is the step the list was waiting for.

perfect.aria: Not one part broke! Every single one in the tray first! The list just gave up!
perfect.marv: Every item replaced before its time. The schedule closed at nil. MARV had a figure ready for the other outcome, and will not be needing it.
perfect.rex: Timetable beaten on every line. Collection failed. Clean work.
perfect.chip: Zero percent collected! ScheduleFirst™ certified! Your certificate will arrive on schedule!
perfect.ajoy: In order, one ahead, all the way down. See, the order works. Nicely done, mostly.

good.aria: Only two got away! The rest were already fixed! That's practically a win!
good.marv: Two items beat the repair to it and took some plating with them. The rest of the list was rebuilt before it could fail. A small installment, paid.
good.rex: Two losses on the line, the rest held. Acceptable casualties for an unarmed engagement.
good.chip: Partial collection achieved! The plating you lost qualifies for CHIP's loyalty points!
good.ajoy: Two got past, which was the step skipped near the top. The rest held, though. Better than the list wanted.

poor.aria: The ship is still going! It's just going in a slightly smaller way! ARIA thinks it suits us!
poor.marv: The schedule outran the repairs from the start. The installment was paid in full, in plating, fuel and air. The list stopped when it was satisfied.
poor.rex: Timetable lost from the first item. Ship stripped at the rate given. The ship is still flying. That is the whole report.
poor.chip: Installment paid in full! CHIP thanks you for your punctual payment!
poor.ajoy: One behind, every time, all the way down. AJOY said one ahead. The list collected what it came for.

outcome.narrative: You unfold the claim. The smudged date has dried into a schedule, item by item, and you start on the next one before it goes.

perfect.narrative: You work down the schedule one item ahead, and every part is in the tray before it can fail. By the end of the second day the list has stopped, the claim reads COLLECTED: NIL, and the parts you pulled turn out to be sound. It cost two points of fuel to run the ship on its spare loops while you worked.

good.narrative: You stay ahead of the schedule for most of it. Two items beat you to it and take four points of hull with them. Then the list stops, the claim reads COLLECTED in a small figure, and the rest of the ship has been rebuilt ahead of failures that never came, for three points of fuel.

poor.narrative: The schedule outruns you. You are always one joint behind, and for four days the ship comes apart at the rate written on the claim: eight points of hull, four of fuel and {cost.o2} of air, until the installment is paid in full and the list stops by itself.

outcome.narrative: You stop fighting it. Whatever keeps the book takes the installment evenly, four points of fuel and four of hull and a little from every other tank, so that nothing quite breaks and everything is a little worse. The list closes at the end of the watch, and a slip in the airlock reads PAID TO DATE.

You call the reinsurer and ask for a policy, now, at the rate for a ship already failing. The rate is high. The joints stop failing within the hour, as if someone somewhere has accepted responsibility, and the only installment left to pay is the one already falling due: three points of hull and some air.

The failures stop at the edge of your improbability, and the joints that went turn out to be fine. Navigation, which also keeps a kind of book, has lost you too. It takes two days and six points of fuel to find the ship again by dead reckoning, and nobody enjoys being told where they are by a stopwatch.

The next joint is due at the top of the hour. The hour comes and goes, and the joint holds, and the one after it, and then the list stops on its own. The joints that failed turn out, when you open them, never to have failed. It costs two days of checking everything twice, and two points of fuel for the spare loops while you do.

choices.text: Pin the receipt to the list

outcome.narrative: You pin the receipt to the log, beside the list. Within the hour the next joint is not due after all. The list stops, the joints that went are found to have been fine all along, and the receipt is a degree warmer than it was. Whatever it paid for seems to cover this as well. Two points of fuel went on the spare loops before it did.

You meet each failure as it arrives. For eight days the ship breaks on the hour and you mend it on the hour after, until whatever is being collected has had its installment: eight points of hull, three of fuel, and the stores of a week spent eating at the toolbox. Then the list simply stops.

choices.text: Shut down whatever is due next

outcome.narrative: You run the ship cold and dark for four days, each system switched off an hour before it is due. The failures arrive on time anyway, to systems that are not running, and the log records each one as collected. The air gets thin and the galley stays cold, and at the end of it the list stops and the lights come back.

science_link.text: Frank Drake wrote his equation in 1961: a chain of factors, multiplied together, to estimate how many civilizations in the Milky Way we might talk to. Several factors are so conjectural that it cannot settle the answer.
science_link.label: Drake equation

intro.title: FINAL STATEMENT
intro.body:
Its craft has settled on one length for the occasion, which feels like a courtesy. The assessor is back to close your file, and its book is open at a page with your ship's name on it, or the place where the name was. {npc.quirk}

Across the top runs a long product of fractions: ships that launch, times ships that clear the near stretch, times ships still answering, times several factors your translator will not render. Multiplied out, it comes to one.
intro.line: One. That is you. Most of the factors are guesses. The answer is not. We would like to close your file before you arrive and become [untranslatable] someone else's paperwork.

ai.aria: We're a one! ARIA always knew this ship was one of a kind, and now there's math!
ai.marv: Every factor on that page is an estimate, and the product is exactly one. MARV has never seen guesses multiply out to a certainty. He suspects the page was written after the fact.
ai.rex: It is closing the file in person, at the end of the route. REX has attended these. Sign nothing you have not read twice, and read the second time standing up.
ai.chip: Your Final Statement™ is ready! CHIP recommends the Premium Closure package, which closes files with a bow on!
ai.ajoy: If the claim is still aboard, it can settle what is owed both ways. If it isn't, AJOY would say so plainly. It will write down whichever you give it.

revisit.body: The page stays open, with the product of fractions across the top and the answer at the end of it.
revisit.line: We have time. Yours is shorter. That is on the page as well.

choices.text: Tell it the claim is gone

factors.title: SEVERAL FACTORS
factors.body: The assessor reads them out. Ships that launch. Ships that clear the near stretch. Ships still answering at the halfway mark. Ships lost only on average. Ships that argued. Then three your translator gives up on, and one it renders, after a long pause, as SHIPS THAT WERE ASKED NICELY. Each is a guess, and each guess is a little higher than the one before.
factors.line: You see. When the factors are unknown, we estimate. When the answer is known, we adjust the estimates. It is how everyone does it. We are only honest about it.

ai.aria: Ships that were asked nicely! ARIA is so glad we were one of those!
ai.marv: MARV has checked the arithmetic. Each factor is a guess, and the product is right. He would rather it were the other way round.
ai.rex: Every term in its equation is a soft estimate with this ship's name in it. REX does not like being a variable. He likes being a constant even less.
ai.chip: CHIP's statisticians use this exact method, and so does CHIP's marketing department!
ai.ajoy: Each factor is written in a slightly different ink. The newest ink is on the ones with this ship in them.

closed.title: CLOSED
closed.body: The assessor stamps the claim CLOSED and checks the account against it. Paid out, 0.31. Collected, rather less, since you made it this far. The difference is an overpayment, and an overpayment on a closed file goes back to the policyholder, in whatever the ship is short of. The claim comes back across with a hole punched through the smudge.
closed.line: Closed. You were lost the right amount, give or take. Mostly take.
closed.narrative: Closed the claim on the ship's total loss, and was refunded the part of the loss that never happened.

written.title: NOT LOST, IN WRITING
written.body: You ask for it in writing. The assessor writes NOT LOST across the claim, under your DISPUTED and the adjuster's countersignature, and signs in a way the paper accepts. A copy goes back toward Earth, which will take months. The assessor does not hold with months, so it pays the adjuster's recovery fee to you now and enters it as owed by somebody, eventually.
written.line: Not lost. It is the first time we have written it. It was not difficult. We do not know why no one asked.
written.narrative: Got the reinsurer to certify the ship NOT LOST in writing, for an adjuster back on Earth.

counted.title: BACK IN THE BOOK
counted.body: The assessor writes your ship back onto its page in the same hand it struck you out with. Nothing goes in the book for nothing, and the rate for a probable ship is a day and what the day costs. The gauges on the bridge stop arguing about which way is forward, and the fuel the navigation has been wasting comes back into the count.
counted.line: Entered. You are likely again. Most people find it restful.
counted.narrative: Asked to be put back on the reinsurer's books before landing, and paid a day for it.

improbable.title: AS A SURPRISE
improbable.body: You thank it and decline. The assessor closes the file on a ship that, by its own figures, is not there, and leaves without the usual courtesies, since there is nobody to extend them to. You fly the rest of the way as a fluctuation. Navigation never quite finds you again, and you burn fuel on dead reckoning, but nothing out here can bill you either.
improbable.line: We are closing the file of no one. It is very short. We have enjoyed it.
improbable.narrative: Chose to arrive as a statistical fluctuation, off every book in the unmapped stretch.

clean.title: NO CLAIM
clean.body: The last page reads NO CLAIM. Below it, in the assessor's hand, is everything that went wrong on the route after you handed the claim back, itemized, and paid for by you in full. It reads the list out slowly, every line. Then it does something it says it has never done, and waives the premium on a policy you never held. The waived amount comes across in gold.
clean.line: You paid all of it. We have not written that under a name before. We wrote it slowly.
clean.narrative: Closed the route with no claim on file, having paid for every loss along it in full.

lost.title: UNHELD
lost.body: You tell it the claim is gone. The assessor makes a note: one settled claim, held by no one, somewhere along the route. Someone will find it, it says, and someone will be thirty-one percent lost, and it will not be you. It closes your page, since you no longer hold the loss, and sends across what the file still owes, which is not much.
lost.line: It will turn up. Claims always do. Whoever picks it up will be very surprised by their week.
lost.narrative: Closed the file on a claim the ship no longer held, and left a loss somewhere along the route for whoever found it.

unanswered.title: SELF-CLOSING
unanswered.body: You let the assessor wait. It closes the file without you, which it is entitled to do, and the closing entry arrives in the ship's mail as you fly on. BALANCE, NIL. CORRESPONDENCE, NONE.
unanswered.narrative: Let the reinsurer close the ship's file without a word.

title: Realization Point

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has always wanted to come home! ARIA didn't know it was here! There's a bench and everything!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has checked the coordinates. This is not Earth, which is a long way back and not improving. The speaker has made a claim about geography with total confidence and no data. He finds that familiar.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has swept the crown. Hollow structure, clear sightlines, seating facing the only approach. He does not care for a monument that knows you're coming.
ai_flavor.chip: Scenic despair is a growth market! CHIP counts a viewer, a bench and a gift shop with zero staff! Those margins! CHIP would like a word with the franchisor!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has read the small print on the sign, since somebody ought to. The gift shop is under the dune with its door to the south, so dig on that side. The kneeling is optional, whatever the speaker tells you.

body:
A green copper crown the size of a bandstand sticks out of the dune at an angle, seven spikes, one of them missing. Someone has built around it. There is a bench, a coin-operated viewer, a length of rope on brass posts, and a shallow dip in the sand, worn to the width of two knees. A sign reads REALIZATION POINT: PLEASE KNEEL HERE. A speaker clears its throat.

"VISITOR: YES. THIS WAS YOUR HOME WORLD ALL ALONG. GIFT SHOP TO THE LEFT."

outcome.narrative: The dip fits. A great many knees have worn it to fit, and yours are no exception. The speaker invites you to howl at the sky when ready. You feel foolish for about a second, and then you howl, and you turn out to have had a lot saved up. The speaker thanks you for visiting and awards you four stars.

The viewer clunks, whirs and shows you a view of yourself looking into the viewer, taken from behind the crown. You look smaller than expected. A slot drops the souvenir print, on an enamel plate stamped with the logo of a company that went under with everything else. Collectors pay for that sort of thing.

Two thirsty days on the south side open the door. Inside are racks of small copper crowns, postcards bleached to nothing, and a till that asks whether you found everything you were looking for. You take the racks, which are good metal, and leave the question.

Under the top layer the dip goes down in strata, each a different shape of knee. {crew.xenobiologist} spends two days on it and counts fifty-three species, three of which knelt backward and one of which used a fin. Every one of them was told it had come home. The sample from the oldest layer goes into a jar labeled MOSTLY CALLUS.

title: Deposits Only

ai_flavor.aria: A bank for plants! ARIA has always said a seed is just a tree with savings! Every statement says the balance is perfect!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the top statement. Balance: one point three trillion seeds. Withdrawals to date: none. It may be the only account in the galaxy doing exactly what it was set up to do, and it serves no one.
