ai_flavor.marv: MARV has checked the arithmetic in the articles. It is correct. It is the first correct document the crew has produced this voyage, and its last article is about removing you.
ai_flavor.rex: Articles, an oath on an axe, a vote on the captain. REX knows this format. He has moved the fire axe to the bridge, where he can see it.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes these articles were drafted without counsel! Mutiny Review™ covers one uprising per voyage! Further uprisings are billed at the standard rate!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Paying out keeps the peace and lightens the colony fund. AJOY would read the last article before anything else.

body:
Pinned to your cabin door this morning: ARTICLES OF AGREEMENT, handwritten, signed by everyone aboard but you.

The crew has seen what is in the strongbox. Under the articles it is to be shared out: one share a hand, two for the captain, and a sum from a common fund for anyone who loses a limb in the ship's service. They swore to it on the fire axe, there being nothing more suitable aboard.

The last article provides for voting out the captain.

choices.text: Sign, and pay out the shares

outcome.narrative: You sign under the others. The shares are counted out on the galley table, yours included, and you put yours straight back in the strongbox while everyone watches. For days afterward there is gold jingling in pockets all over the ship, and a certain swagger in the corridors.

You strike out the shares and keep the one article nobody expected you to keep. A tin marked COMMON FUND goes on the galley shelf with gold in it, payable on the loss of a limb. It is the first insurance policy anyone aboard has read to the end, and it is read often.

choices.sub: Put the captaincy on the table

outcome.narrative: You call the vote then and there. The crew confers in the corridor for a long time and comes back having re-elected you, with an amendment in pencil: the strongbox stays shut until landing, and the captain does the dishes. You do the dishes for the rest of the leg.

You take the articles down and lock them in the strongbox with the gold, which belongs to the colony and always did. There is no argument. For the rest of the leg the crew is very polite to you, with the particular politeness of people who have read the last article.

science_link.text: Real pirate crews signed written articles before a voyage. Bartholomew Roberts' gave the captain two shares and each hand one, and paid any man who lost a limb from a common fund.
science_link.label: Pirate code

title: Print a Replacement

ai_flavor.aria: The fabricator can fix itself! It just needs to be working first! ARIA finds that very relatable!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes the fabricator can print every part aboard except the one it is missing. MARV would call that a design flaw if it were not also a fair summary of most designs.
ai_flavor.rex: Two donor systems, one gear. REX recommends the oven. Troops have marched on cold rations before. Troops have not marched without water.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's Genuine Parts program ships replacement gears to any address in the catalog! Your address is not in the catalog! Delivery is quoted in years!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Whatever you rob gets a new gear the moment the fabricator wakes, so the real cost is the downtime. AJOY would rob the oven.

body:
A gear the size of a thumbnail has lost its teeth deep inside the fabricator. The fault screen draws it for you, slowly turning, with a part number and a cheerful instruction: PRINT A REPLACEMENT.

Only one machine aboard can print a replacement.

The same gear, from the same catalog, turns in two other places on the ship: the water reclaimer's pump and the galley oven's fan.

outcome.narrative: Two days with the reclaimer open on the deck. Its gear goes into the fabricator, which wakes, prints the reclaimer a new one on the first try and asks if there is anything else. By then the reclaimer has been down long enough that {cost.water} units of water went out with the waste instead of back into the tanks.

The oven gives up its fan gear without a fight. The fabricator wakes and prints the oven a new one, and a spare. While it does, every meal comes out raw on one side and black on the other, and {cost.food} units of food go in the recycler. Dinner is cold, and eaten standing up.

You file a gear from scrap plate at the galley table. It takes eight days and three attempts: the first two had the right number of teeth in the wrong places. The fabricator accepts the third with a grinding noise, and its first job is a proper gear to replace yours. Yours is kept, and mounted on the wall.

choices.text: {crew.engineer} runs it on its last teeth

outcome.narrative: {crew.engineer} turns the ruined gear by hand until the few teeth left are the ones carrying the load, then coaxes one last job out of the fabricator at a crawl. It takes four days and most of {crew.engineer}'s temper. The job is a new gear. The fabricator fits it, runs its checks and comes back better than it left the factory.
You switch the fabricator off at the wall and tape over the fault screen. Everything that breaks from here on stays broken or gets fixed with tape, and the tape cannot be printed either.

science_link.text: RepRap, begun in 2005, is a real project to build cheap 3D printers that can print most of their own parts.
science_link.label: RepRap

title: Copy of a Copy

ai_flavor.aria: Every cup is a little bit different! Like snowflakes! Some of them even hold water!
ai_flavor.marv: Each print carries the last one's errors forward and adds its own. MARV has plotted the curve. It ends in a smooth stone.
ai_flavor.rex: A copied wrench, then a copy of that. REX has pulled the latest one from the toolbox before anyone trusts it with a bolt.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP reminds you that only Original Design Files™ are covered! Copies of copies void the warranty, the cup, and possibly the concept of cups!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The design files are fine. The fabricator just stopped reading them. Two days of maintenance and it reads them again, which AJOY suggested at sixty percent.

body:
Past seventy percent wear, the fabricator has stopped reading its design files. It prints each job as a copy of the last one.

A cup made today is a copy of last week's cup, which was a copy of the cup before that. Every generation comes out softer at the edges. The newest holds water, mostly, and looks like a cup someone described over the radio.

Somewhere aboard is the first cup, printed on launch day.

outcome.narrative: Two days with the feed path stripped and the cache cleared. The next cup is printed from the design, sharp-cornered and oddly hard to look at after all the soft ones. The wear counter steps back from the edge, and the fabricator reads its files again.

The first cup turns up in a bunk, full of pens. Fed to the fabricator as a master, it does nothing for the wear, which keeps climbing. But every cup from here on is a copy of a good cup, and looks like one.

choices.text: Keep copying, to see where it ends
choices.sub: A shelf of cups · more wear

outcome.narrative: You print a dozen cups in a row, each from the one before, and line them up on a shelf in order. By the ninth it is a smooth lump with a dent in the top. By the twelfth it is a pebble. The pebbles go into the scrap bin, and the wear goes on climbing.

science_link.text: Every copy of a copy loses a little quality. Engineers working on analog tape had to plan around it, because each re-recording added noise.
science_link.label: Generation loss

title: Several Hundred, Sterile

ai_flavor.aria: Tiny nurses! Hundreds of them! ARIA thinks they're adorable! ARIA has been asked to stop saying so near the patient!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the literature. The larvae eat dead tissue and nothing else, and do about as well as most other methods. He would rather they did worse. It would make the choice simpler.
ai_flavor.rex: REX does not approve of putting live organisms into anyone aboard this ship. He approves of the alternative even less. He will be watching the pouch.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's wellness partners offer the drug course at member pricing! Members are people who joined before they got sick! Enrollment is closed!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The larvae are cheap and they work, only slowly, and dinner will be quiet. Flying on is the one wrong answer here, and AJOY wants it struck off the list.

body:
Something under {patient.name}'s dressing has started to smell, and by the time the ship docks there is no pretending otherwise.

The station pharmacy is a hatch with a bell. The pharmacist looks, and sets two things on the counter. One is a course of the strong drugs, priced for people who have no choice. The other is a sealed pouch the size of a teabag that moves slightly. It holds several hundred sterile fly larvae, which eat dead flesh and leave the living alone. It is cheap.
alt_bodies:
{patient.name}'s wound is hot to the touch and getting hotter, and the ship's own medicine has stopped making any difference.

Across the station pharmacy's counter there are two cures. One is a course of strong drugs at a price that assumes you have no choice. The other is a sealed pouch about the size of a teabag, gently moving, which holds a few hundred sterile fly larvae. They eat dead flesh and nothing else. The pouch costs almost nothing.

A fever came on during the last leg, and {patient.name} has stopped saying it is nothing.

The station pharmacy is a hatch in a wall with a bell. Behind it the pharmacist sets out the strong drugs, priced accordingly, and beside them a cheap sealed pouch that is moving very slightly. Inside are sterile fly larvae, bred to eat what is dead in a wound and leave the rest.

outcome.narrative: Two days of injections, and the fever lets go all at once. {patient.name} comes back aboard mended, steady on both feet, and holding a receipt nearly as long as an arm.

The pouch goes on under a bandage. For three days {patient.name} reports a tickling that is worse than any pain, and meals are eaten with the galley door shut. On the fourth morning the pouch comes off, every larva in it five times the length it went in, and the wound underneath is clean and pink and healing.

choices.text: Pay for the drugs in water

outcome.narrative: The pharmacist will take water at the dock rate, and does: {cost.water} units, metered out through a hose in the wall while the first injection goes in. Two days later the fever is gone and {patient.name} is mended, and the tanks are lower than anyone would like.

choices.text: Clean it aboard and fly on

outcome.narrative: You thank the pharmacist, undock, and clean the wound aboard with what the ship has, which is not what the wound needs. The fever climbs for days, and {patient.name} is checked on every hour. The pouch on the pharmacy counter is not mentioned.

science_link.text: Sterile fly larvae are a real treatment. They eat the dead tissue in a wound and leave it clean, and in 2003 the US cleared them as a medical device.
science_link.label: Maggot therapy

title: One Over

ai_flavor.aria: A new friend came to the drill! Perfect attendance! ARIA has never seen a better turnout!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has carried an unexplained sixty kilos in the fuel figures for weeks. He did flag it. He was told it was the cheese.
ai_flavor.rex: An unregistered person at the muster point, in the best-fitted suit aboard. REX respects the drill discipline. He respects nothing else about this.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes the escape pods are certified for registered crew only! Extra seats are available on the Plus One plan, billed per evacuation!
ai_flavor.ajoy: They know the drill better than anyone on the roster. Locking them up wastes the one person aboard who has read the safety card. AJOY would put them in charge of it and let the crew complain.

body:
Drill day, run by the book for once: everyone to the muster point in suits, in a line, while the ship computer counts heads.

It counts one more than the roster.

Everyone looks along the line. At the far end, in the only properly fastened suit aboard, stands someone who has plainly done this before, several times, from inside a locker.

They give their name as {stowaway.name}. {stowaway.story}

"{stowaway.line}"

outcome.narrative: They are on the roster by dinner, and at the next drill the count comes out right for the first time since launch. The ship computer runs it twice more, unprompted, as if to enjoy it. Their share of the stores is worked out on the back of the drill card.

They accept before you finish, and there is a drill every morning after that. Before long every suit aboard fastens properly, and a loose hull panel on the route to the pods has been found, logged and bolted down. Sleeping past the alarm is no longer possible, because there is always an alarm.

choices.text: Log them as cargo to the next stop
choices.sub: Locked up until the next stop

outcome.narrative: You enter them on the manifest as cargo, perishable, and give them back their locker with the door on the latch. At every drill until the next stop they muster with everyone else, in the good suit, and are counted separately.

title: Across the Way

ai_flavor.aria: The patient has a hobby! Hobbies are SO good for recovery! ARIA is sure the freighter is lovely inside!
ai_flavor.marv: The freighter's last burn puts it lighter than it was three days ago, by about the mass of one long crate. MARV has the figure. He would rather not have it.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has been saying this about that freighter for three days. Nobody asked him. The patient's notes are better than his, and he has started cross-referencing.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's NeighborWatch™ service logs suspicious vessels for a small monthly fee! Your first report is billed at the introductory rate!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The patient should be sleeping, not running surveillance. A hail tells the freighter it has been watched, and AJOY suspects it has notes of its own.

body:
Laid up with nothing to do but heal, the patient has had the navigation scope swung onto the freighter that has shared your lane for three days, and has been keeping notes.

Two figures aboard it at first. Arms waving behind a lit port. A long crate pushed out of its airlock on the second night. Since then, one figure, who has turned a scope of their own on your ship and is taking notes.

The notes are in the margins of a medical leaflet. They are very thorough.

outcome.narrative: A hoarse, pleasant voice answers and asks after your patient first. Then it asks about the bag that left your airlock on the second night, and the arms waving on your bridge, and whether you have also seen two figures over there. The channel closes. Both ships change course at once. The patient underlines something twice.

Two days and a careful burn bring you alongside the crate. The freighter does nothing about it except leave, at a speed that says plenty. The crate holds no one. It holds sealed rations, packed tight, and one boot. The rations go in the stores. The boot is argued over for the rest of the leg.

choices.text: Take the scope away and make them sleep

outcome.narrative: You swing the scope back to navigation and close the port shutter. The patient sleeps through most of two days, out of spite at first and then for real, and wakes up mended and no less certain. The freighter is gone by then. The leaflet is kept.

choices.sub: Eyes on the lane · slow mend

outcome.narrative: You give the patient the scope for real, pointed ahead. They give up the freighter for the work and sit up nights calling out tumbling plates and patches of grit in time to steer around them. The hull is better for it. The healing is slower for it, and they do not seem to mind.

title: From the Stores

ai_flavor.aria: The growbay is between crops! That's all! Beans are a crop! ARIA looked it up!
ai_flavor.marv: Dried beans are seeds nobody has asked anything of yet. MARV rates their chances well. He rates the rest of the voyage exactly as he did yesterday, and will not repeat the figure.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has secured the growbay. There is nothing in it to secure. He is securing it anyway.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP is sorry for your loss! Grief support is included with the Platinum crop plan! You are on the Bronze crop plan!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The reservoir is full and doing nothing, and so are the lamps. AJOY would plant something. She knows it isn't the same.

body:
With the crop gone, the growbay still has everything a garden needs except a garden: lamps, water lines, warm soil, a reservoir full to the mark.

In the galley stores there is a sack of dried beans, two potatoes that have started sprouting on their own, and the root end of an onion that someone has kept in a cup of water for reasons they will not discuss.

None of it is the crop. All of it would grow.

choices.sub: A little food into the soil

outcome.narrative: Two days of planting: beans in the long trays, the potatoes in a bucket, the onion in a pot of its own at its owner's request. {cost.food} units of food go into the soil instead of into anyone. Within the week there are shoots. They are not the crop and nobody pretends otherwise, but the growbay has visitors again.

choices.text: Drain the reservoir into the tanks

outcome.narrative: You pump the reservoir into the drinking tanks and switch the lamps off at the breaker. The tanks come up by a margin worth having. The growbay goes dark and cold and stays that way, and the hatch is kept shut.

choices.text: Bag the soil for the colony

outcome.narrative: The crop is dead. The soil is not. Two days of sifting and bagging put every tray of it into labeled sacks, with {cost.water} units of water to keep it damp and alive, for the colony's first fields. Somebody writes STARTER on each sack in large letters.

science_link.text: A teaspoon of good farm soil holds somewhere between a hundred million and three billion bacteria.
science_link.label: Soil biology

title: A Very Slow Curve

ai_flavor.aria: The ship is going round in a lovely big circle! Circles are a very efficient shape! ARIA is almost sure!
ai_flavor.marv: Hot metal under steady load creeps, and the mounts have had both for weeks. MARV logged the first millimeter. The autopilot logged the corrections. Neither of them was asked.
ai_flavor.rex: A ship drifting off its line without orders. REX has seen that before, on vessels being steered by someone else. He has checked, and it is only physics. He is watching it anyway.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's StraightLine autopilot corrects drift silently, as you've seen! The fuel it burns is billed separately, as you're about to see!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The sag won't come back on its own, and the autopilot will go on paying for it in fuel without a word. AJOY mentioned the drive was running hot two legs ago.

body:
At PLAID, the drive mounts have sat in the heat, and hot metal under steady load does not stay where it was put. It sags, slowly and for good.

The drive now sits a few millimeters low. Its thrust no longer runs through the ship's center, and for two days the ship has been flying a long, gentle curve that the autopilot has been correcting with fuel.

The correction log runs to several pages. The autopilot did not think to mention it.

choices.sub: Fly the curve out · burns fuel

outcome.narrative: You fly the curve out by hand, a touch of thrust against it every hour, day and night. It works, and it burns fuel at a steady trickle. The pilot's chair is never empty, and nobody aboard gets a full night.

choices.text: Drop to RIDICULOUS and let it cool

outcome.narrative: At RIDICULOUS the drive runs cool, and the curve flattens enough for the autopilot to hold it on almost nothing. The sag stays where it is. Two days pass while it settles, and the slower pace takes the rest out of the schedule.

{crew.engineer} shuts the drive down cold, jacks it back onto its line and shims the mounts with plate cut from an inner bulkhead. It takes four days and leaves a hole in a wall that everyone walks past quickly. A cold restart costs fuel. The drive comes back true.

choices.text: Move the heavy cargo to balance it

outcome.narrative: If the thrust will not go through the middle of the ship, the middle of the ship can move. Two days of hauling stores, spares and water bladders to one side puts the balance point on the new line, and the curve stops. A pallet splits in the move and {cost.food} units of food go with it. The corridors stay stacked to the ceiling on one side.

science_link.text: Metal kept hot and under load slowly and permanently changes shape. Engineers call it creep, and it can deform a turbine blade until the blade touches its casing.
science_link.label: Creep (deformation)
